142/// The relation(s) whose columns an expression of a `MERGE` reads.
143#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
144enum MergeSide {
145    Neither,
146    Target,
147    Source,
148    Both,
149}
150
151impl MergeSide {
152    fn and(self, other: MergeSide) -> MergeSide {
153        match (self, other) {
154            (MergeSide::Neither, side) | (side, MergeSide::Neither) => side,
155            (a, b) if a == b => a,
156            _ => MergeSide::Both,
157        }
158    }
159}

161/// For SELECT projection items; helps simplify any required disambiguation.
162enum ProjectionItem {
163    QualifiedExprs(PlSmallStr, Vec<Expr>),
164    /// The `bool` marks whether the expr here came from an explicit `AS` alias.
165    /// In that case there is only 1 item in the vec; only `SELECT *` produces
166    /// multiple expressions.
167    Exprs(Vec<Expr>, bool),
168}
169
170/// Extract the output column name from an expression (if it has one).
171fn expr_output_name(expr: &Expr) -> Option<&PlSmallStr> {
172    match expr {
173        Expr::Column(name) | Expr::Alias(_, name) => Some(name),
174        _ => None,
175    }
176}
177
178/// Disambiguate qualified wildcard columns that conflict with each other or other projections.
179fn disambiguate_projection_cols(
180    items: Vec<ProjectionItem>,
181    schema: &Schema,
182) -> PolarsResult<Vec<(Expr, bool)>> {
183    // Establish qualified wildcard names (with counts), and other expression names
184    let mut qualified_wildcard_names: PlHashMap<PlSmallStr, usize> = PlHashMap::new();
185    let mut other_names: PlHashSet<PlSmallStr> = PlHashSet::new();
186    for item in &items {
187        match item {
188            ProjectionItem::QualifiedExprs(_, exprs) => {
189                for expr in exprs {
190                    if let Some(name) = expr_output_name(expr) {
191                        *qualified_wildcard_names.entry(name.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
192                    }
193                }
194            },
195            ProjectionItem::Exprs(exprs, _) => {
196                for expr in exprs {
197                    if let Some(name) = expr_output_name(expr) {
198                        other_names.insert(name.clone());
199                    }
200                }
201            },
202        }
203    }
204
205    // Names requiring disambiguation (duplicates across wildcards, eg: `tbl1.*`,`tbl2.*`)
206    let needs_suffix: PlHashSet<PlSmallStr> = qualified_wildcard_names
207        .into_iter()
208        .filter(|(name, count)| *count > 1 || other_names.contains(name))
209        .map(|(name, _)| name)
210        .collect();
211
212    // Output, applying suffixes where needed
213    let mut result: Vec<(Expr, bool)> = Vec::new();
214    for item in items {
215        match item {
216            ProjectionItem::QualifiedExprs(tbl_name, exprs) if !needs_suffix.is_empty() => {
217                for expr in exprs {
218                    if let Some(name) = expr_output_name(&expr) {
219                        if needs_suffix.contains(name) {
220                            let suffixed = format_pl_smallstr!("{}:{}", name, tbl_name);
221                            if schema.contains(suffixed.as_str()) {
222                                // RENAME can give a column the name of another one.
223                                let expr = match strip_outer_alias(&expr) {
224                                    Expr::Column(name) if name == suffixed => Expr::Column(name),
225                                    e => e.alias(suffixed),
226                                };
227                                result.push((expr, false));
228                                continue;
229                            }
230                            if other_names.contains(name) {
231                                polars_bail!(
232                                    SQLInterface:
233                                    "column '{}' is duplicated in the SELECT (explicitly, and via the `*` wildcard)", name
234                                );
235                            }
236                        }
237                    }
238                    result.push((expr, false));
239                }
240            },
241            ProjectionItem::QualifiedExprs(_, exprs) => {
242                result.extend(exprs.into_iter().map(|e| (e, false)));
243            },
244            ProjectionItem::Exprs(exprs, is_explicit_alias) => {
245                result.extend(exprs.into_iter().map(|e| (e, is_explicit_alias)));
246            },
247        }
248    }
249    Ok(result)
250}
251
252/// Assign unique output names to SELECT-list projections that would otherwise collide.
253///
254/// SQL allows repeated and derived output names in a SELECT list; Polars frames do not.
255/// The first projection to claim a name keeps it, and a later unaliased projection that
256/// collides gets a `name:n` suffix. Two cases are deliberately left to collide: explicit
257/// `AS` aliases, which are never renamed (`SELECT 1 AS x, 2 AS x`), and an unaliased
258/// expression that verbatim repeats the one already holding the name (`SELECT a, a`),
259/// which is a duplicate selection rather than an incidental clash.
260fn disambiguate_output_names(exprs: Vec<(Expr, bool)>, schema: &Schema) -> PolarsResult<Vec<Expr>> {
261    let protected: PlHashSet<PlSmallStr> = exprs
262        .iter()
263        .filter(|(_, is_explicit_alias)| *is_explicit_alias)
264        .map(|(e, _)| Ok(e.to_field(schema)?.name))
265        .collect::<PolarsResult<_>>()?;
266
267    let mut used: PlHashSet<PlSmallStr> = PlHashSet::new();
268    let mut claimed: PlHashMap<PlSmallStr, Expr> = PlHashMap::new();
269    let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(exprs.len());
270    for (expr, is_explicit_alias) in exprs {
271        let name = expr.to_field(schema)?.name;
272        // A repeated constant gets a new name, like other constants.
273        let verbatim_repeat =
274            !is_constant(&expr) && claimed.get(&name).is_some_and(|claimant| claimant == &expr);
275        if is_explicit_alias
276            || verbatim_repeat
277            || (!used.contains(&name) && !protected.contains(&name))
278        {
279            if !is_explicit_alias {
280                claimed.entry(name.clone()).or_insert_with(|| expr.clone());
281            }
282            used.insert(name);
283            result.push(expr);
284        } else {
285            let mut n = 1usize;
286            let unique_name = loop {
287                let candidate = format_pl_smallstr!("{}:{}", name, n);
288                if !used.contains(&candidate) && !protected.contains(&candidate) {
289                    break candidate;
290                }
291                n += 1;
292            };
293            used.insert(unique_name.clone());
294            claimed.insert(unique_name.clone(), expr.clone());
295            result.push(expr.alias(unique_name));
296        }
297    }
298    Ok(result)
299}

301/// What to do with the rows whose WHERE predicate evaluates to true.
302#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
303pub(crate) enum FilterMode {
304    /// `SELECT ... WHERE`: keep exactly the rows where the predicate is true
305    /// (rows where it is false or NULL are dropped).
306    KeepTrue,
307    /// `DELETE ... WHERE`: drop exactly the rows where the predicate is true
308    /// (rows where it is false or NULL are kept).
309    RemoveTrue,
310}

312/// The SQLContext is the main entry point for executing SQL queries.

314pub struct SQLContext {
315    pub(crate) table_map: Arc<RwLock<PlHashMap<String, LazyFrame>>>,
316    pub(crate) function_registry: Arc<dyn FunctionRegistry>,
317    /// Set once a caller installs their own registry; user-defined functions cannot be
318    /// carried in the DSL, so such a context resolves its queries eagerly.
319    custom_function_registry: bool,
320    pub(crate) lp_arena: Arena<IR>,
321    pub(crate) expr_arena: Arena<AExpr>,
322
323    cte_map: PlHashMap<String, LazyFrame>,
324    table_aliases: PlHashMap<String, String>,
325    /// Relations the current `FROM` declares (once per occurrence), which are the
326    /// only ones a qualified column may name.
327    active_relations: Vec<RelationName>,
328    joined_aliases: PlHashMap<String, PlHashMap<String, String>>,
329    /// The current statement's FROM items that are not tables, read only by qualified columns.
330    pub(crate) from_item_frames: PlHashMap<String, LazyFrame>,
331    join_base: Option<JoinBase>,
332    /// The (joined table, column) pairs of the USING clauses of the joins processed so far in
333    /// the current join chain.
334    join_using_cols: Vec<(String, String)>,
335    /// The values of uncorrelated `EXISTS` subqueries that were planned while lowering,
336    /// taken when the `EXISTS` expression is parsed.
337    pub(crate) exists_values: Vec<(Query, Expr)>,
338    pub(crate) named_windows: PlHashMap<String, WindowSpec>,
339    pub(crate) group_scope: GroupScope,
340    /// The attached catalogs.
341    catalogs: CatalogRegistry,
342    /// Scans of the catalog tables the current statement reads, by full name. Looked up after
343    /// CTEs and registered tables.
344    catalog_tables: PlHashMap<String, LazyFrame>,
345    /// The catalog table names of a deferred statement, as written and in full; used to rewrite
346    /// the statement again when it is parsed from its text.
347    catalog_names: Vec<RewrittenName>,
348    /// The names the current statement wrote for its catalog tables, by position.
349    catalog_spellings: CatalogSpellings,
350    /// The local time that `CURRENT_DATE` and friends read in the current statement, set on
351    /// first use. Shared with the contexts of its subqueries.
352    statement_time: Arc<OnceLock<NaiveDateTime>>,
353    /// Whether a qualifier may only name a relation that a `FROM` declares, also before any
354    /// `FROM` is processed. Kept by the contexts of subqueries.
355    pub(crate) strict_relations: bool,
356    /// How many subqueries enclose this scope. CTEs, derived tables and set operands don't
357    /// count: they read no enclosing scope.
358    pub(crate) nesting: usize,
359}

395    /// The types of the SELECT aliases that the clause being parsed can read. They are only

397    alias_types: Schema,
398}

430impl SQLContext {
431    /// Create a new SQLContext.
432    /// ```rust
433    /// # use polars_sql::SQLContext;
434    /// # fn main() {
435    /// let ctx = SQLContext::new();
436    /// # }
437    /// ```
438    pub fn new() -> Self {
439        Self::default()
440    }
441
442    /// Get the names of all registered tables, in sorted order.
443    pub fn get_tables(&self) -> Vec<String> {
444        let mut tables = Vec::from_iter(self.table_map.read().unwrap().keys().cloned());
445        tables.sort_unstable();
446        tables
447    }
448
449    /// Register a [`LazyFrame`] as a table in the SQLContext.
450    /// ```rust
451    /// # use polars_sql::SQLContext;
452    /// # use polars_core::prelude::*;
453    /// # use polars_lazy::prelude::*;
454    /// # fn main() {
455    ///
456    /// let mut ctx = SQLContext::new();
457    /// let df = df! {
458    ///    "a" =>  [1, 2, 3],
459    /// }.unwrap().lazy();
460    ///
461    /// ctx.register("df", df);
462    /// # }
463    ///```
464    pub fn register(&self, name: &str, lf: LazyFrame) {
465        self.table_map.write().unwrap().insert(name.to_owned(), lf);
466    }
467
468    /// Unregister a [`LazyFrame`] table from the [`SQLContext`].
469    pub fn unregister(&self, name: &str) {
470        self.table_map.write().unwrap().remove(&name.to_owned());
471    }
472
473    /// Attach a catalog under `name`. A table name starting with `name` refers to a table of
474    /// this catalog; with `default`, so does a table name that starts with no attached catalog.
475    /// A table name without namespace parts gets `default_namespace`. Registered tables and
476    /// CTEs take precedence. The same name replaces the catalog with the new `default_namespace`
477    /// and options, but keeps its default status: `default = false` never removes the default.
478    /// A name that differs from an attached one only in case is an error.
479    ///
480    /// The catalog only resolves names: the scans of its tables are passed to
481    /// [`SQLContext::execute_with_catalog_tables`] (see [`SQLContext::catalog_tables`]).
482    pub fn register_catalog(
483        &mut self,
484        name: &str,
485        default_namespace: Option<Vec<String>>,
486        default: bool,
487    ) -> PolarsResult<()> {
488        self.catalogs.register(name, default_namespace, default)
489    }
490
491    /// The name of the default catalog, if one is set.
492    pub fn default_catalog(&self) -> Option<&str> {
493        self.catalogs.default_catalog()
494    }
495
496    /// Make the attached catalog `name` (exact, else ignoring case) the default.
497    pub fn set_default_catalog(&mut self, name: &str) -> PolarsResult<()> {
498        self.catalogs.set_default(name)
499    }
500
501    /// Detach a catalog (exact name, else ignoring case), returning the name it had.
502    pub fn unregister_catalog(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
503        self.catalogs.unregister(name)
504    }
505
506    /// The catalog tables that `query` reads, once each.
507    pub fn catalog_tables(&self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<Vec<CatalogTable>> {
508        let mut stmt = parse_single_statement(query)?;
509        let mut tables = Vec::new();
510        for (_, full_name) in self.rewrite_catalog_names(&mut stmt)?.0 {
511            let table = CatalogTable {
512                catalog: full_name[0].clone(),
513                identifier: full_name[1..].to_vec(),
514            };
515            if !tables.contains(&table) {
516                tables.push(table);
517            }
518        }
519        Ok(tables)
520    }
521
522    /// The catalog statement of `query`, if any, for the caller to perform:
523    /// [`SQLContext::execute`] rejects it.
524    pub fn catalog_statement(&self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
525        let stmt = parse_single_statement(query)?;
526        match &stmt {
527            Statement::Drop {
528                object_type: ObjectType::Table,
529                ..
530            } => {},
531            Statement::CreateTable(create_table) if !create_table.temporary => {
532                return self.catalog_create_table(create_table);
533            },
534            Statement::AlterTable(alter) => return self.catalog_alter_table(alter),
535            Statement::Insert(insert) => return self.catalog_insert(insert, None),
536            Statement::Truncate(truncate) => return self.catalog_truncate(truncate),
537            Statement::Delete(delete) => return self.catalog_delete(delete),
538            Statement::Update(update) => return self.catalog_update(update),
539            Statement::Merge(merge) => return self.catalog_merge(merge),
540            Statement::Query(query) => {
541                let insert = match query.body.as_ref() {
542                    SetExpr::Insert(Statement::Insert(insert)) => insert,
543                    SetExpr::Update(_) => {
544                        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "UPDATE does not support a WITH clause")
545                    },
546                    SetExpr::Delete(_) => {
547                        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support a WITH clause")
548                    },
549                    SetExpr::Merge(_) => polars_bail!(
550                        SQLInterface: "WITH before MERGE is not yet supported; put the WITH clause inside a subquery in USING"
551                    ),
552                    _ => return Ok(None),
553                };
554                return self.catalog_insert(insert, Some(query));
555            },
556            Statement::CreateSchema { .. } => {
557                let (name, if_not_exists, options) = create_schema_parts(&stmt)?;
558                let Some((name, namespace)) = self.catalog_schema_target(name)? else {
559                    return Ok(None);
560                };
561                return Ok(Some(CatalogStatement::CreateSchema {
562                    name,
563                    namespace,
564                    if_not_exists,
565                    properties: create_schema_options(options)?,
566                }));
567            },
568            Statement::Drop {
569                object_type: ObjectType::Schema,
570                ..
571            } => {
572                let (name, if_exists) = drop_schema_parts(&stmt)?;
573                return Ok(self.catalog_schema_target(name)?.map(|(name, namespace)| {
574                    CatalogStatement::DropSchema {
575                        name,
576                        namespace,
577                        if_exists,
578                    }
579                }));
580            },
581            _ => return Ok(None),
582        }
583        let (names, if_exists, purge) = drop_table_parts(&stmt)?;
584        Ok(self
585            .catalog_drop_target(names, purge)?
586            .map(|(name, table)| CatalogStatement::DropTable {
587                name,
588                table,
589                if_exists,
590                purge,
591            }))
592    }
593
594    /// The catalog table that a `CREATE TABLE` of `name` creates, resolved as in a read; `None`
595    /// for a registered table. A name that a catalog applies to but gives no namespace is an
596    /// error, so it doesn't silently create a registered table.
597    fn catalog_create_target(&self, name: &ObjectName) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogTable>> {
598        let Some(parts) = name_parts(name) else {
599            return Ok(None);
600        };
601        let named = self.catalogs.named_catalog(&parts);
602        let Some(catalog) = named.or(self.catalogs.default_catalog()) else {
603            return Ok(None);
604        };
605        if let Some(table) = self.catalogs.resolve(&parts) {
606            return Ok(Some(table));
607        }
608        let temp_hint = match named {
609            Some(_) => "",
610            None => ", or use `CREATE TEMP TABLE` for a local table",
611        };
612        polars_bail!(
613            SQLInterface: "table '{}' has no namespace: catalog '{}' has no default namespace; write '{}.<namespace>.{}'{}",
614            display_name(&parts), catalog, catalog, parts.last().unwrap(), temp_hint
615        )
616    }
617
618    /// The catalog statement of a `CREATE TABLE`, if its name resolves to a catalog table.
619    fn catalog_create_table(
620        &self,
621        create_table: &CreateTable,
622    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
623        let Some(table) = self.catalog_create_target(&create_table.name)? else {
624            return Ok(None);
625        };
626        self.validate_create_table(create_table, true)?;
627        let CreateTable {
628            name,
629            if_not_exists,
630            columns,
631            query,
632            like,
633            table_options,
634            hive_formats,
635            partition_by,
636            hive_distribution,
637            ..
638        } = create_table;
639        polars_ensure!(like.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CREATE TABLE ... LIKE` is not supported for catalog tables");
640        polars_ensure!(query.is_none() || columns.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` does not take column definitions");
641        polars_ensure!(query.is_some() || !columns.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "CREATE TABLE expected a query, column definitions, or LIKE clause");
642        let (schema, required) = create_table_columns(columns)?;
643        let query = query.as_ref().map(|q| q.to_string());
644        let location = hive_formats.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.location.as_deref());
645        let (location, properties) = create_table_options(table_options, location)?;
646        let partition_by = create_table_partitioning(partition_by.as_deref(), hive_distribution)?;
647
648        // A registered table of the written or the full name would hide the new table from reads.
649        let tbl_name = object_name_to_string(name);
650        let full_name = table.full_name();
651        if let Some(registered) = self.registered_table_key(&tbl_name)? {
652            let hint = match name.0.len() == full_name.len() {
653                true => "unregister it".to_string(),
654                false => format!(
655                    "write the full name '{}', or unregister it",
656                    display_name(&full_name)
657                ),
658            };
659            polars_bail!(
660                SQLInterface: "table '{}' would be hidden by registered table '{}'; {}",
661                tbl_name, registered, hint
662            );
663        }
664        if let Some(registered) = self.registered_table_key(&full_name.join("."))? {
665            polars_bail!(
666                SQLInterface: "table '{}' would be hidden by registered table '{}'; unregister it",
667                tbl_name, registered
668            );
669        }
670        Ok(Some(CatalogStatement::CreateTable {
671            name: tbl_name,
672            table,
673            if_not_exists: *if_not_exists,
674            schema,
675            query,
676            required,
677            location,
678            properties,
679            partition_by,
680        }))
681    }

683    /// Execute `query` with the scans of the catalog tables it reads, by full name (see
684    /// [`SQLContext::catalog_tables`]).
685    pub fn execute_with_catalog_tables(
686        &mut self,
687        query: &str,
688        tables: Vec<(Vec<String>, LazyFrame)>,
689    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
690        self.catalog_tables = tables
691            .into_iter()
692            .map(|(full_name, lf)| (full_name.join("."), lf))
693            .collect();
694        let res = self.execute(query);
695        self.catalog_tables.clear();
696        self.catalog_names.clear();
697        self.catalog_spellings.clear();
698        res
699    }

701    /// The predicate of the rows a `DELETE` of a catalog table removes (see
702    /// [`SQLContext::catalog_statement`]), planned as a `SELECT`'s `WHERE` against the scan of
703    /// that table in `tables`, by full name. Without a `WHERE`, every row.
704    pub fn catalog_delete_predicate(

707        tables: Vec<(Vec<String>, LazyFrame)>,

710            .into_iter()
711            .map(|(full_name, lf)| (full_name.join("."), lf))
712            .collect();
713        let res = self.delete_predicate(query);
714        // the predicate is DSL: the plans built for it hold the table's scan
715        self.lp_arena = Default::default();
716        self.expr_arena = Default::default();
717        self.clear_statement_state();
718        res
719    }

759    /// Plan a catalog `MERGE` of `source` (its source, as [`Self::catalog_merge_source`] gave it,

762    pub fn catalog_merge_plan(
763        &mut self,

779    fn merge_source(&mut self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<MergeSourcePlan> {
780        let stmt = self.parse_catalog_dml(query)?;
781        let Statement::Merge(merge) = &stmt else {
782            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "expected a MERGE statement, got `{}`", stmt)
783        };
784        let parts = merge_parts(merge)?;
785        let (target_schema, target) = self.merge_target(parts.target)?;
786        // the source is planned alone: the target's alias must not hide its name
787        self.table_aliases.clear();
788        let source_twj = TableWithJoins {
789            relation: parts.source.clone(),
790            joins: vec![],
791        };
792        self.set_active_relations(std::slice::from_ref(&source_twj));
793        let mut source_lf = self.execute_from_statement(&source_twj)?;
794        let source_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut source_lf)?;
795        for name in [MERGE_FILE, MERGE_POS, MERGE_SOURCE_ROW, MERGE_ACTION] {
796            polars_ensure!(
797                !target_schema.contains(name) && !source_schema.contains(name),
798                SQLInterface: "MERGE does not support a column named '{}'", name
799            );
800        }
801        let source = self.merge_source_relation(parts.source)?;
802        check_distinct_relations(&target, &source)?;
803        let scope = MergeScope {
804            target: &target,
805            source: &source,
806            target_schema: &target_schema,
807            source_schema: &source_schema,
808        };
809        let mut keys = Vec::new();
810        for (column, key) in merge_keys(parts.on, &scope)? {
811            let key = parse_sql_expr(&key, self, Some(&source_schema))?;
812            polars_ensure!(
813                is_row_wise(&key, &source_schema)?,
814                SQLInterface: "aggregate and set-returning functions are not allowed in ON of a MERGE"
815            );
816            keys.push((column, key));
817        }
818        let columns = merge_source_columns(&parts, &scope);
819        Ok(MergeSourcePlan {
820            source: source_lf.select(columns.iter().map(|c| col(c.as_str())).collect::<Vec<_>>()),
821            keys,
822        })
823    }
824
825    /// The schema and relation name of a `MERGE`'s target, resolved as a table read.
826    fn merge_target(&mut self, target: &TableFactor) -> PolarsResult<(SchemaRef, RelationName)> {
827        let twj = TableWithJoins {
828            relation: target.clone(),
829            joins: vec![],
830        };
831        self.set_active_relations(std::slice::from_ref(&twj));
832        let mut lf = self.get_table(target)?.1;
833        let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
834        let name = relation_name(target)
835            .map(|name| name.spelled(target, &self.catalog_spellings))
836            .ok_or_else(
837                || polars_err!(SQLInterface: "MERGE requires a named catalog table as its target"),
838            )?;
839        Ok((schema, name))
840    }
841
842    fn merge_plan(&mut self, query: &str, source: LazyFrame) -> PolarsResult<MergePlan> {
843        let stmt = self.parse_catalog_dml_keeping_clock(query)?;
844        let Statement::Merge(merge) = &stmt else {
845            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "expected a MERGE statement, got `{}`", stmt)
846        };
847        let parts = merge_parts(merge)?;
848        let (target_schema, target) = self.merge_target(parts.target)?;
849        let written: Vec<&PlSmallStr> = target_schema
850            .iter_names()
851            .filter(|name| ![MERGE_FILE, MERGE_POS].contains(&name.as_str()))
852            .collect();
853        // The collected source, under its name in the statement.
854        let source_relation = self.merge_source_relation(parts.source)?;
855        let target_name = match parts.target {
856            TableFactor::Table { name, .. } => object_name_to_string(name),
857            _ => String::new(),
858        };
859        let source_factor = match parts.source {
860            // its own name, unless that would also resolve the target
861            TableFactor::Table {
862                name,
863                alias: None,
864                args: None,
865                ..
866            } if !object_name_to_string(name).eq_ignore_ascii_case(&target_name) => {
867                self.cte_map.insert(object_name_to_string(name), source);
868                parts.source.clone()
869            },
870            _ => {
871                self.cte_map.insert(MERGE_SOURCE.to_string(), source);
872                TableFactor::Table {
873                    name: ObjectName::from(vec![Ident::new(MERGE_SOURCE)]),
874                    alias: Some(TableAlias {
875                        explicit: true,
876                        name: Ident::new(
877                            source_relation.parts().last().cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
878                        ),
879                        columns: vec![],
880                        at: None,
881                    }),
882                    args: None,
883                    with_hints: vec![],
884                    version: None,
885                    with_ordinality: false,
886                    partitions: vec![],
887                    json_path: None,
888                    sample: None,
889                    index_hints: vec![],
890                }
891            },
892        };
893
894        // WHEN MATCHED: the pairs of target and source rows that match ON
895        let twj = TableWithJoins {
896            relation: parts.target.clone(),
897            joins: vec![Join {
898                relation: source_factor.clone(),
899                global: false,
900                join_operator: JoinOperator::Inner(JoinConstraint::On(parts.on.clone())),
901            }],
902        };
903        let from = std::slice::from_ref(&twj);
904        self.active_relations = declared_relations(from, &self.catalog_spellings);
905        let mut joined = self.execute_from_statement(&twj)?;
906        self.set_join_base(from);
907        let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut joined)?;
908        // a value from the pair alone, as the join evaluates it
909        let _ = self.merge_expr(parts.on, &schema, "ON")?;
910        let mut values = Vec::new();
911        let mut conditions = Vec::new();
912        let mut matched = Vec::new();
913        for (k, clause) in parts.matched.iter().enumerate() {
914            let number = clause.number;
915            conditions.push(match &clause.predicate {
916                Some(predicate) => self.merge_condition(predicate, &schema, number)?,
917                None => lit(true),
918            });
919            matched.push(match &clause.action {
920                MergeActionParts::Update(assignments) => {
921                    let mut columns = Vec::with_capacity(assignments.len());
922                    for (j, (column, value)) in assignments.iter().enumerate() {
923                        polars_ensure!(
924                            written.iter().any(|c| c.as_str() == column),
925                            ColumnNotFound: "column '{}' not found; column names are case-sensitive", column
926                        );
927                        let location = format!("the SET of column '{column}' in WHEN clause {number}");
928                        let value = self.merge_expr(value, &schema, &location)?;
929                        values.push(value.clone().alias(format!("__polars_merge_set_{k}_{j}")));
930                        columns.push((column.clone(), value));
931                    }
932                    MergeClausePlan {
933                        kind: "update",
934                        number,
935                        columns,
936                    }
937                },
938                MergeActionParts::Delete => MergeClausePlan {
939                    kind: "delete",
940                    number,
941                    columns: vec![],
942                },
943                MergeActionParts::Nothing => MergeClausePlan {
944                    kind: "nothing",
945                    number,
946                    columns: vec![],
947                },
948                MergeActionParts::Insert { .. } => {
949                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "WHEN MATCHED takes UPDATE, DELETE or DO NOTHING (WHEN clause {})", number)
950                },
951            });
952        }
953        let action = first_clause(conditions).alias(MERGE_ACTION);
954        values.push(action.clone());
955        // Fails as the `SELECT` of these values would.
956        DataFrame::empty_with_schema(&schema)
957            .lazy()
958            .select(values)
959            .collect()?;
960        let pairs = joined.with_column(action);
961
962        // WHEN NOT MATCHED: the source rows, which see the source alone
963        self.joined_aliases.clear();
964        self.join_base = None;
965        self.table_aliases.clear();
966        let source_twj = TableWithJoins {
967            relation: source_factor,
968            joins: vec![],
969        };
970        let from = std::slice::from_ref(&source_twj);
971        self.active_relations = declared_relations(from, &self.catalog_spellings);
972        let mut source_lf = self.execute_from_statement(&source_twj)?;
973        self.set_join_base(from);
974        let source_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut source_lf)?;
975        let scope = MergeScope {
976            target: &target,
977            source: &source_relation,
978            target_schema: &target_schema,
979            source_schema: &source_schema,
980        };
981        let mut values = Vec::new();
982        let mut conditions = Vec::new();
983        let mut not_matched = Vec::new();
984        for (k, clause) in parts.not_matched.iter().enumerate() {
985            let number = clause.number;
986            if let Some(predicate) = &clause.predicate {
987                check_no_target_reference(predicate, &scope, number)?;
988            }
989            conditions.push(match &clause.predicate {
990                Some(predicate) => self.merge_condition(predicate, &source_schema, number)?,
991                None => lit(true),
992            });
993            not_matched.push(match &clause.action {
994                MergeActionParts::Insert {
995                    columns: listed,
996                    values: inserted,
997                } => {
998                    let targets: Vec<String> = match listed {
999                        Some(listed) => {
1000                            for column in listed {
1001                                polars_ensure!(
1002                                    written.iter().any(|c| c.as_str() == column),
1003                                    ColumnNotFound: "column '{}' not found; column names are case-sensitive", column
1004                                );
1005                            }
1006                            listed.clone()
1007                        },
1008                        None => {
1009                            polars_ensure!(
1010                                inserted.len() == written.len(),
1011                                SQLInterface: "the INSERT of WHEN clause {} gives {} values for {} target columns; without a column list it takes one value per column (list the columns to insert)",
1012                                number, inserted.len(), written.len()
1013                            );
1014                            written.iter().map(|c| c.to_string()).collect()
1015                        },
1016                    };
1017                    let mut columns = Vec::with_capacity(targets.len());
1018                    for (j, (column, value)) in targets.into_iter().zip(inserted).enumerate() {
1019                        check_no_target_reference(value, &scope, number)?;
1020                        let location = format!("the INSERT values of WHEN clause {number}");
1021                        let value = self.merge_expr(value, &source_schema, &location)?;
1022                        values.push(value.clone().alias(format!("__polars_merge_ins_{k}_{j}")));
1023                        columns.push((column, value));
1024                    }
1025                    MergeClausePlan {
1026                        kind: "insert",
1027                        number,
1028                        columns,
1029                    }
1030                },
1031                MergeActionParts::Nothing => MergeClausePlan {
1032                    kind: "nothing",
1033                    number,
1034                    columns: vec![],
1035                },
1036                _ => polars_bail!(
1037                    SQLInterface: "WHEN NOT MATCHED takes INSERT or DO NOTHING (WHEN clause {})", number
1038                ),
1039            });
1040        }
1041        let action = first_clause(conditions).alias(MERGE_ACTION);
1042        values.push(action.clone());
1043        DataFrame::empty_with_schema(&source_schema)
1044            .lazy()
1045            .select(values)
1046            .collect()?;
1047        let inserts = source_lf.with_column(action);
1048        Ok(MergePlan {
1049            pairs,
1050            inserts,
1051            matched,
1052            not_matched,
1053        })
1054    }
1055
1056    /// Plan the condition of `WHEN` clause `number` of a `MERGE`: boolean, a NULL never holding.
1057    fn merge_condition(
1058        &mut self,
1059        expr: &SQLExpr,
1060        schema: &Schema,
1061        number: usize,
1062    ) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
1063        let location = format!("the condition of WHEN clause {number}");
1064        let condition = self.merge_expr(expr, schema, &location)?;
1065        let dtype = DataFrame::empty_with_schema(schema)
1066            .lazy()
1067            .select([condition.clone().alias("c")])
1068            .collect_schema()?
1069            .get("c")
1070            .cloned()
1071            .unwrap_or(DataType::Null);
1072        match dtype {
1073            DataType::Boolean => Ok(condition),
1074            DataType::Null => Ok(condition.cast(DataType::Boolean)),
1075            dtype => polars_bail!(
1076                SQLInterface: "{} of a MERGE must be boolean, not {}", location, dtype
1077            ),
1078        }
1079    }
1080
1081    /// The name a `MERGE`'s source is known by: its alias, else its table name as written.
1082    fn merge_source_relation(&self, source: &TableFactor) -> PolarsResult<RelationName> {
1083        if let TableFactor::Table {
1084            alias: None,
1085            args: None,
1086            ..
1087        } = source
1088            && let Some(name) = relation_name(source)
1089        {
1090            return Ok(name.spelled(source, &self.catalog_spellings));
1091        }
1092        merge_source_relation(source)
1093    }
1094
1095    /// Plan an expression of a `MERGE` against `schema`: a value from its own row.
1096    fn merge_expr(
1097        &mut self,
1098        expr: &SQLExpr,
1099        schema: &Schema,
1100        location: &str,
1101    ) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
1102        if let Some(base) = &self.join_base
1103            && !self.joined_aliases.is_empty()
1104        {
1105            check_for_ambiguous_column_refs(
1106                expr,
1107                &self.joined_aliases,
1108                &base.table_name,
1109                &base.using_cols,
1110                &self.active_relations,
1111                schema,
1112            )?;
1113        }
1114        let planned = parse_sql_expr(expr, self, Some(schema))?;
1115        polars_ensure!(
1116            is_row_wise(&planned, schema)?,
1117            SQLInterface: "aggregate and set-returning functions are not allowed in {} of a MERGE", location
1118        );
1119        polars_ensure!(
1120            !planned.clone().meta().has_multiple_outputs(),
1121            SQLInterface: "{} of a MERGE must be a single expression", location
1122        );
1123        Ok(planned)
1124    }
1125
1126    fn parse_catalog_dml(&mut self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<Statement> {
1127        self.statement_time = Default::default();
1128        self.parse_catalog_dml_keeping_clock(query)
1129    }
1130
1131    /// As `parse_catalog_dml`, on the clock of the statement's earlier planning calls.
1132    fn parse_catalog_dml_keeping_clock(&mut self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<Statement> {
1133        let mut stmt = parse_single_statement(query)?;
1134        self.catalog_spellings = self.rewrite_catalog_names(&mut stmt)?.1;
1135        desugar_quantified_subqueries(&mut stmt);
1136        Ok(stmt)
1137    }
1138
1139    fn delete_predicate(&mut self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
1140        let stmt = self.parse_catalog_dml(query)?;
1141        let Statement::Delete(delete) = &stmt else {
1142            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "expected a DELETE statement, got `{}`", stmt)
1143        };
1144        let (from, selection) = delete_parts(delete)?;
1145        let mut lf = self.delete_target(from)?;
1146        self.dml_predicate(&mut lf, selection, "DELETE")
1147    }
1148
1149    fn update_plan(&mut self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<(Expr, Vec<(String, Expr)>)> {
1150        let stmt = self.parse_catalog_dml(query)?;
1151        let Statement::Update(update) = &stmt else {
1152            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "expected an UPDATE statement, got `{}`", stmt)
1153        };
1154        let (target, assignments, selection) = update_parts(update)?;
1155        polars_ensure!(
1156            matches!(target.relation, TableFactor::Table { .. }),
1157            SQLInterface: "UPDATE of `{}` is not supported", target.relation
1158        );
1159        let mut lf = self.delete_target(target)?;
1160        let predicate = self.dml_predicate(&mut lf, selection, "UPDATE")?;
1161        let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
1162        let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(assignments.len());
1163        for (column, value) in assignments {
1164            polars_ensure!(
1165                schema.contains(&column),
1166                ColumnNotFound: "column '{}' not found; column names are case-sensitive", column
1167            );
1168            let expr = parse_sql_expr(&value, self, Some(&*schema))?;
1169            polars_ensure!(
1170                is_row_wise(&expr, &schema)?,
1171                SQLInterface: "the value of column '{}' in the SET of an UPDATE must come from its own row (no aggregate or set-returning function)",
1172                column
1173            );
1174            polars_ensure!(
1175                !expr.clone().meta().has_multiple_outputs(),
1176                SQLInterface: "the value of column '{}' in the SET of an UPDATE must be a single expression",
1177                column
1178            );
1179            values.push((column, expr));
1180        }
1181        // Fails as the `SELECT` of these values would.
1182        DataFrame::empty_with_schema(&schema)
1183            .lazy()
1184            .select(
1185                values
1186                    .iter()
1187                    .map(|(c, e)| e.clone().alias(c.as_str()))
1188                    .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
1189            )
1190            .collect()?;
1191        Ok((predicate, values))
1192    }
1193
1194    /// The predicate of a catalog `DELETE` or `UPDATE`'s `WHERE`, against `lf`; every row
1195    /// without one.
1196    fn dml_predicate(
1197        &mut self,
1198        lf: &mut LazyFrame,
1199        selection: Option<&SQLExpr>,
1200        statement: &str,
1201    ) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
1202        let Some(selection) = selection else {
1203            return Ok(lit(true));
1204        };
1205        polars_ensure!(
1206            !expr_contains_subquery(selection),
1207            SQLInterface: "subqueries are not supported in the WHERE of a catalog {}", statement
1208        );
1209        let n_grouping_calls = self.group_scope.grouping_calls.len();
1210        if let Some(predicate) = self.input_independent_predicate(selection)? {
1211            self.reject_grouping_in_where(n_grouping_calls)?;
1212            // A NULL condition matches nothing.
1213            let df = DataFrame::empty()
1214                .lazy()
1215                .select([predicate.cast(DataType::Boolean)])
1216                .collect()?;
1217            let value = df.columns()[0].get(0)?;
1218            return Ok(lit(matches!(value, AnyValue::Boolean(true))));
1219        }
1220        let schema = self.get_frame_schema(lf)?;
1221        let mut predicate = parse_sql_expr(selection, self, Some(&*schema))?;
1222        self.reject_grouping_in_where(n_grouping_calls)?;
1223        if predicate.clone().meta().has_multiple_outputs() {
1224            predicate = all_horizontal([predicate])?;
1225        }
1226        // Fails as the `WHERE` of a `SELECT` would (eg: a timestamp across time zones).
1227        DataFrame::empty_with_schema(&schema)
1228            .lazy()
1229            .filter(predicate.clone())
1230            .collect()?;
1231        Ok(predicate)
1232    }
1233
1234    /// Rewrite the catalog table names of `stmt` to their full names (see
1235    /// [`rewrite_catalog_names`]): by the attached catalogs, else by the names a deferred
1236    /// statement recorded.
1237    fn rewrite_catalog_names(
1238        &self,
1239        stmt: &mut Statement,
1240    ) -> PolarsResult<(Vec<RewrittenName>, CatalogSpellings)> {
1241        if self.catalogs.is_empty() && self.catalog_names.is_empty() {
1242            return Ok(Default::default());
1243        }
1244        let table_map = self.table_map.read().unwrap();
1245        // A name matching several tables ignoring case is left for the lookup to report.
1246        let is_local = |name: &str| !matches!(key_ignoring_case(&table_map, name), Ok(None));
1247        if self.catalogs.is_empty() {
1248            let recorded = |parts: &[String]| {
1249                let (_, full) = self.catalog_names.iter().find(|(w, _)| w == parts)?;
1250                Some(full.clone())
1251            };
1252            rewrite_catalog_names(stmt, recorded, is_local)
1253        } else {
1254            let resolve = |parts: &[String]| self.catalogs.resolve(parts).map(|t| t.full_name());
1255            rewrite_catalog_names(stmt, resolve, is_local)
1256        }
1257    }
1258
1259    /// Error for a statement changing a table of an attached catalog, which SQL can't do yet.
1260    /// The name resolves as in a read, so a table of the default catalog is also an error.
1261    fn ensure_not_catalog_table(&self, name: &ObjectName, statement: &str) -> PolarsResult<()> {
1262        let Some(parts) = name_parts(name) else {
1263            return Ok(());
1264        };
1265        let named = self.catalogs.named_catalog(&parts);
1266        let Some(table) = self.catalogs.resolve(&parts) else {
1267            return match named {
1268                Some(catalog) => polars_bail!(
1269                    SQLInterface: "{} on a table of attached catalog '{}' is not supported{}",
1270                    statement, catalog, self.catalogs.unresolved_hint(&parts).unwrap_or_default()
1271                ),
1272                None => Ok(()),
1273            };
1274        };
1275        let resolved = match named {
1276            Some(_) => String::new(),
1277            None => format!(
1278                " ('{}' is '{}')",
1279                display_name(&parts),
1280                display_name(&table.full_name())
1281            ),
1282        };
1283        polars_bail!(
1284            SQLInterface: "{} on a table of attached catalog '{}' is not supported{}",
1285            statement, table.catalog, resolved
1286        )
1287    }
1288
1289    /// Execute a SQL query, returning a [`LazyFrame`].
1290    /// ```rust
1291    /// # use polars_sql::SQLContext;
1292    /// # use polars_core::prelude::*;
1293    /// # use polars_lazy::prelude::*;
1294    /// # fn main() {
1295    ///
1296    /// let mut ctx = SQLContext::new();
1297    /// let df = df! {
1298    ///    "a" =>  [1, 2, 3],
1299    /// }
1300    /// .unwrap();
1301    ///
1302    /// ctx.register("df", df.clone().lazy());
1303    /// let sql_df = ctx.execute("SELECT * FROM df").unwrap().collect().unwrap();
1304    /// assert!(sql_df.equals(&df));
1305    /// # }
1306    ///```
1307    pub fn execute(&mut self, query: &str) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
1308        let mut stmt = parse_single_statement(query)?;
1309
1310        if self.can_defer(&stmt) {
1311            // The plan keeps the statement as written: translating it rewrites the names of its
1312            // catalog tables again, also where it was written each.
1313            let catalog_names = match self.catalogs.is_empty() {
1314                true => Vec::new(),
1315                false => self.rewrite_catalog_names(&mut stmt.clone())?.0,
1316            };
1317            return Ok(LazyFrame::from(self.defer_query(
1318                query,
1319                stmt,
1320                &catalog_names,
1321            )));
1322        }
1323
1324        let (_, catalog_spellings) = self.rewrite_catalog_names(&mut stmt)?;
1325        desugar_quantified_subqueries(&mut stmt);
1326        self.catalog_spellings = catalog_spellings;
1327        self.statement_time = Default::default();
1328        let res = self.execute_statement(&stmt).inspect_err(|_| {
1329            self.clear_statement_state();
1330        })?;
1331
1332        // Ensure the result uses the proper arenas.
1333        // This will instantiate new arenas with a new version.
1334        let lp_arena = std::mem::take(&mut self.lp_arena);
1335        let expr_arena = std::mem::take(&mut self.expr_arena);
1336        res.set_cached_arena(lp_arena, expr_arena);
1337
1338        self.clear_statement_state();
1339        Ok(res)
1340    }
1341
1342    /// Whether resolving `stmt` can be deferred to the DSL -> IR conversion.
1343    ///
1344    /// A user-defined function does not survive the round trip through the DSL.
1345    fn can_defer(&self, stmt: &Statement) -> bool {
1346        !self.custom_function_registry && is_read_only_query(stmt)
1347    }
1348
1349    /// Build a [`DslPlan::SQL`] holding `query` and a snapshot of the relations it references.
1350    ///
1351    /// `stmt` is kept alongside so that resolving does not parse `query` again.
1352    fn defer_query(
1353        &self,
1354        query: &str,
1355        mut stmt: Statement,
1356        catalog_names: &[RewrittenName],
1357    ) -> DslPlan {
1358        // Only registered tables: catalog tables travel separately, with their full names.
1359        let table_map = self.table_map.read().unwrap();
1360        let relations = statement_table_identifiers(&stmt, true, true)
1361            .into_iter()
1362            .flat_map(|name| {
1363                if let Ok(Some(lf)) = get_ignoring_case(&table_map, &name) {
1364                    return vec![(PlSmallStr::from_string(name), lf.logical_plan.clone())];
1365                }
1366                // Tables matching only ignoring case are all kept, so resolving reports them.
1367                table_map
1368                    .iter()
1369                    .filter(|(key, _)| key.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&name))
1370                    .map(|(key, lf)| (PlSmallStr::from_str(key), lf.logical_plan.clone()))
1371                    .collect()
1372            })
1373            .collect();
1374
1375        // Catalog tables keep their full names, so parsing `query` again can rewrite it.
1376        let to_parts = |parts: &[String]| parts.iter().map(|p| PlSmallStr::from_str(p)).collect();
1377        let catalog_tables = catalog_names
1378            .iter()
1379            .filter_map(|(written, full)| {
1380                let lf = self.catalog_tables.get(&full.join("."))?;
1381                Some((to_parts(written), to_parts(full), lf.logical_plan.clone()))
1382            })
1383            .collect();
1384
1385        desugar_quantified_subqueries(&mut stmt);
1386        DslPlan::SQL {
1387            query: Arc::new(query.to_owned()),
1388            relations,
1389            catalog_tables,
1390            cached_stmt: CachedSqlStatement::new(Arc::new(stmt)),
1391        }
1392    }
1393
1394    /// Execute `query` eagerly against the given arenas, returning the resulting DSL.
1395    ///
1396    /// Resolves a [`DslPlan::SQL`] node. The caller's arenas are used so that input schemas
1397    /// resolve into the arenas of the ongoing conversion. `cached` is the desugared statement
1398    /// the node was built with, and `query` is only parsed when it is absent.
1399    pub(crate) fn execute_with_arenas(
1400        &mut self,
1401        query: &str,
1402        cached: Option<&Statement>,
1403        lp_arena: &mut Arena<IR>,
1404        expr_arena: &mut Arena<AExpr>,
1405    ) -> PolarsResult<DslPlan> {
1406        let rewritten;
1407        let stmt = match cached {
1408            Some(stmt) if self.catalog_names.is_empty() => stmt,
1409            cached => {
1410                let mut stmt = match cached {
1411                    Some(stmt) => stmt.clone(),
1412                    None => {
1413                        let mut stmt = parse_single_statement(query)?;
1414                        desugar_quantified_subqueries(&mut stmt);
1415                        stmt
1416                    },
1417                };
1418                self.catalog_spellings = self.rewrite_catalog_names(&mut stmt)?.1;
1419                rewritten = stmt;
1420                &rewritten
1421            },
1422        };
1423
1424        self.statement_time = Default::default();
1425        std::mem::swap(&mut self.lp_arena, lp_arena);
1426        std::mem::swap(&mut self.expr_arena, expr_arena);
1427        let res = self.execute_statement(stmt);
1428        std::mem::swap(&mut self.lp_arena, lp_arena);
1429        std::mem::swap(&mut self.expr_arena, expr_arena);
1430
1431        self.clear_statement_state();
1432        Ok(res?.logical_plan)
1433    }
1434
1435    fn clear_statement_state(&mut self) {
1436        self.cte_map.clear();
1437        self.catalog_tables.clear();
1438        self.catalog_names.clear();
1439        self.catalog_spellings.clear();
1440        self.table_aliases.clear();
1441        self.joined_aliases.clear();
1442        self.from_item_frames.clear();
1443        self.join_base = None;
1444        self.exists_values.clear();
1445        self.named_windows.clear();
1446        // a failed statement may not have restored it
1447        self.group_scope = Default::default();
1448    }

1450    /// The local time, to microseconds, that `CURRENT_DATE` and friends read in the current
1451    /// statement.
1452    pub(crate) fn statement_time(&self) -> NaiveDateTime {
1453        *self
1454            .statement_time
1455            .get_or_init(|| chrono::Local::now().naive_local().trunc_subsecs(6))
1456    }
