1478impl SQLContext {
1479    pub(crate) fn isolated(&self) -> Self {
1480        Self {
1481            // Deep-copy/clone to isolate
1482            table_map: Arc::new(RwLock::new(self.table_map.read().unwrap().clone())),
1483            named_windows: self.named_windows.clone(),
1484            cte_map: self.cte_map.clone(),
1485            from_item_frames: self.from_item_frames.clone(),
1486
1487            // Context-level; needs to remain visible in nested scopes.
1488            // (Note: shared by Arc, no need to deep-copy)
1489            function_registry: self.function_registry.clone(),
1490            custom_function_registry: self.custom_function_registry,
1491            catalogs: self.catalogs.clone(),
1492            catalog_tables: self.catalog_tables.clone(),
1493            catalog_names: self.catalog_names.clone(),
1494            catalog_spellings: self.catalog_spellings.clone(),
1495            statement_time: self.statement_time.clone(),
1496            strict_relations: self.strict_relations,
1497            nesting: self.nesting + 1,
1498
1499            ..Default::default()
1500        }
1501    }
1502
1503    pub(crate) fn execute_statement(&mut self, stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
1504        let ast = stmt;
1505        Ok(match ast {
1506            Statement::Query(query) => match query.body.as_ref() {
1507                SetExpr::Insert(Statement::Insert(insert)) => self.execute_insert(insert)?,
1508                _ => self.execute_query(query)?,
1509            },
1510            stmt @ Statement::ShowTables { .. } => self.execute_show_tables(stmt)?,
1511            stmt @ Statement::CreateTable { .. } => self.execute_create_table(stmt)?,
1512            stmt @ Statement::Drop {
1513                object_type: ObjectType::Table,
1514                ..
1515            } => self.execute_drop_table(stmt)?,
1516            stmt @ Statement::CreateSchema { .. } => {
1517                let (name, ..) = create_schema_parts(stmt)?;
1518                self.execute_schema_ddl("CREATE SCHEMA", name)?
1519            },
1520            stmt @ Statement::Drop {
1521                object_type: ObjectType::Schema,
1522                ..
1523            } => {
1524                let (name, _) = drop_schema_parts(stmt)?;
1525                self.execute_schema_ddl("DROP SCHEMA", name)?
1526            },
1527            Statement::AlterTable(alter) => self.execute_alter_table(alter)?,
1528            Statement::Insert(insert) => self.execute_insert(insert)?,
1529            stmt @ Statement::Explain { .. } => self.execute_explain(stmt)?,
1530            Statement::Truncate(truncate) => self.execute_truncate_table(truncate)?,
1531            stmt @ Statement::Delete { .. } => self.execute_delete_from_table(stmt)?,
1532            Statement::Update(update) => self.execute_update(update)?,
1533            Statement::Merge(merge) => self.execute_merge(merge)?,
1534            _ => polars_bail!(
1535                SQLInterface: "statement type is not supported:\n{:?}", ast,
1536            ),
1537        })
1538    }
1539
1540    pub(crate) fn execute_query(&mut self, query: &Query) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
1541        self.register_ctes(query)?;
1542        self.validate_query(query)?;
1543
1544        let lf = self.process_query(&query.body, query)?;
1545        self.process_limit_offset(lf, &query.limit_clause, &query.fetch)
1546    }
1547
1548    pub(crate) fn get_frame_schema(&mut self, frame: &mut LazyFrame) -> PolarsResult<SchemaRef> {
1549        frame.schema_with_arenas(&mut self.lp_arena, &mut self.expr_arena)
1550    }
1551
1552    /// `expr` with each subquery, and each read of its result, replaced by a null of its dtype,
1553    /// so that it can be typed before the subqueries are resolved.
1554    pub(crate) fn with_typed_subqueries(&mut self, expr: &Expr) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
1555        let mut dtypes = PlHashMap::default();
1556        for e in expr {
1557            if let Expr::SubPlan(lp, names) = e {
1558                for (name, select_expr) in names.iter() {
1559                    let mut lf = LazyFrame::from((***lp).clone()).select([select_expr.clone()]);
1560                    let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
1561                    dtypes.insert(name.clone(), schema.get_at_index(0).unwrap().1.clone());
1562                }
1563            }
1564        }
1565        if dtypes.is_empty() {
1566            return Ok(expr.clone());
1567        }
1568        let typed_null = |name: &PlSmallStr| lit(Scalar::null(dtypes[name].clone()));
1569        Ok(expr.clone().map_expr(|e| match &e {
1570            Expr::SubPlan(_, names) => typed_null(&names[0].0),
1571            Expr::Column(name) if dtypes.contains_key(name) => typed_null(name),
1572            _ => e,
1573        }))
1574    }
1575
1576    /// The relation qualifying a compound identifier (see `match_qualifier`) and the qualifier's
1577    /// length. Before a `FROM` is processed, any leading run naming a table qualifies.
1578    pub(crate) fn resolve_qualifier(
1579        &self,
1580        idents: &[Ident],
1581    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<(String, usize)>> {
1582        if self.active_relations.is_empty() {
1583            if self.strict_relations {
1584                return Ok(None);
1585            }
1586            for len in (1..idents.len()).rev() {
1587                let qualifier = join_idents(&idents[..len]);
1588                if self.get_relation_frame(&qualifier)?.is_some() {
1589                    return Ok(Some((qualifier, len)));
1590                }
1591            }
1592            return Ok(None);
1593        }
1594        match match_qualifier(idents, self.active_relations.iter()) {
1595            None => Ok(None),
1596            Some((matches, len)) => match matches.as_slice() {
1597                [relation] => {
1598                    let key = relation.key();
1599                    // Relations are looked up by their dotted name, which `s.t` and an alias
1600                    // `"s.t"` share.
1601                    polars_ensure!(
1602                        !self.active_relations.iter().any(|r| r.key() == key && r != *relation),
1603                        SQLInterface: "ambiguous reference to table \"{}\" (another relation in FROM has the same dotted name; use a different alias)",
1604                        key
1605                    );
1606                    Ok(Some((key, len)))
1607                },
1608                _ => Err(ambiguous_relation_err(
1609                    &join_idents(&idents[..len]),
1610                    &matches,
1611                )),
1612            },
1613        }
1614    }
1615
1616    /// Make the relations of `from` the ones a qualified column may name.
1617    pub(crate) fn set_active_relations(&mut self, from: &[TableWithJoins]) {
1618        self.active_relations = declared_relations(from, &self.catalog_spellings);
1619    }
1620
1621    /// The names the current statement wrote for its catalog tables, by position.
1622    pub(crate) fn catalog_spellings(&self) -> &CatalogSpellings {
1623        &self.catalog_spellings
1624    }
1625
1626    /// Hint for a qualifier that names no relation in scope because an alias hides it.
1627    pub(crate) fn hidden_by_alias_hint(&self, qualifier: &str) -> Option<String> {
1628        self.active_relations.iter().find_map(|alias| {
1629            let alias = alias.key();
1630            let table = self.table_aliases.get(&alias)?;
1631            qualifier_names(table, qualifier)
1632                .then(|| format!("; table \"{qualifier}\" is hidden by alias \"{alias}\""))
1633        })
1634    }
1635
1636    /// Resolve a relation innermost-scope-first: a `FROM` alias, then a CTE, then
1637    /// a registered table.
1638    fn get_table_from_current_scope(&self, name: &str) -> PolarsResult<Option<LazyFrame>> {
1639        if let Some(aliased) = get_ignoring_case(&self.table_aliases, name)? {
1640            if let Some(lf) = self.get_table_unaliased(aliased)? {
1641                return Ok(Some(lf));
1642            }
1643        }
1644        self.get_table_unaliased(name)
1645    }
1646
1647    /// The frame of the relation `name` that a qualified column reads, exact names first.
1648    pub(crate) fn get_relation_frame(&self, name: &str) -> PolarsResult<Option<LazyFrame>> {
1649        if let Some(lf) = self.from_item_frames.get(name) {
1650            return Ok(Some(lf.clone()));
1651        }
1652        if let Some(lf) = self.get_table_from_current_scope(name)? {
1653            return Ok(Some(lf));
1654        }
1655        Ok(get_ignoring_case(&self.from_item_frames, name)?.cloned())
1656    }
1657
1658    fn get_table_unaliased(&self, name: &str) -> PolarsResult<Option<LazyFrame>> {
1659        if let Some(lf) = get_ignoring_case(&self.cte_map, name)? {
1660            return Ok(Some(lf.clone()));
1661        }
1662        if let Some(lf) = get_ignoring_case(&self.table_map.read().unwrap(), name)? {
1663            return Ok(Some(lf.clone()));
1664        }
1665        Ok(get_ignoring_case(&self.catalog_tables, name)?.cloned())
1666    }
1667
1668    /// Restore the catalog tables of a deferred statement: (name as written, full name, plan).
1669    pub(crate) fn restore_catalog_tables(&mut self, tables: Vec<SqlCatalogTable>) {
1670        let to_strings = |parts: &[PlSmallStr]| parts.iter().map(|p| p.to_string()).collect();
1671        for (written, full, plan) in tables {
1672            let full: Vec<String> = to_strings(&full);
1673            self.catalog_tables
1674                .insert(full.join("."), LazyFrame::from(plan));
1675            self.catalog_names.push((to_strings(&written), full));
1676        }
1677    }
1678
1679    /// The registered table `name` refers to (ignoring case, as in `FROM`).
1680    fn registered_table_key(&self, name: &str) -> PolarsResult<Option<String>> {
1681        Ok(key_ignoring_case(&self.table_map.read().unwrap(), name)?.cloned())
1682    }
1683
1684    /// Execute a query in an isolated context. This prevents subqueries from mutating
1685    /// arenas and other context state. Returns both the LazyFrame *and* its associated
1686    /// Schema (so that the correct arenas are used when determining schema).
1687    pub(crate) fn execute_isolated<F>(&mut self, query: F) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame>
1688    where
1689        F: FnOnce(&mut Self) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame>,
1690    {
1691        let mut ctx = self.isolated();
1692        // Not a subquery scope; a subquery caller counts one itself.
1693        ctx.nesting = self.nesting;
1694
1695        // Execute query with clean state (eg: nested/subquery)
1696        let lf = query(&mut ctx)?;
1697
1698        // Save state
1699        lf.set_cached_arena(ctx.lp_arena, ctx.expr_arena);
1700
1701        Ok(lf)
1702    }
1703
1704    fn expr_or_ordinal(
1705        &mut self,
1706        e: &SQLExpr,
1707        exprs: &[Expr],
1708        selected: Option<&[Expr]>,
1709        schema: Option<&Schema>,
1710        clause: &str,
1711    ) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
1712        match e {
1713            SQLExpr::UnaryOp {
1714                op: SQLUnaryOperator::Minus,
1715                expr,
1716            } if matches!(
1717                **expr,
1718                SQLExpr::Value(ValueWithSpan {
1719                    value: SQLValue::Number(_, _),
1720                    ..
1721                })
1722            ) =>
1723            {
1724                if let SQLExpr::Value(ValueWithSpan {
1725                    value: SQLValue::Number(ref idx, _),
1726                    ..
1727                }) = **expr
1728                {
1729                    Err(polars_err!(
1730                    SQLSyntax:
1731                    "negative ordinal values are invalid for {}; found -{}",
1732                    clause,
1733                    idx
1734                    ))
1735                } else {
1736                    unreachable!()
1737                }
1738            },
1739            SQLExpr::Value(ValueWithSpan {
1740                value: SQLValue::Number(idx, _),
1741                ..
1742            }) => {
1743                // note: sql queries are 1-indexed
1744                let idx = idx.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| {
1745                    polars_err!(
1746                        SQLSyntax:
1747                        "negative ordinal values are invalid for {}; found {}",
1748                        clause,
1749                        idx
1750                    )
1751                })?;
1752                // note: "selected" cols represent final projection order, so we use those for
1753                // ordinal resolution. "exprs" may include cols that are subsequently dropped.
1754                let cols = if let Some(cols) = selected {
1755                    cols
1756                } else {
1757                    exprs
1758                };
1759                Ok(cols
1760                    .get(idx - 1)
1761                    .ok_or_else(|| {
1762                        polars_err!(
1763                            SQLInterface:
1764                            "{} ordinal value must refer to a valid column; found {}",
1765                            clause,
1766                            idx
1767                        )
1768                    })?
1769                    .clone())
1770            },
1771            SQLExpr::Value(v) => Err(polars_err!(
1772                SQLSyntax:
1773                "{} requires a valid expression or positive ordinal; found {}", clause, v,
1774            )),
1775            _ => {
1776                // Handle qualified cross-aliasing in ORDER BY clauses
1777                // (eg: `SELECT a AS b, -b AS a ... ORDER BY self.a`)
1778                let mut expr = parse_sql_expr(e, self, schema)?;
1779                if matches!(e, SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(_)) {
1780                    if let Some(schema) = schema {
1781                        expr = expr.map_expr(|ex| match &ex {
1782                            Expr::Column(name) => {
1783                                let prefixed = format!("__POLARS_ORIG_{}", name.as_str());
1784                                if schema.contains(prefixed.as_str()) {
1785                                    col(prefixed)
1786                                } else {
1787                                    ex
1788                                }
1789                            },
1790                            _ => ex,
1791                        });
1792                    }
1793                }
1794                Ok(expr)
1795            },
1796        }
1797    }
1798
1799    /// Track the columns of the joined relation `r_name` that also exist on the left
1800    /// side, and so are stored under an aliased name in the joined frame. The other
1801    /// relations of the right input (`right_relations`) refer to these columns too.
1802    pub(crate) fn record_joined_aliases(
1803        &mut self,
1804        r_name: &str,
1805        right_relations: &[String],
1806        left_schema: &Schema,
1807        right_schema: &Schema,
1808        joined_schema: &Schema,
1809    ) -> PolarsResult<()> {
1810        let renamed: PlHashMap<String, String> = right_schema
1811            .iter_names()
1812            .filter(|name| left_schema.contains(name))
1813            .filter_map(|name| {
1814                let aliased_name = format!("{name}:{r_name}");
1815                joined_schema
1816                    .contains(aliased_name.as_str())
1817                    .then(|| (name.to_string(), aliased_name))
1818            })
1819            .collect();
1820        for relation in right_relations {
1821            if relation == r_name {
1822                continue;
1823            }
1824            let Some(mut relation_lf) = self.get_relation_frame(relation)? else {
1825                continue;
1826            };
1827            let relation_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut relation_lf)?;
1828            let aliases = self.joined_aliases.entry(relation.clone()).or_default();
1829            for name in aliases.values_mut() {
1830                if let Some(aliased_name) = renamed.get(name.as_str()) {
1831                    *name = aliased_name.clone();
1832                }
1833            }
1834            for (name, aliased_name) in &renamed {
1835                if relation_schema.contains(name) && !aliases.contains_key(name) {
1836                    aliases.insert(name.clone(), aliased_name.clone());
1837                }
1838            }
1839        }
1840        self.joined_aliases.insert(r_name.to_string(), renamed);
1841        Ok(())
1842    }
1843
1844    /// Error if the unqualified column `name` exists in more than one of the joined
1845    /// relations of the current `FROM`.
1846    pub(crate) fn check_unqualified_column(&self, name: &str) -> PolarsResult<()> {
1847        match &self.join_base {
1848            Some(base) => check_ambiguous_column(
1849                name,
1850                &self.joined_aliases,
1851                &base.table_name,
1852                &base.using_cols,
1853                &self.active_relations,
1854            ),
1855            None => Ok(()),
1856        }
1857    }
1858
1859    /// Set the join base of a block from its `FROM`, once its relations are resolved.
1860    /// Unqualified columns of the block are checked against it.
1861    pub(crate) fn set_join_base(&mut self, from: &[TableWithJoins]) {
1862        self.join_base = from.first().and_then(|first| {
1863            Some(JoinBase {
1864                table_name: get_table_name(&first.relation)?,
1865                using_cols: from
1866                    .iter()
1867                    .flat_map(|tbl_expr| &tbl_expr.joins)
1868                    .filter_map(|join| {
1869                        let cols = get_using_cols(&join.join_operator)?;
1870                        let r_name = get_table_name(&join.relation)?;
1871                        Some(cols.map(move |c| (r_name.clone(), c)))
1872                    })
1873                    .flatten()
1874                    .collect(),
1875            })
1876        });
1877    }
1878
1879    /// Check the SELECT and WHERE expressions of a block for ambiguous unqualified
1880    /// columns (if there were joins). `schema` is the schema of the joined frame.
1881    pub(crate) fn check_select_column_refs(
1882        &self,
1883        select_stmt: &Select,
1884        schema: &Schema,
1885    ) -> PolarsResult<()> {
1886        let Some(base) = &self.join_base else {
1887            return Ok(());
1888        };
1889        if self.joined_aliases.is_empty() {
1890            return Ok(());
1891        }
1892        let check_expr = |e: &SQLExpr| {
1893            check_for_ambiguous_column_refs(
1894                e,
1895                &self.joined_aliases,
1896                &base.table_name,
1897                &base.using_cols,
1898                &self.active_relations,
1899                schema,
1900            )
1901        };
1902        for item in &select_stmt.projection {
1903            match item {
1904                SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(e) | SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr: e, .. } => {
1905                    check_expr(e)?
1906                },
1907                // `s.*` reads a struct column `s` when no relation is named `s`.
1908                SelectItem::QualifiedWildcard(
1909                    SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::ObjectName(name),
1910                    _,
1911                ) => {
1912                    let parts = name
1913                        .0
1914                        .iter()
1915                        .filter_map(|p| p.as_ident().cloned())
1916                        .chain([Ident::new("*")])
1917                        .collect();
1918                    check_expr(&SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(parts))?
1919                },
1920                _ => {},
1921            }
1922        }
1923        if let Some(where_expr) = &select_stmt.selection {
1924            check_expr(where_expr)?;
1925        }
1926        Ok(())
1927    }
1928
1929    /// The joined-frame name of a column of `tbl_name`, as `resolve_qualifier` returned it.
1930    pub(super) fn resolve_name(&self, tbl_name: &str, column_name: &str) -> String {
1931        if let Some(aliases) = self.joined_aliases.get(tbl_name) {
1932            if let Some(name) = aliases.get(column_name) {
1933                return name.to_string();
1934            }
1935        }
1936        column_name.to_string()
1937    }
1938
1939    /// Clone `query` with `order_by` cleared, for passing to the operands of a set operation.
1940    fn set_op_operand_query(query: &Query) -> Query {
1941        let mut query = query.clone();
1942        query.order_by = None;
1943        query
1944    }
1945
1946    fn process_query(&mut self, expr: &SetExpr, query: &Query) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
1947        match expr {
1948            SetExpr::Select(select_stmt) => self.execute_select(select_stmt, query),
1949            SetExpr::Query(nested_query) => {
1950                // The CTEs of a parenthesized query stay visible to the ORDER BY wrapping it.
1951                let lf = self.execute_query(nested_query)?;
1952                self.process_order_by(lf, &query.order_by, None)
1953            },
1954            SetExpr::SetOperation {
1955                op: SetOperator::Union,
1956                set_quantifier,
1957                left,
1958                right,
1959            } => self.process_union(left, right, set_quantifier, query),
1960
1961            #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
1962            SetExpr::SetOperation {
1963                op: op @ (SetOperator::Intersect | SetOperator::Except),
1964                set_quantifier,
1965                left,
1966                right,
1967            } => self.process_except_intersect(left, right, op, set_quantifier, query),
1968
1969            SetExpr::Values(Values {
1970                explicit_row: _,
1971                rows,
1972                value_keyword: _,
1973            }) => {
1974                let lf = self.process_values(rows.iter().map(|p| &p.content))?;
1975                self.process_order_by(lf, &query.order_by, None)
1976            },
1977
1978            SetExpr::Table(tbl) => {
1979                if let Some(table_name) = tbl.table_name.as_ref() {
1980                    let name = match &tbl.schema_name {
1981                        Some(schema_name) => format!("{schema_name}.{table_name}"),
1982                        None => table_name.clone(),
1983                    };
1984                    self.get_table_from_current_scope(&name)?.ok_or_else(|| {
1985                        polars_err!(
1986                            SQLInterface: "no table or alias named '{}' found",
1987                            tbl
1988                        )
1989                    })
1990                } else {
1991                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "'TABLE' requires valid table name")
1992                }
1993            },
1994            op => {
1995                polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "'{}' operation is currently unsupported", op)
1996            },
1997        }
1998    }
1999
2000    #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
2001    fn process_except_intersect(
2002        &mut self,
2003        left: &SetExpr,
2004        right: &SetExpr,
2005        op: &SetOperator,
2006        quantifier: &SetQuantifier,
2007        query: &Query,
2008    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2009        let (join_type, op_name) = match op {
2010            SetOperator::Except => (JoinType::Anti, "EXCEPT"),
2011            SetOperator::Intersect => (JoinType::Semi, "INTERSECT"),
2012            _ => unreachable!("process_except_intersect is only reached for EXCEPT/INTERSECT"),
2013        };
2014
2015        // Note: each side of the EXCEPT/INTERSECT operation should execute
2016        // in isolation to prevent context state leakage between them
2017        let operand_query = Self::set_op_operand_query(query);
2018        let mut lf = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.process_query(left, &operand_query))?;
2019        let mut rf = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.process_query(right, &operand_query))?;
2020        let lf_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
2021        let rf_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut rf)?;
2022
2023        let lf_cols: Vec<_> = lf_schema.iter_names_cloned().map(col).collect();
2024        let bag_semantics = matches!(quantifier, SetQuantifier::All);
2025        let rf_cols = match quantifier {
2026            SetQuantifier::ByName => None,
2027            SetQuantifier::Distinct | SetQuantifier::None | SetQuantifier::All => {
2028                let rf_cols: Vec<_> = rf_schema.iter_names_cloned().map(col).collect();
2029                if lf_cols.len() != rf_cols.len() {
2030                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "{} requires equal number of columns in each table (use '{} BY NAME' to combine mismatched tables)", op_name, op_name)
2031                }
2032                Some(rf_cols)
2033            },
2034            _ => {
2035                polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "'{} {}' is not supported", op_name, quantifier.to_string())
2036            },
2037        };
2038
2039        // The rows are compared as values of each column's common type, as UNION
2040        // combines them.
2041        let mut lf_casts = Vec::new();
2042        let mut rf_casts = Vec::new();
2043        for (i, (l_name, l_dtype)) in lf_schema.iter().enumerate() {
2044            let right = match rf_cols {
2045                Some(_) => rf_schema.get_at_index(i),
2046                None => rf_schema
2047                    .get_full(l_name)
2048                    .map(|(_, name, dtype)| (name, dtype)),
2049            };
2050            let Some((r_name, r_dtype)) = right else {
2051                continue;
2052            };
2053            if l_dtype != r_dtype {
2054                let dtype = try_get_supertype(l_dtype, r_dtype)?;
2055                lf_casts.push(cast_matching_struct_fields(l_name, l_dtype, &dtype));
2056                rf_casts.push(cast_matching_struct_fields(r_name, r_dtype, &dtype));
2057            }
2058        }
2059        if !lf_casts.is_empty() {
2060            lf = lf.with_columns(lf_casts);
2061            rf = rf.with_columns(rf_casts);
2062        }
2063
2064        let lf = if bag_semantics {
2065            let occurrence_col = unique_column_name();
2066            let mut lf_on = lf_cols.clone();
2067            let mut rf_on =
2068                rf_cols.expect("ALL quantifier always resolves the right-hand columns above");
2069
2070            lf = lf.with_column(
2071                int_range(lit(0), len(), 1, DataType::Int64)
2072                    .over(lf_cols.clone())?
2073                    .alias(occurrence_col.clone()),
2074            );
2075            rf = rf.with_column(
2076                int_range(lit(0), len(), 1, DataType::Int64)
2077                    .over(rf_on.clone())?
2078                    .alias(occurrence_col.clone()),
2079            );
2080            lf_on.push(col(occurrence_col.clone()));
2081            rf_on.push(col(occurrence_col.clone()));
2082
2083            let joined_tbl = lf
2084                .join_builder()
2085                .with(rf)
2086                .how(join_type)
2087                .join_nulls(true)
2088                .left_on(lf_on)
2089                .right_on(rf_on)
2090                .finish()?;
2091            joined_tbl.drop(cols([occurrence_col]))
2092        } else {
2093            let join = lf.join_builder().with(rf).how(join_type).join_nulls(true);
2094            let joined_tbl = match rf_cols {
2095                Some(rf_cols) => join.left_on(lf_cols).right_on(rf_cols).finish(),
2096                None => join.on(lf_cols).finish(),
2097            }?;
2098            joined_tbl.unique(None, UniqueKeepStrategy::Any)
2099        };
2100        self.process_order_by(lf, &query.order_by, None)
2101    }
2102
2103    fn process_union(
2104        &mut self,
2105        left: &SetExpr,
2106        right: &SetExpr,
2107        quantifier: &SetQuantifier,
2108        query: &Query,
2109    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2110        let quantifier = *quantifier;
2111
2112        // Note: each side of the UNION operation should execute
2113        // in isolation to prevent context state leakage between them
2114        let operand_query = Self::set_op_operand_query(query);
2115        let mut lf = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.process_query(left, &operand_query))?;
2116        let mut rf = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.process_query(right, &operand_query))?;
2117
2118        let opts = UnionArgs {
2119            parallel: true,
2120            to_supertypes: true,
2121            maintain_order: false,
2122            ..Default::default()
2123        };
2124        let lf = match quantifier {
2125            // UNION [ALL | DISTINCT]
2126            SetQuantifier::All | SetQuantifier::Distinct | SetQuantifier::None => {
2127                let lf_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
2128                let rf_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut rf)?;
2129                if lf_schema.len() != rf_schema.len() {
2130                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "UNION requires equal number of columns in each table (use 'UNION BY NAME' to combine mismatched tables)")
2131                }
2132                // rename `rf` columns to match `lf` if they differ; SQL behaves
2133                // positionally on UNION ops (unless using the "BY NAME" qualifier)
2134                if lf_schema.iter_names().ne(rf_schema.iter_names()) {
2135                    rf = rf.rename(rf_schema.iter_names(), lf_schema.iter_names(), true);
2136                }
2137                let concatenated = concat(vec![lf, rf], opts);
2138                match quantifier {
2139                    SetQuantifier::Distinct | SetQuantifier::None => {
2140                        concatenated.map(|lf| lf.unique(None, UniqueKeepStrategy::Any))
2141                    },
2142                    _ => concatenated,
2143                }
2144            },
2145            // UNION ALL BY NAME
2146            #[cfg(feature = "diagonal_concat")]
2147            SetQuantifier::AllByName => concat_lf_diagonal(vec![lf, rf], opts),
2148            // UNION [DISTINCT] BY NAME
2149            #[cfg(feature = "diagonal_concat")]
2150            SetQuantifier::ByName | SetQuantifier::DistinctByName => {
2151                let concatenated = concat_lf_diagonal(vec![lf, rf], opts);
2152                concatenated.map(|lf| lf.unique(None, UniqueKeepStrategy::Any))
2153            },
2154            #[allow(unreachable_patterns)]
2155            _ => {
2156                polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "'UNION {}' is not currently supported", quantifier)
2157            },
2158        }?;
2159
2160        self.process_order_by(lf, &query.order_by, None)
2161    }
2162
2163    /// Process UNNEST as a lateral operation when it contains column references
2164    /// (handles `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(col) AS name` by exploding the referenced col).
2165    fn process_unnest_lateral(
2166        &self,
2167        lf: LazyFrame,
2168        alias: &Option<TableAlias>,
2169        array_exprs: &[SQLExpr],
2170        with_offset: bool,
2171    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2172        let alias = alias
2173            .as_ref()
2174            .ok_or_else(|| polars_err!(SQLSyntax: "UNNEST table must have an alias"))?;
2175        polars_ensure!(!with_offset, SQLInterface: "UNNEST tables do not (yet) support WITH ORDINALITY|OFFSET");
2176
2177        let (mut explode_cols, mut rename_from, mut rename_to) = (
2178            Vec::with_capacity(array_exprs.len()),
2179            Vec::with_capacity(array_exprs.len()),
2180            Vec::with_capacity(array_exprs.len()),
2181        );
2182        let is_single_col = array_exprs.len() == 1;
2183
2184        for (i, arr_expr) in array_exprs.iter().enumerate() {
2185            let col_name = match arr_expr {
2186                SQLExpr::Identifier(ident) => PlSmallStr::from_str(&ident.value),
2187                SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(parts) => {
2188                    PlSmallStr::from_str(&parts.last().unwrap().value)
2189                },
2190                SQLExpr::Array(_) => polars_bail!(
2191                    SQLInterface: "CROSS JOIN UNNEST with both literal arrays and column references is not supported"
2192                ),
2193                other => polars_bail!(
2194                    SQLSyntax: "UNNEST expects column references or array literals, found {:?}", other
2195                ),
2196            };
2197            // alias: column name from "AS t(col)", or table alias
2198            if let Some(name) = alias
2199                .columns
2200                .get(i)
2201                .map(|c| c.name.value.as_str())
2202                .or_else(|| is_single_col.then_some(alias.name.value.as_str()))
2203                .filter(|name| !name.is_empty() && *name != col_name.as_str())
2204            {
2205                rename_from.push(col_name.clone());
2206                rename_to.push(PlSmallStr::from_str(name));
2207            }
2208            explode_cols.push(col_name);
2209        }
2210
2211        let mut lf = lf.explode(
2212            Selector::ByName {
2213                names: Arc::from(explode_cols),
2214                strict: true,
2215            },
2216            ExplodeOptions {
2217                empty_as_null: true,
2218                keep_nulls: true,
2219            },
2220        );
2221        if !rename_from.is_empty() {
2222            lf = lf.rename(rename_from, rename_to, true);
2223        }
2224        Ok(lf)
2225    }
2226
2227    fn process_values<'a>(
2228        &mut self,
2229        values: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Vec<SQLExpr>>,
2230    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2231        let frame_rows: Vec<Vec<AnyValue>> = values.map(|row| {
2232            row.iter().map(|expr| {
2233                let expr = parse_sql_expr(expr, self, None)?;
2234                match expr {
2235                    Expr::Literal(value) => {
2236                        value.to_any_value()
2237                            .ok_or_else(|| polars_err!(SQLInterface: "invalid literal value: {:?}", value))
2238                            .map(|av| av.into_static())
2239                    },
2240                    _ => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "VALUES clause expects literals; found {}", expr),
2241                }
2242            }).collect()
2243        }).collect::<PolarsResult<_>>()?;
2244
2245        // Each column takes the supertype of all its rows, not the first row's type.
2246        let width = frame_rows.first().map_or(0, Vec::len);
2247        polars_ensure!(
2248            frame_rows.iter().all(|row| row.len() == width),
2249            SQLSyntax: "VALUES rows must all have the same number of values"
2250        );
2251        let columns = (0..width)
2252            .map(|i| {
2253                let values: Vec<AnyValue> = frame_rows.iter().map(|row| row[i].clone()).collect();
2254                series_from_literals(format_pl_smallstr!("column_{i}"), &values).map(Column::from)
2255            })
2256            .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
2257        Ok(DataFrame::new_infer_height(columns)?.lazy())
2258    }
2259
2260    // EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM DF
2261    fn execute_explain(&mut self, stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2262        match stmt {
2263            Statement::Explain { statement, .. } => {
2264                let lf = self.execute_statement(statement)?;
2265                let plan = lf.describe_optimized_plan()?;
2266                let plan = plan
2267                    .split('\n')
2268                    .collect::<Series>()
2269                    .with_name(PlSmallStr::from_static("Logical Plan"))
2270                    .into_column();
2271                let df = DataFrame::new_infer_height(vec![plan])?;
2272                Ok(df.lazy())
2273            },
2274            _ => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "unexpected statement type; expected EXPLAIN"),
2275        }
2276    }
2277
2278    // SHOW TABLES
2279    fn execute_show_tables(&mut self, _: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2280        let tables = Column::new("name".into(), self.get_tables());
2281        let df = DataFrame::new_infer_height(vec![tables])?;
2282        Ok(df.lazy())
2283    }
2284
2285    // DROP TABLE <tbl>
2286    fn execute_drop_table(&mut self, stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2287        let (names, if_exists, purge) = drop_table_parts(stmt)?;
2288        if let Some((name, table)) = self.catalog_drop_target(names, purge)? {
2289            polars_bail!(
2290                SQLInterface: "DROP TABLE of catalog table '{}' ('{}') must be performed on the catalog (see `SQLContext::catalog_statement`)",
2291                name, display_name(&table.full_name())
2292            );
2293        }
2294
2295        let mut table_map = self.table_map.write().unwrap();
2296        // Resolve every name before dropping any, so an error drops nothing.
2297        let mut keys = Vec::with_capacity(names.len());
2298        for name in names {
2299            let tbl = object_name_to_string(name);
2300            // `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS <tbl>` is a no-op on a missing table;
2301            // otherwise dropping a table that doesn't exist is an error.
2302            match key_ignoring_case(&table_map, &tbl)?.cloned() {
2303                Some(key) => keys.push(key),
2304                None if if_exists => {},
2305                None => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "table '{}' does not exist", tbl),
2306            }
2307        }
2308        for key in keys {
2309            table_map.remove(&key);
2310        }
2311        Ok(DataFrame::empty().lazy())
2312    }
2313
2314    /// The catalog table a `DROP TABLE` targets, with its name as written. A registered table
2315    /// of that name comes first, as in a read.
2316    fn catalog_drop_target(
2317        &self,
2318        names: &[ObjectName],
2319        purge: bool,
2320    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<(String, CatalogTable)>> {
2321        let mut target = None;
2322        for name in names {
2323            // Only names that resolve are checked against registered tables, so other names
2324            // keep their errors in order.
2325            let Some(table) = name_parts(name).and_then(|parts| self.catalogs.resolve(&parts))
2326            else {
2327                continue;
2328            };
2329            let tbl = object_name_to_string(name);
2330            if self.registered_table_key(&tbl)?.is_some() {
2331                continue;
2332            }
2333            polars_ensure!(
2334                names.len() == 1,
2335                SQLInterface: "DROP TABLE of catalog table '{}' ('{}') takes one table name",
2336                tbl, display_name(&table.full_name())
2337            );
2338            target = Some((tbl, table));
2339        }
2340        polars_ensure!(
2341            !purge || target.is_some(),
2342            SQLInterface: "`DROP ... PURGE` only applies to catalog tables"
2343        );
2344        Ok(target)
2345    }
2346
2347    /// The catalog namespace a `CREATE SCHEMA` or `DROP SCHEMA` of `name` targets, with the name
2348    /// as written; `None` if no catalog applies.
2349    fn catalog_schema_target(
2350        &self,
2351        name: &ObjectName,
2352    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<(String, CatalogNamespace)>> {
2353        if self.catalogs.is_empty() {
2354            return Ok(None);
2355        }
2356        let schema = object_name_to_string(name);
2357        let Some(parts) = name_parts(name) else {
2358            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "invalid schema name '{}'", schema)
2359        };
2360        polars_ensure!(
2361            parts.iter().all(|part| !part.is_empty()),
2362            SQLInterface: "schema name '{}' has an empty part", schema
2363        );
2364        if let [one] = parts.as_slice()
2365            && let Some(catalog) = self.catalogs.catalog_name(one)
2366        {
2367            polars_bail!(
2368                SQLInterface: "'{}' is an attached catalog; write '{}.<schema>', or '<catalog>.{}' for a schema of that name",
2369                one, catalog, one
2370            );
2371        }
2372        Ok(self
2373            .catalogs
2374            .resolve_namespace(&parts)
2375            .map(|namespace| (schema, namespace)))
2376    }
2377
2378    // CREATE SCHEMA / DROP SCHEMA, which only a catalog has
2379    fn execute_schema_ddl(&self, statement: &str, name: &ObjectName) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2380        if let Some((name, namespace)) = self.catalog_schema_target(name)? {
2381            polars_bail!(
2382                SQLInterface: "{} of catalog schema '{}' ('{}') must be performed on the catalog (see `SQLContext::catalog_statement`)",
2383                statement, name, display_name(&namespace.full_name())
2384            );
2385        }
2386        polars_ensure!(
2387            !self.catalogs.is_empty(),
2388            SQLInterface: "`{}` is supported only for attached catalogs", statement
2389        );
2390        polars_bail!(
2391            SQLInterface: "schema '{}' has no catalog: no default catalog is set; write '<catalog>.{}'",
2392            object_name_to_string(name), object_name_to_string(name)
2393        )
2394    }
2395
2396    /// The catalog table an `ALTER TABLE` or `INSERT` of `name` changes, with its name as written.
2397    /// A registered table of that name comes first, as in a read, and has neither.
2398    fn catalog_change_target(
2399        &self,
2400        name: &ObjectName,
2401    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<(String, CatalogTable)>> {
2402        let tbl = object_name_to_string(name);
2403        if self.registered_table_key(&tbl)?.is_some() {
2404            return Ok(None);
2405        }
2406        Ok(name_parts(name)
2407            .and_then(|parts| self.catalogs.resolve(&parts))
2408            .map(|table| (tbl, table)))
2409    }
2410
2411    /// The catalog statement of an `ALTER TABLE`, if its name resolves to a catalog table.
2412    fn catalog_alter_table(&self, alter: &AlterTable) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
2413        let Some((name, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(&alter.name)? else {
2414            return Ok(None);
2415        };
2416        polars_ensure!(!alter.only, SQLInterface: "`ALTER TABLE ONLY` is not supported");
2417        polars_ensure!(
2418            alter.location.is_none() && alter.on_cluster.is_none() && alter.table_type.is_none(),
2419            SQLInterface: "unsupported ALTER TABLE statement: `{}`", alter
2420        );
2421        let [op] = alter.operations.as_slice() else {
2422            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "`ALTER TABLE` takes one operation per statement")
2423        };
2424        Ok(Some(CatalogStatement::AlterTable {
2425            name,
2426            table,
2427            if_exists: alter.if_exists,
2428            operation: alter_table_operation(op)?,
2429        }))
2430    }
2431
2432    // ALTER TABLE, which only a catalog table has
2433    fn execute_alter_table(&self, alter: &AlterTable) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2434        if let Some((name, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(&alter.name)? {
2435            polars_bail!(
2436                SQLInterface: "ALTER TABLE of catalog table '{}' ('{}') must be performed on the catalog (see `SQLContext::catalog_statement`)",
2437                name, display_name(&table.full_name())
2438            );
2439        }
2440        Err(self.catalog_tables_only("ALTER TABLE", &alter.name))
2441    }
2442
2443    /// The error of `statement` on `name`, which is not a catalog table.
2444    fn catalog_tables_only(&self, statement: &str, name: &ObjectName) -> PolarsError {
2445        let tbl = object_name_to_string(name);
2446        let parts = name_parts(name);
2447        // a registered table hides the catalog table of that name
2448        let hint = match parts
2449            .as_deref()
2450            .and_then(|parts| self.catalogs.resolve(parts))
2451        {
2452            Some(table) => format!(
2453                "; '{}' is a registered table, write '{}' for the catalog table",
2454                tbl,
2455                display_name(&table.full_name())
2456            ),
2457            None => parts
2458                .and_then(|parts| self.catalogs.unresolved_hint(&parts))
2459                .unwrap_or_default(),
2460        };
2461        polars_err!(SQLInterface: "`{}` is supported only for catalog tables{}", statement, hint)
2462    }
2463
2464    /// The catalog statement of an `INSERT`, if its table resolves to a catalog table; `outer` is a
2465    /// query around it (`WITH ... INSERT ...`).
2466    fn catalog_insert(
2467        &self,
2468        insert: &Insert,
2469        outer: Option<&Query>,
2470    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
2471        let TableObject::TableName(name) = &insert.table else {
2472            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "`INSERT` into a table function is not supported")
2473        };
2474        let Some((tbl, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(name)? else {
2475            return Ok(None);
2476        };
2477        let Some(source) = insert_source(insert, outer)? else {
2478            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "`INSERT ... DEFAULT VALUES` is not supported for catalog tables")
2479        };
2480        let columns = insert
2481            .columns
2482            .iter()
2483            .map(|column| match name_parts(column).as_deref() {
2484                Some([part]) => Ok(part.clone()),
2485                _ => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "INSERT column names must be unqualified; found `{}`", column),
2486            })
2487            .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
2488        Ok(Some(CatalogStatement::Insert {
2489            name: tbl,
2490            table,
2491            columns,
2492            query: source.to_string(),
2493            overwrite: insert.overwrite,
2494        }))
2495    }
2496
2497    // INSERT, which only a catalog table has
2498    fn execute_insert(&self, insert: &Insert) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2499        let statement = if insert.overwrite {
2500            "INSERT OVERWRITE"
2501        } else {
2502            "INSERT"
2503        };
2504        let TableObject::TableName(name) = &insert.table else {
2505            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "`INSERT` into a table function is not supported")
2506        };
2507        if let Some((tbl, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(name)? {
2508            polars_bail!(
2509                SQLInterface: "{} of catalog table '{}' ('{}') must be performed on the catalog (see `SQLContext::catalog_statement`)",
2510                statement, tbl, display_name(&table.full_name())
2511            );
2512        }
2513        Err(self.catalog_tables_only(statement, name))
2514    }
2515
2516    // DELETE FROM <tbl> [WHERE ...]
2517    fn execute_delete_from_table(&mut self, stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2518        let Statement::Delete(delete) = stmt else {
2519            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "unexpected statement type; expected DELETE")
2520        };
2521        let (from, selection) = delete_parts(delete)?;
2522        if let TableFactor::Table { name, .. } = &from.relation
2523            && let Some((tbl, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(name)?
2524        {
2525            polars_bail!(
2526                SQLInterface: "DELETE of catalog table '{}' ('{}') must be performed on the catalog (see `SQLContext::catalog_statement`)",
2527                tbl, display_name(&table.full_name())
2528            );
2529        }
2530        let lf = self.delete_target(from)?;
2531        match selection {
2532            // no WHERE clause; equivalent to TRUNCATE (drop all rows)
2533            None => Ok(lf.clear()),
2534            // apply constraint as inverted filter (drops rows matching the selection)
2535            Some(selection) => {
2536                self.process_where(lf, Some(selection), FilterMode::RemoveTrue, None)
2537            },
2538        }
2539    }
2540
2541    fn delete_target(&mut self, from: &TableWithJoins) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2542        self.set_active_relations(std::slice::from_ref(from));
2543        Ok(self.get_table(&from.relation)?.1)
2544    }

2546    /// The catalog statement of a `DELETE`, if its table resolves to a catalog table.
2547    fn catalog_delete(&self, delete: &Delete) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
2548        let (from, selection) = delete_parts(delete)?;
2549        let TableFactor::Table { name, .. } = &from.relation else {
2550            return Ok(None);
2551        };
2552        let Some((tbl, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(name)? else {
2553            return Ok(None);
2554        };
2555        Ok(Some(CatalogStatement::Delete {
2556            name: tbl,
2557            table,
2558            condition: selection.map(|selection| selection.to_string()),
2559            subquery: selection.is_some_and(expr_contains_subquery),
2560            hint_unsupported_part: selection.and_then(hint_unsupported_part),
2561        }))
2562    }

2564    /// The catalog statement of an `UPDATE`, if its table resolves to a catalog table.
2565    fn catalog_update(&self, update: &Update) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
2566        let (target, assignments, selection) = update_parts(update)?;
2567        let TableFactor::Table { name, .. } = &target.relation else {
2568            return Ok(None);
2569        };
2570        let Some((tbl, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(name)? else {
2571            return Ok(None);
2572        };
2573        Ok(Some(CatalogStatement::Update {
2574            name: tbl,
2575            table,
2576            columns: assignments.into_iter().map(|(column, _)| column).collect(),
2577            condition: selection.map(|selection| selection.to_string()),
2578            subquery: selection.is_some_and(expr_contains_subquery),
2579            hint_unsupported_part: selection.and_then(hint_unsupported_part),
2580        }))
2581    }

2583    // UPDATE <tbl> SET ... [WHERE ...]: only for catalog tables

2598    /// The catalog statement of a `MERGE`, if its target resolves to a catalog table.

2613            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "MERGE requires a named catalog table as its target")
2614        };

2624    // TRUNCATE <tbl>
2625    fn execute_truncate_table(&mut self, truncate: &Truncate) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2626        let (name, if_exists) = truncate_parts(truncate)?;
2627        if let Some((tbl, table)) = self.catalog_change_target(name)? {
2628            polars_bail!(
2629                SQLInterface: "TRUNCATE of catalog table '{}' ('{}') must be performed on the catalog (see `SQLContext::catalog_statement`)",
2630                tbl, display_name(&table.full_name())
2631            );
2632        }
2633        let tbl = object_name_to_string(name);
2634        let mut table_map = self.table_map.write().unwrap();
2635        match key_ignoring_case(&table_map, &tbl)?.cloned() {
2636            Some(key) => {
2637                let lf = table_map.get_mut(&key).unwrap();
2638                *lf = lf.clone().clear();
2639                Ok(lf.clone())
2640            },
2641            // `TRUNCATE TABLE IF EXISTS <tbl>` is a no-op on a missing table.
2642            None if if_exists => Ok(DataFrame::empty().lazy()),
2643            None => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "table '{}' does not exist", tbl),
2644        }
2645    }
2646
2647    /// The catalog statement of a `TRUNCATE`, if its name resolves to a catalog table.
2648    fn catalog_truncate(&self, truncate: &Truncate) -> PolarsResult<Option<CatalogStatement>> {
2649        let (name, if_exists) = truncate_parts(truncate)?;
2650        Ok(self
2651            .catalog_change_target(name)?
2652            .map(|(name, table)| CatalogStatement::Truncate {
2653                name,
2654                table,
2655                if_exists,
2656            }))
2657    }
2658
2659    fn register_cte(&mut self, name: &str, lf: LazyFrame) {
2660        // Lookups ignore case, so a new name must replace an outer one that differs only in case.
2661        self.cte_map
2662            .retain(|key, _| !key.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name));
2663        self.cte_map.insert(name.to_owned(), lf);
2664    }
2665
2666    fn register_ctes(&mut self, query: &Query) -> PolarsResult<()> {
2667        if let Some(with) = &query.with {
2668            let (order, reads_itself) = if with.recursive {
2669                recursive_cte_order(with)?
2670            } else {
2671                let n = with.cte_tables.len();
2672                ((0..n).collect(), vec![false; n])
2673            };
2674            let mut reference_counts = PlHashMap::<String, usize>::new();
2675            let mut collector = TableIdentifierCollector::default();
2676            let _ = dyn_visit::visit(query, &mut collector);
2677            for name in collector.tables {
2678                *reference_counts.entry(name).or_insert(0) += 1;
2679            }
2680            // The step of a recursive CTE reads the working table, not the CTE itself.
2681            for (cte, _) in with
2682                .cte_tables
2683                .iter()
2684                .zip(&reads_itself)
2685                .filter(|(_, r)| **r)
2686            {
2687                let name = &cte.alias.name.value;
2688                let mut collector = TableIdentifierCollector::default();
2689                let _ = dyn_visit::visit(&*cte.query, &mut collector);
2690                let n_self = collector.tables.iter().filter(|t| *t == name).count();
2691                if let Some(count) = reference_counts.get_mut(name) {
2692                    *count = count.saturating_sub(n_self);
2693                }
2694            }
2695
2696            for idx in order {
2697                let cte = &with.cte_tables[idx];
2698                let cte_name = cte.alias.name.value.clone();
2699                let mut lf = if reads_itself[idx] {
2700                    self.execute_recursive_cte(cte)?
2701                } else {
2702                    // Note: isolate CTE execution to prevent context state leakage
2703                    let lf = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.execute_query(&cte.query))?;
2704                    self.rename_columns_from_table_alias(lf, &cte.alias)?
2705                };
2706                if reference_counts.get(&cte_name).copied().unwrap_or(0) > 1 {
2707                    lf = lf.cache();
2708                }
2709                self.register_cte(&cte_name, lf);
2710            }
2711        }
2712        Ok(())
2713    }
2714
2715    /// Plans a CTE that reads itself: `anchor UNION ALL step`, where only `step` reads the CTE.
2716    /// The step reads the rows of the round before.
2717    fn execute_recursive_cte(&mut self, cte: &Cte) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2718        let name = &cte.alias.name.value;
2719        let query = &cte.query;
2720        let SetExpr::SetOperation {
2721            op: SetOperator::Union,
2722            set_quantifier,
2723            left,
2724            right,
2725        } = &*query.body
2726        else {
2727            polars_bail!(
2728                SQLInterface: "recursive CTE '{}' must have the form `anchor UNION ALL step`", name
2729            )
2730        };
2731        polars_ensure!(
2732            matches!(set_quantifier, SetQuantifier::All),
2733            SQLInterface: "recursive CTE '{}' only supports UNION ALL", name
2734        );
2735        polars_ensure!(
2736            query.with.is_none()
2737                && query.order_by.is_none()
2738                && query.limit_clause.is_none()
2739                && query.fetch.is_none(),
2740            SQLInterface: "recursive CTE '{}' does not support WITH, ORDER BY, LIMIT or FETCH around its UNION ALL", name
2741        );
2742        let term_query = |body: &SetExpr| Query {
2743            body: Box::new(body.clone()),
2744            ..query.as_ref().clone()
2745        };
2746        let anchor_query = term_query(left);
2747        let step_query = term_query(right);
2748        polars_ensure!(
2749            referenced_ctes(&anchor_query, std::slice::from_ref(name)).is_empty(),
2750            SQLInterface: "the anchor of recursive CTE '{}' may not read '{}'", name, name
2751        );
2752
2753        let anchor = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.execute_query(&anchor_query))?;
2754        let mut anchor = self.rename_columns_from_table_alias(anchor, &cte.alias)?;
2755        let mut schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut anchor)?;
2756
2757        // The step runs once per round, so a CTE it reads is cached to compute it only once.
2758        let mut collector = TableIdentifierCollector::default();
2759        let _ = dyn_visit::visit(&step_query, &mut collector);
2760        for (cte_name, lf) in self.cte_map.iter_mut() {
2761            let read_by_step = collector
2762                .tables
2763                .iter()
2764                .any(|t| t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(cte_name) && !t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name));
2765            if read_by_step && !matches!(lf.logical_plan, DslPlan::Cache { .. }) {
2766                *lf = lf.clone().cache();
2767            }
2768        }
2769        let known_caches = self.cache_ids();
2770        let id = UniqueId::new();
2771        // A column with a NULL anchor takes the type of the step. Each pass can type one more
2772        // column, as a column may get its type from another column of the round before.
2773        let mut step;
2774        let mut passes = 0;
2775        loop {
2776            self.register_cte(
2777                name,
2778                DslPlan::WorkingTable {
2779                    id,
2780                    schema: schema.clone(),
2781                }
2782                .into(),
2783            );
2784            step = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.execute_query(&step_query))?;
2785            let step_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut step)?;
2786            polars_ensure!(
2787                step_schema.len() == schema.len(),
2788                SQLInterface: "the anchor and the step of recursive CTE '{}' have a different number of columns ({} and {})",
2789                name, schema.len(), step_schema.len()
2790            );
2791            let typed_schema: Schema = schema
2792                .iter()
2793                .zip(step_schema.iter_values())
2794                .map(|((col_name, dtype), step_dtype)| {
2795                    let dtype = if dtype.is_null() { step_dtype } else { dtype };
2796                    (col_name.clone(), dtype.clone())
2797                })
2798                .collect();
2799            passes += 1;
2800            if typed_schema == *schema || passes > schema.len() {
2801                break;
2802            }
2803            schema = Arc::new(typed_schema);
2804        }
2805
2806        let cast_to_schema = |lf: LazyFrame, lf_schema: &Schema| {
2807            let exprs: Vec<Expr> = lf_schema
2808                .iter()
2809                .zip(schema.iter())
2810                .map(|((lf_name, lf_dtype), (col_name, dtype))| {
2811                    let e = if lf_dtype == dtype {
2812                        col(lf_name.clone())
2813                    } else {
2814                        cast_matching_struct_fields(lf_name, lf_dtype, dtype)
2815                    };
2816                    e.alias(col_name.clone())
2817                })
2818                .collect();
2819            lf.select(exprs)
2820        };
2821        let anchor_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut anchor)?;
2822        let anchor = cast_to_schema(anchor, &anchor_schema);
2823        let step_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut step)?;
2824        let step = cast_to_schema(step, &step_schema);
2825
2826        let round_local_caches: Arc<[UniqueId]> = (&step.logical_plan)
2827            .into_iter()
2828            .filter_map(|plan| match plan {
2829                DslPlan::Cache { id, .. } if !known_caches.contains(id) => Some(*id),
2830                _ => None,
2831            })
2832            .collect::<PlIndexSet<_>>()
2833            .into_iter()
2834            .collect();
2835
2836        Ok(DslPlan::Recursive {
2837            anchor: Arc::new(anchor.logical_plan),
2838            step: Arc::new(step.logical_plan),
2839            id,
2840            round_local_caches,
2841        }
2842        .into())
2843    }
2844
2845    /// The ids of the caches in the registered tables, catalog tables and CTEs.
2846    fn cache_ids(&self) -> PlHashSet<UniqueId> {
2847        let table_map = self.table_map.read().unwrap();
2848        table_map
2849            .values()
2850            .chain(self.catalog_tables.values())
2851            .chain(self.cte_map.values())
2852            .flat_map(|lf| &lf.logical_plan)
2853            .filter_map(|plan| match plan {
2854                DslPlan::Cache { id, .. } => Some(*id),
2855                _ => None,
2856            })
2857            .collect()
2858    }
2859
2860    fn register_named_windows(
2861        &mut self,
2862        named_windows: &[NamedWindowDefinition],
2863    ) -> PolarsResult<()> {
2864        for NamedWindowDefinition(name, expr) in named_windows {
2865            let spec = match expr {
2866                NamedWindowExpr::NamedWindow(ref_name) => self
2867                    .named_windows
2868                    .get(&ref_name.value)
2869                    .ok_or_else(|| {
2870                        polars_err!(
2871                            SQLInterface:
2872                            "named window '{}' references undefined window '{}'",
2873                            name.value, ref_name.value
2874                        )
2875                    })?
2876                    .clone(),
2877                NamedWindowExpr::WindowSpec(spec) => self.resolve_window_spec(spec)?,
2878            };
2879            self.named_windows.insert(name.value.clone(), spec);
2880        }
2881        Ok(())
2882    }
2883
2884    /// The window of an `OVER` clause, with any named window filled in.
2885    pub(crate) fn resolve_window(&self, window: &WindowType) -> PolarsResult<WindowSpec> {
2886        match window {
2887            WindowType::NamedWindow(name) => self.named_window(name),
2888            WindowType::WindowSpec(spec) => self.resolve_window_spec(spec),
2889        }
2890    }
2891
2892    fn named_window(&self, name: &Ident) -> PolarsResult<WindowSpec> {
2893        self.named_windows
2894            .get(&name.value)
2895            .cloned()
2896            .ok_or_else(|| polars_err!(SQLInterface: "named window '{}' was not found", name.value))
2897    }

2899    /// `(w ORDER BY x)` takes the PARTITION BY of `w`, and its ORDER BY if it has one.
2900    /// As in PostgreSQL, it may not replace either of them, and `w` may not have a frame.
2901    fn resolve_window_spec(&self, spec: &WindowSpec) -> PolarsResult<WindowSpec> {
2902        let Some(base_name) = &spec.window_name else {
2903            return Ok(spec.clone());
2904        };
2905        let base = self.named_window(base_name)?;
2906        polars_ensure!(
2907            spec.partition_by.is_empty(),
2908            SQLSyntax: "cannot override PARTITION BY of window '{}'", base_name.value
2909        );
2910        polars_ensure!(
2911            spec.order_by.is_empty() || base.order_by.is_empty(),
2912            SQLSyntax: "cannot override ORDER BY of window '{}'", base_name.value
2913        );
2914        polars_ensure!(
2915            base.window_frame.is_none(),
2916            SQLSyntax: "cannot copy window '{}' because it has a frame clause", base_name.value
2917        );
2918        Ok(WindowSpec {
2919            window_name: None,
2920            partition_by: base.partition_by,
2921            order_by: if spec.order_by.is_empty() {
2922                base.order_by
2923            } else {
2924                spec.order_by.clone()
2925            },
2926            window_frame: spec.window_frame.clone(),
2927        })
2928    }

2930    /// execute the 'FROM' part of the query
2931    pub(crate) fn execute_from_statement(
2932        &mut self,
2933        tbl_expr: &TableWithJoins,
2934    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2935        // Joins narrow the scope for their conditions; the caller's scope is restored after.
2936        let scope = self.active_relations.clone();
2937        let using_cols = std::mem::take(&mut self.join_using_cols);
2938        let lf = self.execute_joins(tbl_expr);
2939        self.active_relations = scope;
2940        self.join_using_cols = using_cols;
2941        lf
2942    }
2943
2944    fn execute_joins(&mut self, tbl_expr: &TableWithJoins) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
2945        let (l_name, mut lf) = self.get_table(&tbl_expr.relation)?;
2946        let relation_keys = |names: Vec<RelationName>| -> Vec<String> {
2947            names.iter().map(RelationName::key).collect()
2948        };
2949        // The factors whose columns the joins so far return.
2950        let mut kept = vec![&tbl_expr.relation];
2951        if !tbl_expr.joins.is_empty() {
2952            for join in &tbl_expr.joins {
2953                // A join condition only sees the relations joined so far.
2954                self.active_relations = factor_relations(
2955                    kept.iter().copied().chain(std::iter::once(&join.relation)),
2956                    &self.catalog_spellings,
2957                );
2958                let left_relations = relation_keys(factor_relations(
2959                    kept.iter().copied(),
2960                    &self.catalog_spellings,
2961                ));
2962                let right_relations = relation_keys(factor_relations(
2963                    std::iter::once(&join.relation),
2964                    &self.catalog_spellings,
2965                ));
2966                let (keep_left, keep_right) = join_keeps_inputs(&join.join_operator);
2967                if !keep_left {
2968                    kept.clear();
2969                    // The columns of the left relations are gone, so are their aliases.
2970                    for relation in &left_relations {
2971                        self.joined_aliases.remove(relation);
2972                    }
2973                }
2974                if keep_right {
2975                    kept.push(&join.relation);
2976                }
2977                // Handle "CROSS JOIN UNNEST(col)" as a lateral join op
2978                if let (
2979                    JoinOperator::CrossJoin(JoinConstraint::None),
2980                    TableFactor::UNNEST {
2981                        alias,
2982                        array_exprs,
2983                        with_offset,
2984                        ..
2985                    },
2986                ) = (&join.join_operator, &join.relation)
2987                {
2988                    if array_exprs.iter().any(|e| !matches!(e, SQLExpr::Array(_))) {
2989                        lf = self.process_unnest_lateral(lf, alias, array_exprs, *with_offset)?;
2990                        continue;
2991                    }
2992                }
2993
2994                let mut join_operator = Cow::Borrowed(&join.join_operator);
2995                let mut lateral_keys = None;
2996                let (r_name, mut rf) = match self.get_table(&join.relation) {
2997                    Ok(table) => table,
2998                    // A derived table that reads the relations joined before it.
2999                    Err(err) => match self.lateral_join(&join.relation, &join.join_operator, &lf) {
3000                        Some(lateral) => {
3001                            lf = lateral.left;
3002                            join_operator = Cow::Owned(lateral.join_operator);
3003                            lateral_keys = Some(lateral.keys);
3004                            (lateral.name, lateral.right)
3005                        },
3006                        None => return Err(err),
3007                    },
3008                };
3009                if r_name.is_empty() {
3010                    // Require non-empty to avoid duplicate column errors from nested self-joins.
3011                    polars_bail!(
3012                        SQLInterface:
3013                        "cannot JOIN on unnamed relation; please provide an alias"
3014                    )
3015                }
3016                let left_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3017                let right_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut rf)?;
3018
3019                lf = match join_operator.as_ref() {
3020                    op @ (JoinOperator::Join(constraint)  // note: bare "join" is inner
3021                    | JoinOperator::FullOuter(constraint)
3022                    | JoinOperator::Left(constraint)
3023                    | JoinOperator::LeftOuter(constraint)
3024                    | JoinOperator::Right(constraint)
3025                    | JoinOperator::RightOuter(constraint)
3026                    | JoinOperator::Inner(constraint)
3027                    | JoinOperator::Anti(constraint)
3028                    | JoinOperator::Semi(constraint)
3029                    | JoinOperator::LeftAnti(constraint)
3030                    | JoinOperator::LeftSemi(constraint)
3031                    | JoinOperator::RightAnti(constraint)
3032                    | JoinOperator::RightSemi(constraint)) => {
3033                        let keep_right = matches!(
3034                            op,
3035                            JoinOperator::RightAnti(_) | JoinOperator::RightSemi(_)
3036                        );
3037                        self.process_join(
3038                            &TableInfo {
3039                                frame: lf,
3040                                name: (&l_name).into(),
3041                                schema: left_schema.clone(),
3042                                relations: left_relations,
3043                            },
3044                            &TableInfo {
3045                                frame: rf,
3046                                name: (&r_name).into(),
3047                                schema: right_schema.clone(),
3048                                relations: right_relations,
3049                            },
3050                            constraint,
3051                            match op {
3052                                JoinOperator::Join(_) | JoinOperator::Inner(_) => JoinType::Inner,
3053                                JoinOperator::Left(_) | JoinOperator::LeftOuter(_) => {
3054                                    JoinType::Left
3055                                },
3056                                JoinOperator::Right(_) | JoinOperator::RightOuter(_) => {
3057                                    JoinType::Right
3058                                },
3059                                JoinOperator::FullOuter(_) => JoinType::Full,
3060                                #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
3061                                JoinOperator::Anti(_)
3062                                | JoinOperator::LeftAnti(_)
3063                                | JoinOperator::RightAnti(_) => JoinType::Anti,
3064                                #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
3065                                JoinOperator::Semi(_)
3066                                | JoinOperator::LeftSemi(_)
3067                                | JoinOperator::RightSemi(_) => JoinType::Semi,
3068                                join_type => polars_bail!(
3069                                    SQLInterface:
3070                                    "join type '{:?}' not currently supported",
3071                                    join_type
3072                                ),
3073                            },
3074                            keep_right,
3075                        )?
3076                    },
3077                    #[cfg(feature = "asof_join")]
3078                    JoinOperator::AsOf {
3079                        match_condition,
3080                        constraint,
3081                    } => self.process_asof_join(
3082                        &TableInfo {
3083                            frame: lf,
3084                            name: (&l_name).into(),
3085                            schema: left_schema.clone(),
3086                            relations: left_relations,
3087                        },
3088                        &TableInfo {
3089                            frame: rf,
3090                            name: (&r_name).into(),
3091                            schema: right_schema.clone(),
3092                            relations: right_relations,
3093                        },
3094                        match_condition,
3095                        constraint,
3096                    )?,
3097                    JoinOperator::CrossJoin(JoinConstraint::None) => {
3098                        lf.cross_join(rf, Some(format_pl_smallstr!(":{}", r_name)))
3099                    },
3100                    JoinOperator::CrossJoin(constraint) => {
3101                        polars_bail!(
3102                            SQLInterface:
3103                            "CROSS JOIN does not support {:?} constraint; consider INNER JOIN instead",
3104                            constraint
3105                        )
3106                    },
3107                    join_type => {
3108                        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "join type '{:?}' not currently supported", join_type)
3109                    },
3110                };
3111                if let Some(keys) = lateral_keys {
3112                    lf = lf.drop(Selector::ByName {
3113                        names: keys.into(),
3114                        strict: false,
3115                    });
3116                }
3117
3118                let joined_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3119                self.record_joined_aliases(
3120                    &r_name,
3121                    &[],
3122                    &left_schema,
3123                    &right_schema,
3124                    &joined_schema,
3125                )?;
3126                if let Some(cols) = get_using_cols(&join.join_operator) {
3127                    self.join_using_cols
3128                        .extend(cols.map(|c| (r_name.clone(), c)));
3129                }
3130            }
3131        };
3132        Ok(lf)
3133    }

3135    /// Check that the SELECT statement only contains supported clauses.
3136    fn validate_select(&self, select_stmt: &Select) -> PolarsResult<()> {
3137        // Destructure "Select" exhaustively; that way if/when new fields are added in
3138        // future sqlparser versions, we'll get a compilation error and can handle them
3139        let Select {
3140            // Supported clauses
3141            distinct: _,
3142            from: _,
3143            group_by: _,
3144            having: _,
3145            named_window: _,
3146            projection: _,
3147            qualify: _,
3148            selection: _,
3149
3150            // Metadata/token fields (can ignore)
3151            flavor: _,
3152            select_token: _,
3153            top_before_distinct: _,
3154            window_before_qualify: _,
3155
3156            // Unsupported clauses
3157            ref cluster_by,
3158            ref connect_by,
3159            ref distribute_by,
3160            ref exclude,
3161            ref into,
3162            ref lateral_views,
3163            ref optimizer_hints,
3164            ref prewhere,
3165            ref select_modifiers,
3166            ref sort_by,
3167            ref top,
3168            ref value_table_mode,
3169        } = *select_stmt;
3170
3171        // Raise specific error messages for unsupported attributes
3172        polars_ensure!(cluster_by.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`CLUSTER BY` clause is not supported");
3173        polars_ensure!(connect_by.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`CONNECT BY` clause is not supported");
3174        polars_ensure!(distribute_by.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`DISTRIBUTE BY` clause is not supported");
3175        polars_ensure!(exclude.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`EXCLUDE` clause is not supported");
3176        polars_ensure!(into.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`SELECT INTO` clause is not supported");
3177        polars_ensure!(lateral_views.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`LATERAL VIEW` clause is not supported");
3178        polars_ensure!(optimizer_hints.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "optimizer hints are not supported");
3179        polars_ensure!(prewhere.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`PREWHERE` clause is not supported");
3180        polars_ensure!(select_modifiers.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`SELECT` modifiers are not supported");
3181        polars_ensure!(sort_by.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`SORT BY` clause is not supported; use `ORDER BY` instead");
3182        polars_ensure!(top.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`TOP` clause is not supported; use `LIMIT` instead");
3183        polars_ensure!(value_table_mode.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`SELECT AS VALUE/STRUCT` is not supported");
3184
3185        Ok(())
3186    }
3187
3188    /// Raise specific errors for any unsupported clauses on a plain table relation.
3189    fn validate_table_factor(&self, factor: &TableFactor) -> PolarsResult<()> {
3190        // Destructure exhaustively; that way if/when new fields are added in future
3191        // sqlparser versions, we'll get a compilation error and can handle them
3192        let TableFactor::Table {
3193            // Supported/handled in `get_table`
3194            name: _,
3195            alias: _,
3196            args: _,
3197
3198            // Unsupported dialect-specific modifiers
3199            ref index_hints,
3200            ref json_path,
3201            ref partitions,
3202            ref sample,
3203            ref version,
3204            ref with_hints,
3205            with_ordinality,
3206        } = *factor
3207        else {
3208            return Ok(());
3209        };
3210
3211        polars_ensure!(!with_ordinality, SQLInterface: "`WITH ORDINALITY` is not supported");
3212        polars_ensure!(index_hints.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "table index hints are not supported");
3213        polars_ensure!(json_path.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table JSON path access is not supported");
3214        polars_ensure!(partitions.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "table `PARTITION` selection is not supported");
3215        polars_ensure!(sample.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `SAMPLE` clause is not supported");
3216        polars_ensure!(version.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table version (time-travel) qualifiers are not supported");
3217        polars_ensure!(with_hints.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "table `WITH (...)` hints are not supported");
3218
3219        Ok(())
3220    }

3222    /// Check that a CREATE TABLE statement only carries supported clauses. A catalog table also
3223    /// takes `LOCATION` and `WITH (...)`, which `create_table_options` checks.
3224    fn validate_create_table(
3225        &self,
3226        create_table: &CreateTable,
3227        for_catalog: bool,
3228    ) -> PolarsResult<()> {
3229        // Destructure exhaustively; that way if/when new fields are added in future
