3230        // sqlparser versions, we'll get a compilation error and can handle them
3231        let CreateTable {
3232            // Supported/handled in `execute_create_table`
3233            name: _,
3234            columns: _,
3235            query: _,
3236            like: _,
3237            ref if_not_exists,
3238            ref or_replace,
3239            ref temporary,
3240
3241            // Unsupported `CREATE [...] TABLE` modifiers
3242            ref copy_grants,
3243            ref unlogged,
3244            ref multiset,
3245            ref fallback,
3246            ref dynamic,
3247            ref external,
3248            ref global,
3249            ref iceberg,
3250            ref require_user,
3251            ref snapshot,
3252            ref strict,
3253            ref transient,
3254            ref volatile,
3255            ref without_rowid,
3256
3257            // Unsupported table definition / storage clauses
3258            ref backup,
3259            ref base_location,
3260            ref catalog,
3261            ref catalog_sync,
3262            ref change_tracking,
3263            ref clone,
3264            ref cluster_by,
3265            ref clustered_by,
3266            ref comment,
3267            ref constraints,
3268            ref data_retention_time_in_days,
3269            ref default_ddl_collation,
3270            ref distkey,
3271            ref diststyle,
3272            ref enable_schema_evolution,
3273            ref external_volume,
3274            ref file_format,
3275            ref for_values,
3276            ref hive_distribution,
3277            ref hive_formats,
3278            ref inherits,
3279            ref initialize,
3280            ref location,
3281            ref max_data_extension_time_in_days,
3282            ref on_cluster,
3283            ref on_commit,
3284            ref order_by,
3285            ref partition_by,
3286            ref partition_of,
3287            ref primary_key,
3288            ref refresh_mode,
3289            ref sortkey,
3290            ref storage_serialization_policy,
3291            ref table_options,
3292            ref target_lag,
3293            ref version,
3294            ref warehouse,
3295            ref with_aggregation_policy,
3296            ref with_row_access_policy,
3297            ref with_storage_lifecycle_policy,
3298            ref with_tags,
3299            ref with_connection,
3300            ref with_data,
3301        } = *create_table;
3302
3303        polars_ensure!(!copy_grants, SQLInterface: "`COPY GRANTS` is not supported");
3304        polars_ensure!(!dynamic, SQLInterface: "`CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE` is not supported");
3305        polars_ensure!(!external, SQLInterface: "`CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` is not supported");
3306        polars_ensure!(!iceberg, SQLInterface: "`CREATE ICEBERG TABLE` is not supported");
3307        polars_ensure!(!*or_replace || *temporary || !for_catalog, SQLInterface: "`CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` is not supported for catalog tables");
3308        polars_ensure!(!*or_replace || *temporary, SQLInterface: "`CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` is not supported");
3309        polars_ensure!(!(*or_replace && *if_not_exists), SQLInterface: "`OR REPLACE` and `IF NOT EXISTS` cannot be combined");
3310        polars_ensure!(!require_user, SQLInterface: "`REQUIRE USER` is not supported");
3311        polars_ensure!(!snapshot, SQLInterface: "`CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE` is not supported");
3312        polars_ensure!(!strict, SQLInterface: "`STRICT` tables are not supported");
3313        polars_ensure!(!transient, SQLInterface: "`CREATE TRANSIENT TABLE` is not supported");
3314        polars_ensure!(!volatile, SQLInterface: "`CREATE VOLATILE TABLE` is not supported");
3315        polars_ensure!(!without_rowid, SQLInterface: "`WITHOUT ROWID` is not supported");
3316        polars_ensure!(!unlogged, SQLInterface: "`CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE` is not supported");
3317        polars_ensure!(multiset.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`MULTISET`/`SET` tables are not supported");
3318        polars_ensure!(fallback.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`FALLBACK` is not supported");
3319        polars_ensure!(backup.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`BACKUP` is not supported");
3320        polars_ensure!(base_location.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`BASE_LOCATION` is not supported");
3321        polars_ensure!(catalog.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CATALOG` is not supported");
3322        polars_ensure!(catalog_sync.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CATALOG_SYNC` is not supported");
3323        polars_ensure!(change_tracking.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CHANGE_TRACKING` is not supported");
3324        polars_ensure!(clone.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CREATE TABLE ... CLONE` is not supported");
3325        polars_ensure!(cluster_by.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `CLUSTER BY` clauses are not supported");
3326        polars_ensure!(clustered_by.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `CLUSTERED BY` clauses are not supported");
3327        polars_ensure!(comment.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `COMMENT` clauses are not supported");
3328        polars_ensure!(constraints.is_empty() || !for_catalog, SQLInterface: "only NOT NULL constraints are supported for catalog tables");
3329        polars_ensure!(constraints.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "table constraints are not supported");
3330        polars_ensure!(data_retention_time_in_days.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS` is not supported");
3331        polars_ensure!(default_ddl_collation.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DEFAULT_DDL_COLLATION` is not supported");
3332        polars_ensure!(distkey.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DISTKEY` is not supported");
3333        polars_ensure!(diststyle.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DISTSTYLE` is not supported");
3334        polars_ensure!(enable_schema_evolution.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`ENABLE_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION` is not supported");
3335        polars_ensure!(external_volume.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`EXTERNAL_VOLUME` is not supported");
3336        polars_ensure!(file_format.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `STORED AS` clauses are not supported");
3337        polars_ensure!(for_values.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`FOR VALUES` clauses are not supported");
3338        polars_ensure!(global.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CREATE GLOBAL/LOCAL TABLE` is not supported");
3339        // sqlparser keeps `LOCATION` in the Hive format.
3340        let hive_format = |f: &HiveFormat| match for_catalog {
3341            true => HiveFormat {
3342                location: None,
3343                ..f.clone()
3344            },
3345            false => f.clone(),
3346        };
3347        polars_ensure!(hive_formats.as_ref().is_none_or(|f| hive_format(f) == HiveFormat::default()), SQLInterface: "Hive table format clauses are not supported");
3348        polars_ensure!(inherits.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `INHERITS` clauses are not supported");
3349        polars_ensure!(initialize.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`INITIALIZE` is not supported");
3350        polars_ensure!(location.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `LOCATION` clauses are not supported");
3351        let partitioned = matches!(hive_distribution, HiveDistributionStyle::PARTITIONED { .. });
3352        polars_ensure!(matches!(hive_distribution, HiveDistributionStyle::NONE) || partitioned, SQLInterface: "Hive table distribution clauses are not supported");
3353        polars_ensure!(!partitioned || for_catalog, SQLInterface: "`PARTITIONED BY` is supported only for catalog tables");
3354        polars_ensure!(for_catalog || matches!(table_options, CreateTableOptions::None), SQLInterface: "table `WITH`/`OPTIONS` clauses are not supported");
3355        polars_ensure!(max_data_extension_time_in_days.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`MAX_DATA_EXTENSION_TIME_IN_DAYS` is not supported");
3356        polars_ensure!(on_cluster.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`ON CLUSTER` clauses are not supported");
3357        polars_ensure!(on_commit.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`ON COMMIT` clauses are not supported");
3358        polars_ensure!(order_by.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `ORDER BY` clauses are not supported");
3359        polars_ensure!(partition_by.is_none() || for_catalog, SQLInterface: "`PARTITION BY` is supported only for catalog tables");
3360        polars_ensure!(partition_of.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`PARTITION OF` clauses are not supported");
3361        polars_ensure!(primary_key.is_none(), SQLInterface: "inline `PRIMARY KEY` clauses are not supported");
3362        polars_ensure!(refresh_mode.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`REFRESH_MODE` is not supported");
3363        polars_ensure!(sortkey.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`SORTKEY` is not supported");
3364        polars_ensure!(storage_serialization_policy.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`STORAGE_SERIALIZATION_POLICY` is not supported");
3365        polars_ensure!(target_lag.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`TARGET_LAG` is not supported");
3366        polars_ensure!(version.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table version (time-travel) qualifiers are not supported");
3367        polars_ensure!(warehouse.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WAREHOUSE` is not supported");
3368        polars_ensure!(with_aggregation_policy.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WITH AGGREGATION POLICY` is not supported");
3369        polars_ensure!(with_row_access_policy.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WITH ROW ACCESS POLICY` is not supported");
3370        polars_ensure!(with_storage_lifecycle_policy.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WITH STORAGE LIFECYCLE POLICY` is not supported");
3371        polars_ensure!(with_tags.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WITH TAG` is not supported");
3372        polars_ensure!(with_connection.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WITH CONNECTION` is not supported");
3373        polars_ensure!(with_data.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`WITH [NO] DATA` is not supported");
3374
3375        Ok(())
3376    }
3377
3378    /// Check that the QUERY only contains supported clauses.
3379    fn validate_query(&self, query: &Query) -> PolarsResult<()> {
3380        // As with "Select" validation (above) destructure "Query" exhaustively
3381        let Query {
3382            // Supported clauses
3383            with: _,
3384            body: _,
3385            order_by: _,
3386            limit_clause: _,
3387            fetch,
3388
3389            // Unsupported clauses
3390            for_clause,
3391            format_clause,
3392            locks,
3393            pipe_operators,
3394            settings,
3395        } = query;
3396
3397        // Raise specific error messages for unsupported attributes
3398        polars_ensure!(for_clause.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`FOR` clause is not supported");
3399        polars_ensure!(format_clause.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`FORMAT` clause is not supported");
3400        polars_ensure!(locks.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "`FOR UPDATE/SHARE` locking clause is not supported");
3401        polars_ensure!(pipe_operators.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "pipe operators are not supported");
3402        polars_ensure!(settings.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`SETTINGS` clause is not supported");
3403
3404        // Validate FETCH clause options (if present)
3405        if let Some(Fetch {
3406            quantity: _, // supported
3407            percent,
3408            with_ties,
3409        }) = fetch
3410        {
3411            polars_ensure!(!percent, SQLInterface: "`FETCH` with `PERCENT` is not supported");
3412            polars_ensure!(!with_ties, SQLInterface: "`FETCH` with `WITH TIES` is not supported");
3413        }
3414        Ok(())
3415    }
3416
3417    /// Register a `GROUPING()` call of the current query block, returning the
3418    /// placeholder column that stands for its value. Repeating a call yields the
3419    /// same placeholder, so every clause of the block refers to one column.
3420    pub(crate) fn register_grouping_call(&mut self, args: Vec<SQLExpr>) -> PlSmallStr {
3421        let calls = &mut self.group_scope.grouping_calls;
3422        match calls.iter().find(|c| c.args == args) {
3423            Some(call) => call.placeholder.clone(),
3424            None => {
3425                let placeholder = new_placeholder();
3426                calls.push(GroupingCall {
3427                    args,
3428                    placeholder: placeholder.clone(),
3429                });
3430                placeholder
3431            },
3432        }
3433    }
3434
3435    /// `schema` with the placeholder columns that the parsed expressions of the block can
3436    /// read: the partition of whole-frame windows, the `GROUPING()` values and the SELECT
3437    /// aliases of the clause being parsed.
3438    pub(crate) fn with_placeholder_columns(&self, schema: &Schema) -> Schema {
3439        let mut schema = schema.clone();
3440        for (name, dtype) in self.group_scope.alias_types.iter() {
3441            if !schema.contains(name) {
3442                schema.with_column(name.clone(), dtype.clone());
3443            }
3444        }
3445        if let Some(partition) = &self.group_scope.whole_frame_partition {
3446            schema.with_column(partition.clone(), DataType::Int32);
3447        }
3448        for call in &self.group_scope.grouping_calls {
3449            schema.with_column(call.placeholder.clone(), DataType::Int64);
3450        }
3451        schema
3452    }
3453
3454    /// The type of `expr` over `schema`, or else over `schema` with the placeholder columns
3455    /// of the block; `None` if it cannot be resolved.
3456    pub(crate) fn expr_dtype(&self, expr: &Expr, schema: Option<&Schema>) -> Option<DataType> {
3457        resolve_expr_dtype(expr, schema).or_else(|| {
3458            let schema = self.with_placeholder_columns(schema?);
3459            resolve_expr_dtype(expr, Some(&schema))
3460        })
3461    }
3462
3463    /// The partition column of the current block's whole-frame windows.
3464    pub(crate) fn whole_frame_partition(&mut self) -> PlSmallStr {
3465        self.group_scope
3466            .whole_frame_partition
3467            .get_or_insert_with(|| {
3468                format_pl_smallstr!("__POLARS_WHOLE_FRAME_{}", unique_column_name())
3469            })
3470            .clone()
3471    }
3472
3473    /// Lower the whole-frame windows of a block without group keys back to their
3474    /// bare expression.
3475    fn resolve_whole_frame_windows(&self, expr: Expr) -> Expr {
3476        self.map_whole_frame_windows(expr, |function| function.clone())
3477    }
3478
3479    /// Replace each whole-frame window in `expr` by `f` of its function.
3480    fn map_whole_frame_windows(&self, expr: Expr, f: impl Fn(&Expr) -> Expr) -> Expr {
3481        let Some(partition) = &self.group_scope.whole_frame_partition else {
3482            return expr;
3483        };
3484        expr.map_expr(|e| match &e {
3485            Expr::Over {
3486                function,
3487                partition_by,
3488                order_by: None,
3489                ..
3490            } if matches!(partition_by.as_slice(), [Expr::Column(name)] if name == partition) => {
3491                f(function)
3492            },
3493            _ => e,
3494        })
3495    }
3496
3497    /// Run `f` with the aggregate calls it parses marked (see `GroupScope::mark_aggregates`).
3498    pub(crate) fn marking_aggregates<T>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> T) -> T {
3499        let mark_aggregates = std::mem::replace(&mut self.group_scope.mark_aggregates, true);
3500        let result = f(self);
3501        self.group_scope.mark_aggregates = mark_aggregates;
3502        result
3503    }
3504
3505    fn contains_grouping_placeholder(&self, expr: &Expr) -> bool {
3506        contains_grouping_placeholder(
3507            expr,
3508            self.group_scope
3509                .grouping_calls
3510                .iter()
3511                .map(|c| &c.placeholder),
3512        )
3513    }
3514
3515    /// Execute the 'SELECT' part of the query.
3516    fn execute_select(&mut self, select_stmt: &Select, query: &Query) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
3517        let has_group_by = match &select_stmt.group_by {
3518            GroupByExpr::Expressions(exprs, _) => !exprs.is_empty(),
3519            GroupByExpr::All(_) => true,
3520        };
3521        let scope = GroupScope {
3522            mark_whole_frame_windows: has_group_by,
3523            ..Default::default()
3524        };
3525        let outer_scope = std::mem::replace(&mut self.group_scope, scope);
3526        let hoisted = self.hoist_outer_select_items(select_stmt);
3527        let select_stmt = hoisted.as_ref().unwrap_or(select_stmt);
3528        let result = check_random_items(select_stmt, query)
3529            .and_then(|_| self.execute_select_block(select_stmt, query));
3530        self.group_scope = outer_scope;
3531        result
3532    }
3533
3534    fn execute_select_block(
3535        &mut self,
3536        select_stmt: &Select,
3537        query: &Query,
3538    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
3539        // Check that the statement doesn't contain unsupported SELECT clauses
3540        self.validate_select(select_stmt)?;
3541
3542        // Parse named windows first, as they may be referenced in the SELECT clause
3543        self.register_named_windows(&select_stmt.named_window)?;
3544
3545        // Get `FROM` table/data
3546        let mut implicit_join_filter: Option<SQLExpr> = None;
3547        let mut lf = if select_stmt.from.is_empty() {
3548            self.active_relations.clear();
3549            DataFrame::new(1, vec![])?.lazy()
3550        } else {
3551            let from = &select_stmt.from;
3552            let first = from.first().unwrap();
3553            // Set before the relations are resolved, so a join constraint
3554            // resolves against them.
3555            self.active_relations = declared_relations(from, &self.catalog_spellings);
3556            let mut lf = self.execute_from_statement(first)?;
3557            if from.len() > 1 {
3558                implicit_join_filter =
3559                    self.process_implicit_joins(&mut lf, from, &select_stmt.selection)?;
3560            }
3561            lf
3562        };
3563
3564        self.set_join_base(&select_stmt.from);
3565        let mut schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3566        self.check_select_column_refs(select_stmt, &schema)?;
3567
3568        // Apply `WHERE` constraint (using residual filter for implicit joins)
3569        let where_expr = if implicit_join_filter.is_some() {
3570            implicit_join_filter.as_ref()
3571        } else {
3572            select_stmt.selection.as_ref()
3573        };
3574
3575        // Shared by every pass over this frame: WHERE, the projection list and HAVING.
3576        let mut bindings = SubqueryBindings::new();
3577
3578        lf = self.filter_on_where(
3579            lf,
3580            &mut schema,
3581            where_expr,
3582            &mut bindings,
3583            Some(select_stmt),
3584        )?;
3585
3586        // HAVING is parsed further below but lowered here, against the pre-aggregation
3587        // frame.
3588        let mut lowered_projection: Option<Vec<SelectItem>> = None;
3589        let mut lowered_having: Option<Cow<'_, SQLExpr>> = None;
3590        {
3591            let mut changed = false;
3592            for (idx, item) in select_stmt.projection.iter().enumerate() {
3593                let (SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(e) | SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr: e, .. }) = item
3594                else {
3595                    continue;
3596                };
3597                let lowered;
3598                (lf, lowered) = self.lower_correlated_subqueries(
3599                    lf,
3600                    &schema,
3601                    e,
3602                    LowerScope::ScalarAndPredicates,
3603                    &mut bindings,
3604                    None,
3605                )?;
3606                if let Cow::Owned(lowered) = lowered {
3607                    changed = true;
3608                    let items =
3609                        lowered_projection.get_or_insert_with(|| select_stmt.projection.clone());
3610                    match &mut items[idx] {
3611                        SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(slot)
3612                        | SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr: slot, .. } => *slot = lowered,
3613                        _ => unreachable!("only expression items are lowered"),
3614                    }
3615                }
3616            }
3617            if let Some(having) = &select_stmt.having {
3618                let lowered;
3619                (lf, lowered) = self.lower_correlated_subqueries(
3620                    lf,
3621                    &schema,
3622                    having,
3623                    LowerScope::ScalarAndPredicates,
3624                    &mut bindings,
3625                    None,
3626                )?;
3627                changed |= matches!(lowered, Cow::Owned(_));
3628                lowered_having = Some(lowered);
3629            }
3630            if changed {
3631                schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3632            }
3633        }
3634        let projection: &[SelectItem] = lowered_projection
3635            .as_deref()
3636            .unwrap_or(&select_stmt.projection);
3637
3638        if let Some(qualify) = &select_stmt.qualify {
3639            check_qualify(qualify, &select_stmt.projection)?;
3640        }
3641
3642        let mark_whole_frame_windows =
3643            std::mem::replace(&mut self.group_scope.mark_whole_frame_windows, true);
3644        let mut projections_with_flags = self.marking_aggregates(|ctx| {
3645            ctx.column_projections(projection, select_stmt.flavor, &schema)
3646        })?;
3647        self.group_scope.mark_whole_frame_windows = mark_whole_frame_windows;
3648        let mut subquery_names;
3649        (lf, subquery_names) = self.process_subqueries(
3650            lf,
3651            projections_with_flags.iter_mut().map(|(e, _)| e).collect(),
3652            SubqueryShape::Scalar,
3653        )?;
3654        for (expr, _) in projections_with_flags.iter_mut() {
3655            *expr = broadcast_subqueries_in_inputs(
3656                expr.clone(),
3657                &subquery_names,
3658                &self.group_scope.subqueries_read_per_row,
3659            );
3660        }
3661        schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3662
3663        // Placeholder names are generated per execution, so an unaliased projection
3664        // named after one gets the name given to any other unnamed scalar expression.
3665        // Matching on the output name rather than the expression shape also catches
3666        // projections that merely derive their name from a placeholder.
3667        if !subquery_names.is_empty() {
3668            for (expr, is_explicit_alias) in projections_with_flags.iter_mut() {
3669                if *is_explicit_alias {
3670                    continue;
3671                }
3672                let is_placeholder_name = expr
3673                    .to_field(&schema)
3674                    .is_ok_and(|f| subquery_names.contains(&f.name));
3675                if is_placeholder_name {
3676                    *expr = expr.clone().alias(PlSmallStr::from_static("literal"));
3677                }
3678            }
3679        }
3680
3681        // QUALIFY filters on windows over the rows the SELECT list reads, so it is computed
3682        // with the SELECT list, as a hidden column. It can name SELECT aliases, which read the
3683        // subqueries of the SELECT list resolved above.
3684        let qualify_column = format_pl_smallstr!("__POLARS_QUALIFY_{}", unique_column_name());
3685        let mut qualify = match &select_stmt.qualify {
3686            Some(qualify) => {
3687                let projections: Vec<Expr> = projections_with_flags
3688                    .iter()
3689                    .map(|(e, _)| e.clone())
3690                    .collect();
3691                let output_names = OutputNames::new(
3692                    &projections,
3693                    &schema,
3694                    &self.with_placeholder_columns(&schema),
3695                );
3696                let output_schema = output_names.extend_schema(&schema);
3697                let mark_whole_frame_windows =
3698                    std::mem::replace(&mut self.group_scope.mark_whole_frame_windows, true);
3699                let parsed = self
3700                    .marking_aggregates(|ctx| parse_sql_expr(qualify, ctx, Some(&output_schema)));
3701                self.group_scope.mark_whole_frame_windows = mark_whole_frame_windows;
3702                let mut qualify = output_names.resolve(parsed?);
3703                if qualify.clone().meta().has_multiple_outputs() {
3704                    qualify = all_horizontal([qualify])?;
3705                }
3706                let qualify_subquery_names;
3707                (lf, qualify_subquery_names) =
3708                    self.process_subqueries(lf, vec![&mut qualify], SubqueryShape::Scalar)?;
3709                if !qualify_subquery_names.is_empty() {
3710                    subquery_names.extend(qualify_subquery_names);
3711                    schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3712                }
3713                let qualify = broadcast_subqueries_in_inputs(
3714                    qualify,
3715                    &subquery_names,
3716                    &self.group_scope.subqueries_read_per_row,
3717                );
3718                Some(qualify.alias(qualify_column.clone()))
3719            },
3720            None => None,
3721        };
3722
3723        let (mut projections, mut explicit_aliases): (Vec<Expr>, Vec<bool>) =
3724            projections_with_flags.into_iter().unzip();
3725
3726        // Apply `UNNEST` expressions
3727        let mut explode_names = Vec::new();
3728        let mut explode_exprs = Vec::new();
3729        let mut explode_lookup = PlHashMap::new();
3730
3731        for expr in &projections {
3732            for e in expr {
3733                if let Expr::Explode { input, .. } = e {
3734                    match input.as_ref() {
3735                        Expr::Column(name) => explode_names.push(name.clone()),
3736                        other_expr => {
3737                            // Note: skip aggregate expressions; those are handled in the GROUP BY phase
3738                            if !has_expr(other_expr, |e| matches!(e, Expr::Agg(_) | Expr::Len)) {
3739                                let temp_name =
3740                                    format_pl_smallstr!("__POLARS_UNNEST_{}", explode_exprs.len());
3741                                explode_exprs.push(other_expr.clone().alias(temp_name.as_str()));
3742                                explode_lookup.insert(other_expr.clone(), temp_name.clone());
3743                                explode_names.push(temp_name);
3744                            }
3745                        },
3746                    }
3747                }
3748            }
3749        }
3750        if !explode_names.is_empty() {
3751            if !explode_exprs.is_empty() {
3752                lf = lf.with_columns(explode_exprs);
3753            }
3754            lf = lf.explode(
3755                Selector::ByName {
3756                    names: Arc::from(explode_names),
3757                    strict: true,
3758                },
3759                ExplodeOptions {
3760                    empty_as_null: true,
3761                    keep_nulls: true,
3762                },
3763            );
3764            projections = projections
3765                .into_iter()
3766                .map(|p| {
3767                    // Update "projections" with column refs to the now-exploded expressions
3768                    p.map_expr(|e| match e {
3769                        Expr::Explode { input, .. } => explode_lookup
3770                            .get(input.as_ref())
3771                            .map(|name| Expr::Column(name.clone()))
3772                            .unwrap_or_else(|| input.as_ref().clone()),
3773                        _ => e,
3774                    })
3775                })
3776                .collect();
3777
3778            schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
3779        }
3780
3781        // Check for "GROUP BY ..." (after determining projections)
3782        let mut group_by_keys: Vec<Expr> = Vec::new();
3783        let mut grouping_sets: Option<Vec<Vec<usize>>> = None;
3784        match &select_stmt.group_by {
3785            // Standard "GROUP BY x, y, z" syntax (also recognising ordinal values)
3786            GroupByExpr::Expressions(group_by_exprs, modifiers) => {
3787                if !modifiers.is_empty() {
3788                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "GROUP BY does not support CUBE, ROLLUP, or TOTALS modifiers")
3789                }
3790                let expanded = expand_grouping_sets(group_by_exprs)?;
3791                let key_exprs: &[SQLExpr] = expanded
3792                    .as_ref()
3793                    .map_or(group_by_exprs, |expanded| &expanded.keys);
3794                // Translate the group expressions, resolving ordinal values and SELECT aliases
3795                group_by_keys = key_exprs
3796                    .iter()
3797                    .map(|e| self.resolve_group_by_key(e, &projections, &schema, true))
3798                    .collect::<PolarsResult<_>>()?;
3799                if let Some(expanded) = expanded {
3800                    let (keys, sets) = canonicalize_keys(group_by_keys, expanded.sets);
3801                    group_by_keys = keys;
3802                    grouping_sets = Some(sets);
3803                }
3804            },
3805            // "GROUP BY ALL" syntax; automatically adds expressions that do not contain
3806            // nested agg/window funcs to the group key (also ignores literals).
3807            GroupByExpr::All(modifiers) => {
3808                if !modifiers.is_empty() {
3809                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "GROUP BY does not support CUBE, ROLLUP, or TOTALS modifiers")
3810                }
3811                projections.iter().for_each(|expr| match expr {
3812                    // immediately match the most common cases (col|agg|len|lit, optionally aliased).
3813                    Expr::Agg(_) | Expr::Len | Expr::Literal(_) => (),
3814                    _ if self.contains_grouping_placeholder(expr) => (),
3815                    Expr::Column(_) => group_by_keys.push(expr.clone()),
3816                    Expr::Alias(e, _)
3817                        if matches!(&**e, Expr::Agg(_) | Expr::Len | Expr::Literal(_)) => {},
3818                    Expr::Alias(e, _) if matches!(&**e, Expr::Column(_)) => {
3819                        if let Expr::Column(name) = &**e {
3820                            group_by_keys.push(col(name.clone()));
3821                        }
3822                    },
3823                    _ => {
3824                        // If not quick-matched, add if no nested agg/window expressions
3825                        if !has_expr(expr, |e| {
3826                            is_marked_aggregate(e)
3827                                || matches!(e, Expr::Agg(_))
3828                                || matches!(e, Expr::Len)
3829                                || matches!(e, Expr::Over { .. })
3830                                || {
3831                                    #[cfg(feature = "dynamic_group_by")]
3832                                    {
3833                                        matches!(e, Expr::Rolling { .. })
3834                                    }
3835                                    #[cfg(not(feature = "dynamic_group_by"))]
3836                                    {
3837                                        false
3838                                    }
3839                                }
3840                        }) {
3841                            group_by_keys.push(expr.clone())
3842                        }
3843                    },
3844                });
3845            },
3846        };
3847        for e in &group_by_keys {
3848            reject_unresolved_subquery(e, "GROUP BY")?;
3849            polars_ensure!(
3850                !self.contains_grouping_placeholder(e),
3851                SQLSyntax: "GROUPING() is not allowed in the GROUP BY clause"
3852            );
3853        }
3854        if grouping_sets.is_none() {
3855            let mut seen: Vec<Expr> = Vec::with_capacity(group_by_keys.len());
3856            group_by_keys.retain(|key| {
3857                let stripped = strip_outer_alias(key);
3858                let is_new = !seen.contains(&stripped);
3859                if is_new {
3860                    seen.push(stripped);
3861                }
3862                is_new
3863            });
3864            // Literal keys do not split the groups. `GROUPING()` needs every key.
3865            let order_by_exprs = match &query.order_by {
3866                Some(OrderBy {
3867                    kind: OrderByKind::Expressions(exprs),
3868                    ..
3869                }) => exprs.iter().map(|ob| &ob.expr).collect(),
3870                _ => vec![],
3871            };
3872            let uses_grouping = !self.group_scope.grouping_calls.is_empty()
3873                || select_stmt
3874                    .having
3875                    .iter()
3876                    .chain(&select_stmt.qualify)
3877                    .chain(order_by_exprs)
3878                    .any(|e| !collect_grouping_calls(e).is_empty());
3879            if !uses_grouping {
3880                let is_literal = |key: &Expr| matches!(strip_outer_alias(key), Expr::Literal(_));
3881                if group_by_keys.iter().all(is_literal) {
3882                    group_by_keys.truncate(1);
3883                } else {
3884                    group_by_keys.retain(|key| !is_literal(key));
3885                }
3886            }
3887        }
3888
3889        let has_group_by = !group_by_keys.is_empty() || grouping_sets.is_some();
3890        if !has_group_by {
3891            polars_ensure!(
3892                self.group_scope.grouping_calls.is_empty(),
3893                SQLSyntax: "GROUPING() requires a GROUP BY clause"
3894            );
3895        }
3896        // Without GROUP BY, a block with aggregates or HAVING is one group, and its windows,
3897        // `RANDOM()` calls and subqueries outside its aggregates run on that one row.
3898        let all_projections = projections
3899            .iter()
3900            .chain(&qualify)
3901            .cloned()
3902            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
3903        lf = if !has_group_by
3904            && lowered_having.is_none()
3905            && !has_windows_over_aggregates(&all_projections)
3906            && !has_subquery_outside_aggregates(&all_projections, &subquery_names)
3907            && !(all_projections.iter().any(has_marked_aggregate)
3908                && all_projections.iter().any(has_random_outside_aggregates))
3909        {
3910            // `GROUP BY ALL` may infer no keys; nothing here runs in a group context.
3911            self.group_scope.mark_whole_frame_windows = false;
3912            projections = all_projections;
3913            explicit_aliases.extend(qualify.is_some().then_some(true));
3914            // Aggregates are marked only until the projections are resolved below.
3915            check_columns_in_aggregates(&projections, &subquery_names)?;
3916
3917            // Initialize containing InheritsContext to handle empty projection case.
3918            let mut projection_heights = ExprSqlProjectionHeightBehavior::InheritsContext;
3919            for p in &projections {
3920                // A window over the whole frame has one value per row, so for the output
3921                // height it counts like a literal.
3922                let height_expr = self.map_whole_frame_windows(p.clone(), |_| lit(1));
3923                projection_heights |= ExprSqlProjectionHeightBehavior::identify_from_expr(
3924                    &without_resolved_subqueries(&height_expr, &subquery_names),
3925                );
3926            }
3927            projections = projections
3928                .into_iter()
3929                .map(|e| strip_aggregate_marks(self.resolve_whole_frame_windows(e)))
3930                .collect();
3931
3932            // Disambiguate SELECT-list output-name collisions.
3933            projections = disambiguate_output_names(
3934                projections.into_iter().zip(explicit_aliases).collect(),
3935                &schema,
3936            )?;
3937
3938            let have_order_by = query.order_by.is_some();
3939
3940            // Note: if there is an 'order by' then we project everything (original cols
3941            // and new projections) and *then* select the final cols by name. If there's no
3942            // 'order by', clause then we can project the final column *expressions* directly.
3943            let mut final_cols = Vec::with_capacity(projections.len());
3944            let mut final_names = Vec::with_capacity(projections.len());
3945            for p in &projections {
3946                let name = p.to_field(schema.deref())?.name;
3947                final_cols.push(if have_order_by {
3948                    col(name.clone())
3949                } else {
3950                    p.clone()
3951                });
3952                final_names.push(col(name));
3953            }
3954
3955            // Without FROM the frame has one row, or none when WHERE removes it.
3956            let reads_frame = !select_stmt.from.is_empty() || select_stmt.selection.is_some();
3957            // Establish the final projection
3958            if have_order_by {
3959                if !reads_frame {
3960                    lf = lf.select(projections);
3961                } else if projection_heights
3962                    .contains(ExprSqlProjectionHeightBehavior::MaintainsColumn)
3963                    || projection_heights == ExprSqlProjectionHeightBehavior::InheritsContext
3964                {
3965                    // We can safely use `with_columns()` and avoid a join if:
3966                    // * There is already a projection that projects to the table height.
3967                    // * All projection heights inherit from context (e.g. all scalar literals that
3968                    //   are to be broadcasted to table height).
3969                    lf = lf.with_columns(projections)
3970                } else {
3971                    // We hit this branch if the output height is not guaranteed to match the table
3972                    // height. E.g.:
3973                    //
3974                    // * SELECT COUNT(*) FROM df ORDER BY sort_key;
3975                    //
3976                    // For these cases we truncate / extend the sorting columns with NULLs to match
3977                    // the output height. We do this by projecting independently and then joining
3978                    // back the original frame on the row index.
3979                    const NAME: PlSmallStr = PlSmallStr::from_static("__PL_INDEX");
3980                    // The row index pairs the two sides, so both must read one
3981                    // materialisation of the frame.
3982                    let cached = lf.cache();
3983                    lf = cached
3984                        .clone()
3985                        .select(projections)
3986                        .with_row_index(NAME, None)
3987                        .join(
3988                            cached.with_row_index(NAME, None),
3989                            [col(NAME)],
3990                            [col(NAME)],
3991                            JoinArgs {
3992                                how: JoinType::Left,
3993                                validation: Default::default(),
3994                                suffix: None,
3995                                slice: None,
3996                                nulls_equal: false,
3997                                coalesce: Default::default(),
3998                                maintain_order: MaintainOrderJoin::Left,
3999                                build_side: None,
4000                            },
4001                        )?;
4002                }
4003            }
4004            let n_selected = final_cols.len() - usize::from(qualify.is_some());
4005            lf = self.process_order_by(lf, &query.order_by, Some(&final_cols[..n_selected]))?;
4006
4007            // Note: If `have_order_by`, with_columns is already done above.
4008            if projection_heights == ExprSqlProjectionHeightBehavior::InheritsContext
4009                && !have_order_by
4010                && reads_frame
4011                && !final_cols.is_empty()
4012            {
4013                // All projections need to be broadcasted to table height, so evaluate in `with_columns()`
4014                lf = lf.with_columns(final_cols).select(final_names);
4015            } else {
4016                lf = lf.select(final_cols);
4017            }
4018            lf
4019        } else {
4020            // HAVING can read SELECT aliases.
4021            let having = lowered_having
4022                .as_deref()
4023                .map(|expr| {
4024                    let alias_types = OutputNames::new(
4025                        &projections,
4026                        &schema,
4027                        &self.with_placeholder_columns(&schema),
4028                    )
4029                    .extend_schema(&Schema::default());
4030                    let outer_alias_types =
4031                        std::mem::replace(&mut self.group_scope.alias_types, alias_types);
4032                    let having =
4033                        self.marking_aggregates(|ctx| parse_sql_expr(expr, ctx, Some(&schema)));
4034                    self.group_scope.alias_types = outer_alias_types;
4035                    having
4036                })
4037                .transpose()?;
4038            let grouping = self.bind_grouping_sets(
4039                &group_by_keys,
4040                grouping_sets,
4041                &projections,
4042                &schema,
4043                &query.order_by,
4044            )?;
4045            let (output_names, order_by);
4046            (lf, output_names, order_by) = self.process_group_by(
4047                lf,
4048                &group_by_keys,
4049                projections,
4050                &explicit_aliases,
4051                having,
4052                qualify.take().map(|e| (qualify_column.clone(), e)),
4053                &query.order_by,
4054                grouping.as_ref(),
4055                &subquery_names,
4056            )?;
4057            // The remaining clauses run on the aggregated frame.
4058            self.group_scope.mark_whole_frame_windows = false;
4059            let visible_cols: Vec<_> = output_names.iter().cloned().map(col).collect();
4060            lf = self.process_order_by(lf, &order_by, Some(&visible_cols))?;
4061
4062            // Drop any extra columns (eg: added to maintain ORDER BY access to original cols).
4063            let mut output_cols = visible_cols;
4064            if select_stmt.qualify.is_some() {
4065                output_cols.push(col(qualify_column.clone()));
4066            }
4067            lf.select(&output_cols)
4068        };
4069
4070        if select_stmt.qualify.is_some() {
4071            lf = lf
4072                .filter(col(qualify_column.clone()))
4073                .drop(Selector::ByName {
4074                    names: Arc::from([qualify_column]),
4075                    strict: true,
4076                });
4077        }
4078
4079        // Apply optional DISTINCT clause.
4080        lf = match &select_stmt.distinct {
4081            Some(Distinct::Distinct) => lf.unique_stable(None, UniqueKeepStrategy::Any),
4082            Some(Distinct::On(exprs)) => {
4083                // TODO: support exprs in `unique` see https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/5760
4084                let schema = Some(self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?);
4085                let cols = exprs
4086                    .iter()
4087                    .map(|e| {
4088                        let expr = parse_sql_expr(e, self, schema.as_deref())?;
4089                        if let Expr::Column(name) = expr {
4090                            Ok(name)
4091                        } else {
4092                            Err(polars_err!(SQLSyntax:"DISTINCT ON only supports column names"))
4093                        }
4094                    })
4095                    .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
4096
4097                // DISTINCT ON has to apply the ORDER BY before the operation.
4098                lf = self.process_order_by(lf, &query.order_by, None)?;
4099                return Ok(lf.unique_stable(
4100                    Some(Selector::ByName {
4101                        names: cols.into(),
4102                        strict: true,
4103                    }),
4104                    UniqueKeepStrategy::First,
4105                ));
4106            },
4107            // Note: `ALL` explicitly keeps duplicate rows (the default), so it's a no-op.
4108            Some(Distinct::All) | None => lf,
4109        };
4110        Ok(lf)
4111    }
4112
4113    /// Returns each projection alongside whether it came from an explicit `AS` alias.
4114    fn column_projections(
4115        &mut self,
4116        projection: &[SelectItem],
4117        flavor: SelectFlavor,
4118        schema: &SchemaRef,
4119    ) -> PolarsResult<Vec<(Expr, bool)>> {
4120        if projection.is_empty() && flavor == SelectFlavor::FromFirstNoSelect {
4121            // eg: bare "FROM tbl" is equivalent to "SELECT * FROM tbl".
4122            return Ok(schema
4123                .iter_names()
4124                .filter(|name| !is_correlated_result_col(name))
4125                .map(|name| (col(name.clone()), false))
4126                .collect());
4127        }
4128        let mut items: Vec<ProjectionItem> = Vec::with_capacity(projection.len());
4129        let mut has_qualified_wildcard = false;
4130
4131        for select_item in projection {
4132            match select_item {
4133                SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(expr) => {
4134                    items.push(ProjectionItem::Exprs(
4135                        vec![parse_sql_expr(expr, self, Some(schema))?],
4136                        false,
4137                    ));
4138                },
4139                SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr, alias } => {
4140                    let expr = parse_sql_expr(expr, self, Some(schema))?;
4141                    items.push(ProjectionItem::Exprs(
4142                        vec![expr.alias(PlSmallStr::from_str(alias.value.as_str()))],
4143                        true,
4144                    ));
4145                },
4146                SelectItem::ExprWithAliases { .. } => {
4147                    polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "multiple aliases per expression are not supported: {:?}", select_item)
4148                },
4149                SelectItem::QualifiedWildcard(kind, wildcard_options) => match kind {
4150                    SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::ObjectName(obj_name) => {
4151                        let tbl_name = obj_name
4152                            .0
4153                            .last()
4154                            .and_then(|p| p.as_ident())
4155                            .map(|i| PlSmallStr::from_str(&i.value))
4156                            .unwrap_or_default();
4157                        let exprs =
4158                            self.process_qualified_wildcard(obj_name, wildcard_options, schema)?;
4159                        items.push(ProjectionItem::QualifiedExprs(tbl_name, exprs));
4160                        has_qualified_wildcard = true;
4161                    },
4162                    SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::Expr(_) => {
4163                        polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "qualified wildcard on expressions not yet supported: {:?}", select_item)
4164                    },
4165                },
4166                SelectItem::Wildcard(wildcard_options) => {
4167                    let cols = schema
4168                        .iter_names()
4169                        .filter(|name| !is_correlated_result_col(name))
4170                        .map(|name| col(name.clone()))
4171                        .collect();
4172                    items.push(ProjectionItem::Exprs(
4173                        self.process_wildcard_additional_options(cols, wildcard_options, schema)?,
4174                        false,
4175                    ));
4176                },
4177            }
4178        }
4179
4180        // Disambiguate qualified wildcards (if any) and flatten expressions
4181        let exprs: Vec<(Expr, bool)> = if has_qualified_wildcard {
4182            disambiguate_projection_cols(items, schema)?
4183        } else {
4184            items
4185                .into_iter()
4186                .flat_map(|item| match item {
4187                    ProjectionItem::Exprs(exprs, is_explicit_alias) => exprs
4188                        .into_iter()
4189                        .map(|e| (e, is_explicit_alias))
4190                        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
4191                    ProjectionItem::QualifiedExprs(_, exprs) => {
4192                        exprs.into_iter().map(|e| (e, false)).collect()
4193                    },
4194                })
4195                .collect()
4196        };
4197        Ok(exprs
4198            .into_iter()
4199            .flat_map(|(expr, is_explicit_alias)| {
4200                expand_exprs(expr, schema)
4201                    .into_iter()
4202                    .map(move |e| (e, is_explicit_alias))
4203            })
4204            .collect())
4205    }
4206
4207    /// Filter `lf`, whose schema is `schema`, on the WHERE condition `where_expr`, lowering
4208    /// its correlated subqueries. The columns of the lowered subqueries stay in the result,
4209    /// and `schema` becomes its schema. `select_stmt` is the block the condition belongs to.
4210    fn filter_on_where(
4211        &mut self,
4212        mut lf: LazyFrame,
4213        schema: &mut SchemaRef,
4214        where_expr: Option<&SQLExpr>,
4215        bindings: &mut SubqueryBindings,
4216        select_stmt: Option<&Select>,
4217    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4218        let quantified = where_expr.and_then(|where_expr| {
4219            let conjuncts = flatten_and_conditions(where_expr);
4220            let rewritten: Vec<_> = conjuncts
4221                .iter()
4222                .map(|conj| quantified_as_exists(self, conj))
4223                .collect();
4224            rewritten.iter().any(Option::is_some).then(|| {
4225                let conjuncts = conjuncts
4226                    .into_iter()
4227                    .zip(rewritten)
4228                    .map(|(conj, rewritten)| rewritten.unwrap_or_else(|| conj.clone()))
4229                    .collect();
4230                combine_conditions(conjuncts, SQLBinaryOperator::And).unwrap()
4231            })
4232        });
4233        let where_expr = quantified.as_ref().or(where_expr);
4234
4235        // A correlated scalar subquery is lowered against the frame as it stands, so
4236        // the conjuncts that don't need it are applied first: the lowering can then
4237        // restrict its aggregate to the rows that survive them.
4238        let mut join_tree = None;
4239        let where_expr: Option<Cow<'_, SQLExpr>> = match where_expr {
4240            Some(where_expr) if expr_contains_scalar_subquery(where_expr) => {
4241                let n_grouping_calls = self.group_scope.grouping_calls.len();
4242                let residual;
4243                (lf, residual) = self.rewrite_subquery_conjuncts(
4244                    lf,
4245                    where_expr,
4246                    FilterMode::KeepTrue,
4247                    schema,
4248                    RewriteStage::BeforeScalarLowering,
4249                )?;
4250                self.reject_grouping_in_where(n_grouping_calls)?;
4251                if let Some(select_stmt) = select_stmt {
4252                    join_tree = self.outer_join_tree(select_stmt, where_expr, &residual)?;
4253                }
4254                *schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
4255                combine_conditions(
4256                    residual.into_iter().cloned().collect(),
4257                    SQLBinaryOperator::And,
4258                )
4259                .map(Cow::Owned)
4260            },
4261            other => other.map(Cow::Borrowed),
4262        };
4263
4264        // Lower correlated scalar subqueries in the WHERE clause before the filter is
4265        // parsed, leaving `[NOT] EXISTS` to `process_where`.
4266        let effective_where = match where_expr.as_deref() {
4267            Some(where_expr) => {
4268                let lowered;
4269                (lf, lowered) = self.lower_correlated_subqueries(
4270                    lf,
4271                    schema,
4272                    where_expr,
4273                    LowerScope::ScalarOnly,
4274                    bindings,
4275                    join_tree.as_ref(),
4276                )?;
4277                if matches!(lowered, Cow::Owned(_)) {
4278                    *schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
4279                }
4280                Some(lowered)
4281            },
4282            None => None,
4283        };
4284
4285        self.process_where(
4286            lf,
4287            effective_where.as_deref(),
4288            FilterMode::KeepTrue,
4289            Some(schema.clone()),
4290        )
4291    }
4292
4293    pub(crate) fn process_where(
4294        &mut self,
4295        mut lf: LazyFrame,
4296        expr: Option<&SQLExpr>,
4297        filter_mode: FilterMode,
4298        schema: Option<SchemaRef>,
4299    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4300        if let Some(expr) = expr {
4301            let schema = match schema {
4302                None => self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?,
4303                Some(s) => s,
4304            };
4305            // Parsing registers any `GROUPING()` call; subqueries keep their own registry.
4306            let n_grouping_calls = self.group_scope.grouping_calls.len();
4307
4308            // A condition that reads no input (eg: "WHERE 1 = 1") is accepted as any type
4309            // that casts to boolean; the planner folds it.
4310            if let Some(predicate) = self.input_independent_predicate(expr)? {
4311                self.reject_grouping_in_where(n_grouping_calls)?;
4312                let predicate = predicate.cast(DataType::Boolean);
4313                return Ok(match filter_mode {
4314                    FilterMode::KeepTrue => lf.filter(predicate),
4315                    FilterMode::RemoveTrue => lf.remove(predicate),
4316                });
4317            }
4318
4319            // Lower eligible `[NOT] EXISTS` / `[NOT] IN (subquery)` conjuncts
4320            // to semi / anti joins; whatever remains goes through the ordinary
4321            // filter path below.
4322            let residual_exprs: Vec<&SQLExpr>;
4323            (lf, residual_exprs) = self.rewrite_subquery_conjuncts(
4324                lf,
4325                expr,
4326                filter_mode,
4327                &schema,
4328                RewriteStage::AfterScalarLowering,
4329            )?;
4330
4331            // Decorrelate any `[NOT] EXISTS` left in a residual conjunct to a boolean
4332            // flag column, rewriting the conjunct to reference it.
4333            let exists_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
4334            let mut bindings = SubqueryBindings::new();
4335            let mut lowered_residuals = Vec::with_capacity(residual_exprs.len());
4336            for e in &residual_exprs {
4337                let lowered;
4338                (lf, lowered) = self.lower_correlated_subqueries(
4339                    lf,
4340                    &exists_schema,
4341                    e,
4342                    LowerScope::ScalarAndPredicates,
4343                    &mut bindings,
4344                    None,
4345                )?;
4346                lowered_residuals.push(lowered);
4347            }
4348
4349            // Whatever is still an uncorrelated `[NOT] IN` / `=` subquery conjunct
4350            // becomes a semi / anti join.
4351            #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
4352            let lowered_residuals = {
4353                let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(lowered_residuals.len());
4354                for e in lowered_residuals {
4355                    match self.try_rewrite_uncorrelated_subquery_conjunct(
4356                        &lf,
4357                        &e,
4358                        filter_mode,
4359                        &schema,
4360                    )? {
4361                        Some(new_lf) => lf = new_lf,
4362                        None => kept.push(e),
4363                    }
4364                }
4365                kept
4366            };
4367
4368            let Some(parsed_residual) = lowered_residuals
4369                .iter()
4370                .map(|e| parse_sql_expr(e, self, Some(&*schema)))
4371                .reduce(|a, b| Ok(a?.and(b?)))
4372            else {
4373                // Every conjunct was rewritten to a join; nothing left to filter.
4374                return Ok(lf);
4375            };
4376            let mut filter_expression = parsed_residual?;
4377            self.reject_grouping_in_where(n_grouping_calls)?;
4378            if filter_expression.clone().meta().has_multiple_outputs() {
4379                filter_expression = all_horizontal([filter_expression])?;
4380            }
4381            let mut placeholders;
4382            (lf, placeholders) =
4383                self.process_subqueries(lf, vec![&mut filter_expression], SubqueryShape::Scalar)?;
4384            lf = match filter_mode {
4385                FilterMode::KeepTrue => lf.filter(filter_expression),
4386                FilterMode::RemoveTrue => lf.remove(filter_expression),
4387            };
4388
4389            // Flag and placeholder columns exist only for the filter above. A SELECT
4390            // projects them away afterwards, but a DELETE returns this frame as-is.
4391            placeholders.extend(bindings.into_iter().map(|(_, _, name)| name));
4392            lf = drop_subquery_placeholders(lf, placeholders);
4393        }
4394        Ok(lf)
4395    }
4396
4397    /// Fail if parsing since `n_grouping_calls` were registered added a `GROUPING()` call.
4398    fn reject_grouping_in_where(&self, n_grouping_calls: usize) -> PolarsResult<()> {
4399        polars_ensure!(
4400            self.group_scope.grouping_calls.len() == n_grouping_calls,
4401            SQLSyntax: "GROUPING() is not allowed in the WHERE clause"
4402        );
4403        Ok(())
4404    }
4405
4406    /// Parse a condition that yields one value independent of any input frame (a literal or
4407    /// elementwise operations over literals); `None` for any other condition.
4408    fn input_independent_predicate(&mut self, expr: &SQLExpr) -> PolarsResult<Option<Expr>> {
4409        if expr_references_any_column(expr) || expr_contains_subquery(expr) {
4410            return Ok(None);
4411        }
4412        let predicate = parse_sql_expr(expr, self, None)?;
4413        let independent = predicate
4414            .clone()
4415            .meta()
4416            .is_input_independent_scalar()
4417            .unwrap_or(false);
4418        Ok(independent.then_some(predicate))
4419    }
4420
4421    /// Join `tbl_left` with `tbl_right`. With `keep_right` (`RIGHT SEMI` / `RIGHT ANTI`),
4422    /// `join_type` is a semi or anti join that keeps the rows of `tbl_right`.
4423    pub(super) fn process_join(
4424        &mut self,
4425        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
4426        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
4427        constraint: &JoinConstraint,
4428        join_type: JoinType,
4429        keep_right: bool,
4430    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4431        // Other joins evaluate the condition per part of the input.
4432        if let JoinConstraint::On(expr) = constraint
4433            && join_type != JoinType::Inner
4434            && contains_random(expr, false)
4435        {
4436            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "RANDOM() in a JOIN condition is only supported for INNER JOIN")
4437        }
4438        if let JoinConstraint::On(expr) = constraint
4439            && expr_contains_subquery(expr)
4440        {
4441            // A correlated subquery in the condition is lowered to a column of the input it
4442            // reads, which then only lives for the join.
4443            if matches!(
4444                join_type,
4445                JoinType::Inner | JoinType::Left | JoinType::Right | JoinType::Full
4446            ) && let Some((left, right, on)) =
4447                self.lower_join_on_subqueries(tbl_left, tbl_right, expr, &join_type)?
4448            {
4449                let lowered: Arc<[PlSmallStr]> = left
4450                    .schema
4451                    .iter_names()
4452                    .filter(|name| !tbl_left.schema.contains(name))
4453                    .chain(
4454                        right
4455                            .schema
4456                            .iter_names()
4457                            .filter(|name| !tbl_right.schema.contains(name)),
4458                    )
4459                    .cloned()
4460                    .collect();
4461                let joined =
4462                    self.process_join(&left, &right, &JoinConstraint::On(on), join_type, false)?;
4463                return Ok(joined.drop(Selector::ByName {
4464                    names: lowered,
4465                    strict: true,
4466                }));
4467            }
4468            return self
4469                .process_join_on_subqueries(tbl_left, tbl_right, expr, join_type, keep_right);
4470        }
4471        self.join_inputs(
4472            tbl_left,
4473            tbl_right,
4474            Some(constraint),
4475            (vec![], vec![]),
4476            join_type,
4477            keep_right,
4478        )
4479    }
4480
4481    /// Join on `constraint` and on the key pairs `extra_keys`. Without either, every row
4482    /// pairs with every row.
4483    fn join_inputs(
4484        &mut self,
4485        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
4486        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
4487        constraint: Option<&JoinConstraint>,
4488        extra_keys: (Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>),
4489        join_type: JoinType,
4490        keep_right: bool,
4491    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4492        let (mut left_on, mut right_on, predicates) = match constraint {
4493            // A condition that reads no input (eg: `ON TRUE`, `ON 1 = 1`) pairs every row with
4494            // every row, or none: join on the condition itself as a boolean key (a null key
4495            // matches nothing, like an unknown condition).
4496            Some(JoinConstraint::On(expr))
4497                if let Some(predicate) = self.input_independent_predicate(expr)? =>
4498            {
4499                (
4500                    vec![strip_join_aliases(predicate).cast(DataType::Boolean)],
4501                    vec![lit(true)],
4502                    vec![],
4503                )
4504            },
4505            Some(constraint) => {
4506                let keys = process_join_constraint(constraint, tbl_left, tbl_right, self)?;
4507                for e in keys.0.iter().chain(&keys.1).chain(&keys.2) {
4508                    reject_unresolved_subquery(e, "JOIN ... ON")?;
4509                }
4510                keys
4511            },
4512            None => (vec![], vec![], vec![]),
4513        };
4514        left_on.extend(extra_keys.0);
4515        right_on.extend(extra_keys.1);
4516        let suffix = format!(":{}", tbl_right.name);
4517        // `RANDOM()` in an inner join condition draws a value per joined row, so it filters the
4518        // joined rows, and the other conditions still pick how the join runs.
4519        let (mut random_predicates, predicates): (Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>) = predicates
4520            .into_iter()
4521            .partition(|p| join_type == JoinType::Inner && has_expr(p, is_random));
4522        if join_type == JoinType::Inner
4523            && left_on
4524                .iter()
4525                .chain(&right_on)
4526                .any(|k| has_expr(k, is_random))
4527        {
4528            let keys = std::mem::take(&mut left_on)
4529                .into_iter()
4530                .zip(std::mem::take(&mut right_on));
4531            for (l, r) in keys {
4532                if has_expr(&l, is_random) || has_expr(&r, is_random) {
4533                    let r = suffix_conflicting_columns(r, tbl_left, tbl_right, &suffix);
4534                    random_predicates.push(l.eq(r));
4535                } else {
4536                    left_on.push(l);
4537                    right_on.push(r);
4538                }
4539            }
4540        }
4541        if left_on.is_empty() && predicates.is_empty() {
4542            left_on.push(lit(true));
4543            right_on.push(lit(true));
4544        }
4545        let (mut left_frame, mut right_frame) = (tbl_left.frame.clone(), tbl_right.frame.clone());
4546        if predicates.is_empty() {
4547            let natural = matches!(constraint, Some(JoinConstraint::Natural));
4548            let key_dtype = |key: &Expr, schema: &Schema| match key {
4549                Expr::Column(name) => schema.get(name).cloned(),
4550                key => key.to_field(schema).ok().map(|f| f.dtype),
4551            };
4552            for (l, r) in left_on.iter_mut().zip(right_on.iter_mut()) {
4553                let (Some(l_dtype), Some(r_dtype)) = (
4554                    key_dtype(l, &tbl_left.schema),
4555                    key_dtype(r, &tbl_right.schema),
4556                ) else {
4557                    continue;
4558                };
4559                let Some((l_cast, r_cast)) =
4560                    sql_join_key_pair(l.clone(), &l_dtype, r.clone(), &r_dtype, true)
4561                else {
4562                    continue;
4563                };
4564                // A coalesced key column takes the common type.
4565                if natural && let (Expr::Column(l_name), Expr::Column(r_name)) = (&*l, &*r) {
4566                    left_frame = left_frame.with_column(l_cast.alias(l_name.clone()));
4567                    right_frame = right_frame.with_column(r_cast.alias(r_name.clone()));
4568                } else {
4569                    (*l, *r) = (l_cast, r_cast);
4570                }
4571            }
4572        }
4573        if keep_right {
4574            polars_ensure!(
4575                predicates.is_empty(),
4576                InvalidOperation: "'{}' join is not supported with non-equi join conditions",
4577                join_type
4578            );
4579            return right_frame
4580                .join_builder()
4581                .with(left_frame)
4582                .left_on(right_on)
4583                .right_on(left_on)
4584                .how(join_type)
4585                .finish();
4586        }
4587        let coalesce_type = match constraint {
4588            // "NATURAL" joins should coalesce; otherwise we disambiguate
4589            Some(JoinConstraint::Natural) => JoinCoalesce::CoalesceColumns,
4590            _ => JoinCoalesce::KeepColumns,
4591        };
4592        // `join_where` and the filter on the joined rows resolve the right columns that the
4593        // left input also has under their suffixed names.
4594        let mut joined_schema = (*tbl_left.schema).clone();
4595        if !predicates.is_empty() || !random_predicates.is_empty() {
4596            for (name, dtype) in tbl_right.schema.iter() {
4597                let name = if tbl_left.schema.contains(name) {
4598                    format_pl_smallstr!("{name}{suffix}")
4599                } else {
4600                    name.clone()
4601                };
4602                joined_schema.insert(name, dtype.clone());
4603            }
4604        }
4605
4606        let joined = if predicates.is_empty() {
4607            // Equi-join: standard left_on/right_on path
4608            left_frame
4609                .join_builder()
4610                .with(right_frame)
4611                .left_on(left_on)
4612                .right_on(right_on)
4613                .how(join_type)
4614                .suffix(suffix)
4615                .coalesce(coalesce_type)
4616                .finish()?
4617        } else {
4618            // Non-equi conditions: convert to predicates for `join_where`.
4619            // Any equi-conditions become equality predicates with right-side
4620            // columns suffixed to match their merged-schema names.
4621            let mut all_predicates = predicates;
4622            for (l, r) in left_on.into_iter().zip(right_on) {
4623                let r_suffixed = suffix_conflicting_columns(r, tbl_left, tbl_right, &suffix);
4624                all_predicates.push(l.eq(r_suffixed));
4625            }
4626            let all_predicates: Vec<Expr> = all_predicates
4627                .into_iter()
4628                .map(|p| {
4629                    sql_join_where_predicate(
4630                        strip_join_aliases(p),
4631                        &tbl_left.schema,
4632                        &joined_schema,
4633                    )
4634                })
4635                .collect();
4636            left_frame
4637                .join_builder()
4638                .with(right_frame)
4639                .how(join_type)
4640                .suffix(suffix)
4641                .coalesce(coalesce_type)
4642                .join_where(all_predicates)
4643        };
4644        let random_predicates = random_predicates.into_iter().map(|p| {
4645            sql_join_where_predicate(strip_join_aliases(p), &tbl_left.schema, &joined_schema)
4646        });
4647        Ok(match random_predicates.reduce(Expr::and) {
4648            Some(predicate) => joined.filter(predicate),
4649            None => joined,
4650        })
4651    }
4652
4653    /// Whether the relation `name` is the right input of a join; any other relation in
4654    /// scope is in the left input.
4655    pub(crate) fn is_right_relation(&self, name: &str, tbl_right: &TableInfo) -> bool {
4656        name == tbl_right.name
4657            || (!self.active_relations.iter().any(|r| r.key() == name)
4658                && name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&tbl_right.name))
4659    }
4660
4661    /// Whether the columns of the joined relation `name` can be found by name, which is not
4662    /// the case for the relations inside an aliased nested join.
4663    pub(crate) fn is_joined_relation(&self, name: &str, tbl_left: &TableInfo) -> bool {
4664        name == tbl_left.name
4665            || name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&tbl_left.name)
4666            || matches!(get_ignoring_case(&self.joined_aliases, name), Ok(Some(_)))
4667    }
4668
4669    /// Which input of a join the column `expr` reads: `Some(true)` for the left input,
4670    /// `Some(false)` for the right one, and `None` if it is not a column or is in both.
4671    pub(crate) fn column_join_input(
4672        &self,
4673        expr: &SQLExpr,
4674        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
4675        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
4676    ) -> Option<bool> {
4677        let column_side = |name: &str| match (
4678            tbl_left.schema.contains(name),
4679            tbl_right.schema.contains(name),
4680        ) {
4681            (true, false) => Some(true),
4682            (false, true) => Some(false),
4683            _ => None,
4684        };
4685        match expr {
4686            SQLExpr::Identifier(ident) => column_side(&ident.value),
4687            // A table qualifier takes precedence over a struct column of the same name.
4688            SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(idents) => match self.resolve_qualifier(idents) {
4689                Ok(Some((name, _))) => Some(!self.is_right_relation(&name, tbl_right)),
4690                Ok(None) => column_side(&idents[0].value),
4691                // An ambiguous qualifier is reported when the condition is parsed.
4692                Err(_) => None,
4693            },
4694            _ => None,
4695        }
4696    }
4697
4698    /// Which inputs of a join `expr` reads, as `(reads_left, reads_right)`. A column found
4699    /// in both inputs counts for neither.
4700    pub(crate) fn join_inputs_read(
4701        &self,
4702        expr: &SQLExpr,
4703        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
4704        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
4705    ) -> (bool, bool) {
4706        let (mut reads_left, mut reads_right) = (false, false);
4707        let _ = visit_expressions(expr, |e| {
4708            match self.column_join_input(e, tbl_left, tbl_right) {
4709                Some(true) => reads_left = true,
4710                Some(false) => reads_right = true,
4711                None => {},
4712            }
4713            ControlFlow::<()>::Continue(())
4714        });
4715        (reads_left, reads_right)
4716    }
4717
4718    /// Join on an `ON` condition that holds subqueries. A conjunct whose own columns read
4719    /// one input is applied to that input first: as a filter if the join drops the rows it
4720    /// rejects, else as a flag column joined against `TRUE`. A conjunct whose subqueries
4721    /// read the other input, or read an input while its own columns read both, filters an
4722    /// inner join of the inputs instead (see `join_then_filter`); semi and anti joins
4723    /// reject it.
4724    fn process_join_on_subqueries(
4725        &mut self,
4726        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
4727        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
4728        expr: &SQLExpr,
4729        join_type: JoinType,
4730        keep_right: bool,
4731    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4732        // Whether the join drops the rows of an input that match no row of the other.
4733        let (filter_left, filter_right) = match (&join_type, keep_right) {
4734            (JoinType::Inner, _) => (true, true),
4735            (JoinType::Left, _) => (false, true),
4736            (JoinType::Right, _) => (true, false),
4737            #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
4738            (JoinType::Semi, _) => (true, true),
4739            #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
4740            (JoinType::Anti, false) => (false, true),
4741            #[cfg(feature = "semi_anti_join")]
4742            (JoinType::Anti, true) => (true, false),
4743            _ => (false, false),
4744        };
4745        let mut left = tbl_left.clone();
4746        let mut right = tbl_right.clone();
4747        let (mut left_on, mut right_on) = (vec![], vec![]);
4748        let mut flags = vec![];
4749        let mut residual = vec![];
4750        let can_defer = !keep_right
4751            && matches!(
4752                join_type,
4753                JoinType::Inner | JoinType::Left | JoinType::Right | JoinType::Full
4754            );
4755        let mut deferred = vec![];
4756        for conjunct in flatten_and_conditions(expr) {
4757            if !expr_contains_subquery(conjunct) {
4758                residual.push(conjunct.clone());
4759                continue;
4760            }
4761            let (subqueries_read_left, subqueries_read_right) = if can_defer {
4762                self.subqueries_join_inputs(conjunct, tbl_left, tbl_right)
4763                    .unwrap_or_default()
4764            } else {
4765                (false, false)
4766            };
4767            let is_left = match self.conjunct_join_inputs(conjunct, tbl_left, tbl_right) {
4768                JoinInputs::Left => true,
4769                JoinInputs::Right => false,
4770                JoinInputs::Neither => !filter_right && filter_left,
4771                inputs @ (JoinInputs::Both | JoinInputs::Unknown) => {
4772                    if subqueries_read_left || subqueries_read_right {
4773                        deferred.push(conjunct.clone());
4774                        continue;
4775                    }
4776                    // Its uncorrelated subqueries become columns of an input.
4777                    let lifted = if matches!(inputs, JoinInputs::Both)
4778                        && self.is_joined_rows_condition(conjunct, &left, &right)?
4779                    {
4780                        self.lift_uncorrelated_subqueries(
4781                            conjunct, &mut left, &mut right, &mut flags,
4782                        )?
4783                    } else {
4784                        None
4785                    };
4786                    residual.push(lifted.unwrap_or_else(|| conjunct.clone()));
4787                    continue;
4788                },
4789            };
4790            if if is_left {
4791                subqueries_read_right
4792            } else {
4793                subqueries_read_left
4794            } {
4795                deferred.push(conjunct.clone());
4796                continue;
4797            }
4798            let (tbl, filter) = if is_left {
4799                (&mut left, filter_left)
4800            } else {
4801                (&mut right, filter_right)
4802            };
4803            // Planning the subqueries here also rejects those that read the other input.
4804            let mut condition =
4805                strip_join_aliases(parse_sql_expr(conjunct, self, Some(&tbl.schema))?);
4806            let placeholders;
4807            (tbl.frame, placeholders) = self.process_subqueries(
4808                tbl.frame.clone(),
4809                vec![&mut condition],
4810                SubqueryShape::Scalar,
4811            )?;
4812            let condition = condition.cast(DataType::Boolean);
4813            if filter {
4814                tbl.frame =
4815                    drop_subquery_placeholders(tbl.frame.clone().filter(condition), placeholders);
4816                continue;
4817            }
4818            let name = unique_column_name();
4819            tbl.frame = drop_subquery_placeholders(
4820                tbl.frame.clone().with_column(condition.alias(name.clone())),
4821                placeholders,
4822            );
4823            tbl.schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut tbl.frame)?;
4824            let (own_keys, other_keys) = if is_left {
4825                (&mut left_on, &mut right_on)
4826            } else {
4827                (&mut right_on, &mut left_on)
4828            };
4829            own_keys.push(col(name.clone()));
4830            other_keys.push(lit(true));
4831            flags.push(name);
4832        }
4833        let residual = combine_conditions(residual, SQLBinaryOperator::And).map(JoinConstraint::On);
4834        let joined = match combine_conditions(deferred, SQLBinaryOperator::And) {
4835            Some(deferred) => self.join_then_filter(
4836                &left,
4837                &right,
4838                residual.as_ref(),
4839                (left_on, right_on),
4840                &deferred,
4841                join_type,
4842            )?,
4843            None => self.join_inputs(
4844                &left,
4845                &right,
4846                residual.as_ref(),
4847                (left_on, right_on),
4848                join_type,
4849                keep_right,
4850            )?,
4851        };
4852        Ok(if flags.is_empty() {
4853            joined
4854        } else {
4855            joined.drop(Selector::ByName {
