4856                names: flags.into(),
4857                strict: false,
4858            })
4859        })
4860    }
4861
4862    /// Join `left` with `right` on `constraint` and `keys`, keeping only the pairs of rows
4863    /// that satisfy `condition`, whose subqueries may read both inputs. The condition
4864    /// filters an inner join of the inputs like a WHERE clause. An outer join then joins
4865    /// the pairs that pass back to its inputs by row index.
4866    fn join_then_filter(
4867        &mut self,
4868        left: &TableInfo,
4869        right: &TableInfo,
4870        constraint: Option<&JoinConstraint>,
4871        keys: (Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>),
4872        condition: &SQLExpr,
4873        join_type: JoinType,
4874    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4875        if join_type == JoinType::Inner {
4876            return self.filtered_inner_join(left, right, constraint, keys, condition);
4877        }
4878        // Not a `_POLARS_TMP` name, which a join with a literal key drops.
4879        let prefix = format_pl_smallstr!("{CORRELATED_COL_PREFIX}{}_", unique_column_name());
4880        let left_index = format_pl_smallstr!("{prefix}left");
4881        let right_index = format_pl_smallstr!("{prefix}right");
4882        let pair_index = format_pl_smallstr!("{prefix}pair");
4883        let mut row_indexed = |tbl: &TableInfo, name: &PlSmallStr| -> PolarsResult<TableInfo> {
4884            let mut frame = row_indexed_once(tbl.frame.clone(), name.clone());
4885            let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut frame)?;
4886            Ok(TableInfo {
4887                frame,
4888                schema,
4889                ..tbl.clone()
4890            })
4891        };
4892        let left = row_indexed(left, &left_index)?;
4893        let right = row_indexed(right, &right_index)?;
4894        let pairs = self
4895            .filtered_inner_join(&left, &right, constraint, keys, condition)?
4896            .select([
4897                col(left_index.clone()),
4898                col(right_index.clone()).alias(pair_index.clone()),
4899            ]);
4900        // Each left row with the right rows it pairs with: only the paired left rows for a
4901        // right join, else every left row, with a null pair index if it has no pair.
4902        let mut paired = left
4903            .frame
4904            .clone()
4905            .join_builder()
4906            .with(pairs)
4907            .on([col(left_index.clone())])
4908            .how(if join_type == JoinType::Right {
4909                JoinType::Inner
4910            } else {
4911                JoinType::Left
4912            })
4913            .coalesce(JoinCoalesce::CoalesceColumns)
4914            .finish()?;
4915        let paired = TableInfo {
4916            schema: self.get_frame_schema(&mut paired)?,
4917            frame: paired,
4918            ..left
4919        };
4920        let joined = self.join_inputs(
4921            &paired,
4922            &right,
4923            None,
4924            (
4925                vec![col(pair_index.clone())],
4926                vec![col(right_index.clone())],
4927            ),
4928            join_type,
4929            false,
4930        )?;
4931        Ok(joined.drop(Selector::ByName {
4932            names: [left_index, pair_index, right_index].into(),
4933            strict: true,
4934        }))
4935    }
4936
4937    /// Inner join `left` with `right` on `constraint` and `keys`, then filter on
4938    /// `condition` like a WHERE clause over the joined relations.
4939    fn filtered_inner_join(
4940        &mut self,
4941        left: &TableInfo,
4942        right: &TableInfo,
4943        constraint: Option<&JoinConstraint>,
4944        keys: (Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>),
4945        condition: &SQLExpr,
4946    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
4947        let mut joined = self.join_inputs(left, right, constraint, keys, JoinType::Inner, false)?;
4948        let mut schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut joined)?;
4949        // Resolves the right columns that the join renamed.
4950        self.record_joined_aliases(&right.name, &[], &left.schema, &right.schema, &schema)?;
4951        // An unqualified column of both inputs is ambiguous, also in the subqueries.
4952        check_for_ambiguous_column_refs(
4953            condition,
4954            &self.joined_aliases,
4955            &left.name,
4956            &self.join_using_cols,
4957            &self.active_relations,
4958            &schema,
4959        )?;
4960        let join_base = self.join_base.replace(JoinBase {
4961            table_name: left.name.to_string(),
4962            using_cols: self.join_using_cols.clone(),
4963        });
4964        let columns: Vec<Expr> = schema.iter_names().cloned().map(col).collect();
4965        let filtered = self.filter_on_where(
4966            joined,
4967            &mut schema,
4968            Some(condition),
4969            &mut SubqueryBindings::new(),
4970            None,
4971        );
4972        self.join_base = join_base;
4973        Ok(filtered?.select(columns))
4974    }
4975
4976    /// Which inputs of a join the conjunct `expr` reads, leaving out the inside of its
4977    /// subqueries. `Unknown` if a column is in neither input or, unqualified, in both.
4978    fn conjunct_join_inputs(
4979        &self,
4980        expr: &SQLExpr,
4981        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
4982        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
4983    ) -> JoinInputs {
4984        struct Reads<'a> {
4985            ctx: &'a SQLContext,
4986            left: &'a TableInfo,
4987            right: &'a TableInfo,
4988            subquery_depth: usize,
4989            reads_left: bool,
4990            reads_right: bool,
4991            unknown: bool,
4992        }
4993
4994        impl Reads<'_> {
4995            fn column(&mut self, name: &str) {
4996                match (
4997                    self.left.schema.contains(name),
4998                    self.right.schema.contains(name),
4999                ) {
5000                    (true, false) => self.reads_left = true,
5001                    (false, true) => self.reads_right = true,
5002                    _ => self.unknown = true,
5003                }
5004            }
5005        }
5006
5007        impl sqlparser::ast::Visitor for Reads<'_> {
5008            type Break = ();
5009
5010            fn pre_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5011                self.subquery_depth += 1;
5012                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5013            }
5014
5015            fn post_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5016                self.subquery_depth -= 1;
5017                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5018            }
5019
5020            fn pre_visit_expr(&mut self, expr: &SQLExpr) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5021                if self.subquery_depth > 0 {
5022                    return ControlFlow::Continue(());
5023                }
5024                match expr {
5025                    SQLExpr::Identifier(ident) => self.column(&ident.value),
5026                    SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(idents) => match self.ctx.resolve_qualifier(idents)
5027                    {
5028                        Ok(Some((name, _))) => match (
5029                            self.left.relations.contains(&name),
5030                            self.right.relations.contains(&name),
5031                        ) {
5032                            (true, false) => self.reads_left = true,
5033                            (false, true) => self.reads_right = true,
5034                            _ => self.unknown = true,
5035                        },
5036                        Ok(None) => self.column(&idents[0].value),
5037                        Err(_) => self.unknown = true,
5038                    },
5039                    _ => {},
5040                }
5041                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5042            }
5043        }
5044
5045        let mut reads = Reads {
5046            ctx: self,
5047            left: tbl_left,
5048            right: tbl_right,
5049            subquery_depth: 0,
5050            reads_left: false,
5051            reads_right: false,
5052            unknown: false,
5053        };
5054        let _ = dyn_visit::visit(expr, &mut reads);
5055        match (reads.unknown, reads.reads_left, reads.reads_right) {
5056            (true, _, _) => JoinInputs::Unknown,
5057            (false, true, true) => JoinInputs::Both,
5058            (false, true, false) => JoinInputs::Left,
5059            (false, false, true) => JoinInputs::Right,
5060            (false, false, false) => JoinInputs::Neither,
5061        }
5062    }
5063
5064    /// Whether the condition `expr`, which reads both inputs of a join, can be planned on
5065    /// their joined rows: each qualifier names a visible relation, and it has no aggregate or
5066    /// window call outside its subqueries. Raises on an ambiguous column.
5067    fn is_joined_rows_condition(
5068        &self,
5069        expr: &SQLExpr,
5070        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
5071        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
5072    ) -> PolarsResult<bool> {
5073        struct Check<'a> {
5074            ctx: &'a SQLContext,
5075            subquery_depth: usize,
5076        }
5077
5078        impl sqlparser::ast::Visitor for Check<'_> {
5079            type Break = ();
5080
5081            fn pre_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5082                self.subquery_depth += 1;
5083                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5084            }
5085
5086            fn post_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5087                self.subquery_depth -= 1;
5088                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5089            }
5090
5091            fn pre_visit_expr(&mut self, expr: &SQLExpr) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5092                if self.subquery_depth > 0 {
5093                    return ControlFlow::Continue(());
5094                }
5095                let is_valid = match expr {
5096                    // Not a struct field, such as `s.f` for a struct column `s`.
5097                    SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(idents) => {
5098                        matches!(self.ctx.resolve_qualifier(idents), Ok(Some(_)))
5099                    },
5100                    // A user-defined function may be an aggregate.
5101                    SQLExpr::Function(function) => {
5102                        function.over.is_none()
5103                            && !PolarsSQLFunctions::try_from_sql(function, self.ctx).is_ok_and(
5104                                |f| {
5105                                    f.is_builtin_aggregate()
5106                                        || matches!(f, PolarsSQLFunctions::Udf(_))
5107                                },
5108                            )
5109                    },
5110                    _ => true,
5111                };
5112                if is_valid {
5113                    ControlFlow::Continue(())
5114                } else {
5115                    ControlFlow::Break(())
5116                }
5117            }
5118        }
5119
5120        let mut check = Check {
5121            ctx: self,
5122            subquery_depth: 0,
5123        };
5124        if self
5125            .subqueries_join_inputs(expr, tbl_left, tbl_right)
5126            .is_none()
5127            || dyn_visit::visit(expr, &mut check).is_break()
5128        {
5129            return Ok(false);
5130        }
5131        // `check` passed qualified columns only, so no struct path needs the joined schema.
5132        check_for_ambiguous_column_refs(
5133            expr,
5134            &self.joined_aliases,
5135            &tbl_left.name,
5136            &self.join_using_cols,
5137            &self.active_relations,
5138            &tbl_left.schema,
5139        )?;
5140        Ok(true)
5141    }
5142
5143    /// Plan the scalar subqueries of `conjunct`, a condition that reads both inputs of a
5144    /// join, as columns of the input that the comparison operand holding them reads (else
5145    /// the left input), and return the condition reading those columns, whose names are
5146    /// added to `columns`. `None` if it has a correlated or another kind of subquery.
5147    fn lift_uncorrelated_subqueries(
5148        &mut self,
5149        conjunct: &SQLExpr,
5150        left: &mut TableInfo,
5151        right: &mut TableInfo,
5152        columns: &mut Vec<PlSmallStr>,
5153    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<SQLExpr>> {
5154        struct Lift {
5155            subquery_depth: usize,
5156            subqueries: Vec<(PlSmallStr, Box<Query>)>,
5157        }
5158
5159        impl VisitorMut for Lift {
5160            type Break = ();
5161
5162            fn pre_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &mut Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5163                self.subquery_depth += 1;
5164                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5165            }
5166
5167            fn post_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &mut Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5168                self.subquery_depth -= 1;
5169                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5170            }
5171
5172            fn pre_visit_expr(&mut self, expr: &mut SQLExpr) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5173                // A subquery operand of ANY/ALL is a set, not a value.
5174                if self.subquery_depth == 0
5175                    && matches!(expr, SQLExpr::AnyOp { .. } | SQLExpr::AllOp { .. })
5176                {
5177                    return ControlFlow::Break(());
5178                }
5179                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5180            }
5181
5182            fn post_visit_expr(&mut self, expr: &mut SQLExpr) -> ControlFlow<()> {
5183                if self.subquery_depth == 0
5184                    && let SQLExpr::Subquery(query) = expr
5185                {
5186                    let name =
5187                        format_pl_smallstr!("{CORRELATED_COL_PREFIX}{}", unique_column_name());
5188                    self.subqueries.push((name.clone(), query.clone()));
5189                    *expr = SQLExpr::Identifier(Ident::with_quote('"', name.as_str()));
5190                }
5191                ControlFlow::Continue(())
5192            }
5193        }
5194
5195        let mut lifted = conjunct.clone();
5196        // The subqueries of each operand of a comparison go to the input it reads.
5197        let operands = match &mut lifted {
5198            SQLExpr::BinaryOp {
5199                left: lhs,
5200                right: rhs,
5201                ..
5202            } => vec![&mut **lhs, &mut **rhs],
5203            expr => vec![expr],
5204        };
5205        let (mut left_subqueries, mut right_subqueries) = (vec![], vec![]);
5206        for operand in operands {
5207            let on_right = matches!(
5208                self.conjunct_join_inputs(operand, left, right),
5209                JoinInputs::Right
5210            );
5211            let mut lift = Lift {
5212                subquery_depth: 0,
5213                subqueries: vec![],
5214            };
5215            if dyn_visit::visit_mut(operand, &mut lift).is_break() {
5216                return Ok(None);
5217            }
5218            if on_right {
5219                right_subqueries.extend(lift.subqueries);
5220            } else {
5221                left_subqueries.extend(lift.subqueries);
5222            }
5223        }
5224        if expr_contains_subquery(&lifted)
5225            || left_subqueries
5226                .iter()
5227                .chain(&right_subqueries)
5228                .any(|(_, query)| is_correlated_subquery(query, self.catalog_spellings()))
5229        {
5230            return Ok(None);
5231        }
5232        self.add_subquery_columns(left, left_subqueries, columns)?;
5233        self.add_subquery_columns(right, right_subqueries, columns)?;
5234        Ok(Some(lifted))
5235    }
5236
5237    /// Add the values of the uncorrelated scalar `subqueries` to `tbl` as the columns they
5238    /// name, and those names to `columns`.
5239    fn add_subquery_columns(
5240        &mut self,
5241        tbl: &mut TableInfo,
5242        subqueries: Vec<(PlSmallStr, Box<Query>)>,
5243        columns: &mut Vec<PlSmallStr>,
5244    ) -> PolarsResult<()> {
5245        if subqueries.is_empty() {
5246            return Ok(());
5247        }
5248        let mut values = subqueries
5249            .iter()
5250            .map(|(_, query)| {
5251                parse_sql_expr(&SQLExpr::Subquery(query.clone()), self, Some(&tbl.schema))
5252            })
5253            .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
5254        let (frame, placeholders) = self.process_subqueries(
5255            tbl.frame.clone(),
5256            values.iter_mut().collect(),
5257            SubqueryShape::Broadcast,
5258        )?;
5259        let values: Vec<Expr> = values
5260            .into_iter()
5261            .zip(&subqueries)
5262            .map(|(value, (name, _))| value.alias(name.clone()))
5263            .collect();
5264        tbl.frame = drop_subquery_placeholders(frame.with_columns(values), placeholders);
5265        tbl.schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut tbl.frame)?;
5266        columns.extend(subqueries.into_iter().map(|(name, _)| name));
5267        Ok(())
5268    }
5269
5270    /// Which input an `ASOF JOIN` match operand reads: `Some(true)` for the left input,
5271    /// `Some(false)` for the right one, and `None` if all its columns are in both.
5272    #[cfg(feature = "asof_join")]
5273    fn asof_operand_is_left(
5274        &self,
5275        expr: &SQLExpr,
5276        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
5277        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
5278    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<bool>> {
5279        let (reads_left, reads_right) = self.join_inputs_read(expr, tbl_left, tbl_right);
5280        polars_ensure!(
5281            !(reads_left && reads_right),
5282            SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN MATCH_CONDITION operand {} reads both tables", expr
5283        );
5284        Ok(match (reads_left, reads_right) {
5285            (true, _) => Some(true),
5286            (_, true) => Some(false),
5287            _ => None,
5288        })
5289    }
5290
5291    /// `ASOF JOIN r MATCH_CONDITION (l.t >= r.t) [ON l.k = r.k AND ... | USING (k, ...)]`.
5292    ///
5293    /// Every left row is kept, paired with the closest right row that satisfies the match
5294    /// condition and has equal keys, or with nulls if there is none.
5295    #[cfg(feature = "asof_join")]
5296    fn process_asof_join(
5297        &mut self,
5298        tbl_left: &TableInfo,
5299        tbl_right: &TableInfo,
5300        match_condition: &SQLExpr,
5301        constraint: &JoinConstraint,
5302    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
5303        let mut condition = match_condition;
5304        while let SQLExpr::Nested(inner) = condition {
5305            condition = inner;
5306        }
5307        let SQLExpr::BinaryOp { left, op, right } = condition else {
5308            polars_bail!(
5309                SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN MATCH_CONDITION must be a single `>=`, `>`, `<=` or `<` comparison, found {}",
5310                match_condition
5311            )
5312        };
5313        polars_ensure!(
5314            matches!(
5315                op,
5316                SQLBinaryOperator::GtEq
5317                    | SQLBinaryOperator::Gt
5318                    | SQLBinaryOperator::LtEq
5319                    | SQLBinaryOperator::Lt
5320            ),
5321            SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN MATCH_CONDITION must be a single `>=`, `>`, `<=` or `<` comparison, found {}",
5322            match_condition
5323        );
5324        polars_ensure!(
5325            expr_references_any_column(left) && expr_references_any_column(right),
5326            SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN MATCH_CONDITION must compare a column of each table, found {}",
5327            match_condition
5328        );
5329        let left_is_left = match (
5330            self.asof_operand_is_left(left, tbl_left, tbl_right)?,
5331            self.asof_operand_is_left(right, tbl_left, tbl_right)?,
5332        ) {
5333            (Some(l), Some(r)) if l != r => l,
5334            (Some(l), None) => l,
5335            (None, Some(r)) => !r,
5336            (Some(_), Some(_)) => polars_bail!(
5337                SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN MATCH_CONDITION must compare a column of each table, found {}",
5338                match_condition
5339            ),
5340            (None, None) => polars_bail!(
5341                SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN MATCH_CONDITION is ambiguous, qualify its columns with their table name: {}",
5342                match_condition
5343            ),
5344        };
5345        let swapped = !left_is_left;
5346        let (left_operand, right_operand) = if swapped {
5347            (right, left)
5348        } else {
5349            (left, right)
5350        };
5351        let left_on =
5352            strip_join_aliases(parse_sql_expr(left_operand, self, Some(&tbl_left.schema))?);
5353        let right_on = strip_join_aliases(parse_sql_expr(
5354            right_operand,
5355            self,
5356            Some(&tbl_right.schema),
5357        )?);
5358        let (strategy, allow_eq) = match (op, swapped) {
5359            (SQLBinaryOperator::GtEq, false) | (SQLBinaryOperator::LtEq, true) => {
5360                (AsofStrategy::Backward, true)
5361            },
5362            (SQLBinaryOperator::Gt, false) | (SQLBinaryOperator::Lt, true) => {
5363                (AsofStrategy::Backward, false)
5364            },
5365            (SQLBinaryOperator::LtEq, false) | (SQLBinaryOperator::GtEq, true) => {
5366                (AsofStrategy::Forward, true)
5367            },
5368            _ => (AsofStrategy::Forward, false),
5369        };
5370
5371        let (left_by, right_by) = match constraint {
5372            JoinConstraint::None => (vec![], vec![]),
5373            _ => {
5374                let (left_by, right_by, predicates) =
5375                    process_join_constraint(constraint, tbl_left, tbl_right, self)?;
5376                polars_ensure!(
5377                    predicates.is_empty(),
5378                    SQLSyntax: "ASOF JOIN only supports `=` conditions in ON; the inequality goes in MATCH_CONDITION"
5379                );
5380                (left_by, right_by)
5381            },
5382        };
5383        for e in [&left_on, &right_on]
5384            .into_iter()
5385            .chain(&left_by)
5386            .chain(&right_by)
5387        {
5388            reject_unresolved_subquery(e, "ASOF JOIN")?;
5389        }
5390
5391        let to_supertype = |l: Expr, r: Expr| -> PolarsResult<(Expr, Expr)> {
5392            let l_dtype = l.to_field(&tbl_left.schema)?.dtype;
5393            let r_dtype = r.to_field(&tbl_right.schema)?.dtype;
5394            asof_key_pair(l, &l_dtype, r, &r_dtype)
5395        };
5396
5397        // `by` keys are column names, so each key pair is computed into a temporary column
5398        // that is dropped after the join.
5399        let mut left = tbl_left.frame.clone();
5400        let mut right = tbl_right.frame.clone();
5401        let mut by_names = Vec::with_capacity(left_by.len());
5402        for (l, r) in left_by.into_iter().zip(right_by) {
5403            let (l, r) = to_supertype(l, r)?;
5404            let name = loop {
5405                let name = unique_column_name();
5406                if !tbl_left.schema.contains(&name) && !tbl_right.schema.contains(&name) {
5407                    break name;
5408                }
5409            };
5410            left = left.with_column(l.alias(name.clone()));
5411            right = right.with_column(r.alias(name.clone()));
5412            by_names.push(name);
5413        }
5414
5415        // Both inputs must be sorted on the match key.
5416        let (left_on, right_on) = to_supertype(left_on, right_on)?;
5417        let left = left.sort_by_exprs([left_on.clone()], SortMultipleOptions::default());
5418        let right = right.sort_by_exprs([right_on.clone()], SortMultipleOptions::default());
5419
5420        let has_by = !by_names.is_empty();
5421        let joined = left
5422            .join_builder()
5423            .with(right)
5424            .left_on([left_on])
5425            .right_on([right_on])
5426            .how(JoinType::AsOf(Box::new(AsOfOptions {
5427                strategy,
5428                tolerance: None,
5429                tolerance_str: None,
5430                left_by: has_by.then(|| by_names.clone()),
5431                right_by: has_by.then(|| by_names.clone()),
5432                allow_eq,
5433                check_sortedness: false,
5434            })))
5435            .suffix(format!(":{}", tbl_right.name))
5436            .coalesce(JoinCoalesce::KeepColumns)
5437            .finish()?;
5438        Ok(if has_by {
5439            joined.drop(Selector::ByName {
5440                names: Arc::from(by_names),
5441                strict: true,
5442            })
5443        } else {
5444            joined
5445        })
5446    }
5447
5448    /// Process implicit (comma-separated) joins from `FROM t1, t2, ...` syntax.
5449    ///
5450    /// Extracts join predicates from the WHERE clause, joining each additional table with
5451    /// either an INNER JOIN (cross-table predicates found) or a CROSS JOIN (no predicates).
5452    /// Tables are joined in the order they become connectable rather than source order.
5453    /// Returns the residual WHERE conditions not consumed as join predicates.
5454    fn process_implicit_joins(
5455        &mut self,
5456        lf: &mut LazyFrame,
5457        from: &[TableWithJoins],
5458        where_clause: &Option<SQLExpr>,
5459    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<SQLExpr>> {
5460        let first = from.first().unwrap();
5461        let mut remaining_where = where_clause.clone();
5462        let mut joined_table_names: Vec<String> = kept_factors(first)
5463            .into_iter()
5464            .filter_map(get_table_name)
5465            .collect();
5466        // Resolving is `&mut self`, so all relations must be resolved up-front rather than
5467        // mid-probe while picking a join order below.
5468        let mut pending = Vec::with_capacity(from.len() - 1);
5469        for tbl_expr in from.iter().skip(1) {
5470            let mut rf = self.execute_from_statement(tbl_expr)?;
5471            let r_name = kept_factors(tbl_expr)
5472                .into_iter()
5473                .next()
5474                .and_then(get_table_name)
5475                .unwrap_or_default();
5476            polars_ensure!(
5477                !r_name.is_empty(),
5478                SQLInterface: "implicit joins require named tables; please provide an alias"
5479            );
5480            let right_schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut rf)?;
5481            pending.push((tbl_expr, rf, r_name, right_schema));
5482        }
5483
5484        // Each round takes the first pending relation with a join predicate against the
5485        // tables joined so far; relations with no predicate yet are deferred. Genuinely
5486        // disconnected relations fall through to a cross join, in source order.
5487        while !pending.is_empty() {
5488            let left_schema = self.get_frame_schema(lf)?;
5489            // Relations each pending entry brings into scope.
5490            let pending_relations: Vec<Vec<String>> = pending
5491                .iter()
5492                .map(|(tbl_expr, ..)| {
5493                    declared_relations(std::slice::from_ref(*tbl_expr), &self.catalog_spellings)
5494                        .iter()
5495                        .map(RelationName::key)
5496                        .collect()
5497                })
5498                .collect();
5499            let deferred_tables = |skip: usize| -> Vec<String> {
5500                pending_relations
5501                    .iter()
5502                    .enumerate()
5503                    .filter(|(i, _)| *i != skip)
5504                    .flat_map(|(_, names)| names.iter().cloned())
5505                    .collect()
5506            };
5507            let next = (0..pending.len())
5508                .find(|&i| {
5509                    let (_, _, r_name, right_schema) = &pending[i];
5510                    extract_join_predicates(
5511                        &remaining_where,
5512                        &joined_table_names,
5513                        r_name,
5514                        &deferred_tables(i),
5515                        &self.active_relations,
5516                        &left_schema,
5517                        right_schema,
5518                    )
5519                    .0
5520                    .is_some()
5521                })
5522                .unwrap_or(0);
5523            let deferred = deferred_tables(next);
5524            let (tbl_expr, rf, r_name, right_schema) = pending.remove(next);
5525            let (join_expr, residual) = extract_join_predicates(
5526                &remaining_where,
5527                &joined_table_names,
5528                &r_name,
5529                &deferred,
5530                &self.active_relations,
5531                &left_schema,
5532                &right_schema,
5533            );
5534
5535            *lf = if let Some(on_expr) = join_expr {
5536                self.process_join(
5537                    &TableInfo {
5538                        frame: lf.clone(),
5539                        name: PlSmallStr::from_str(
5540                            &joined_table_names.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
5541                        ),
5542                        schema: left_schema.clone(),
5543                        relations: joined_table_names.clone(),
5544                    },
5545                    &TableInfo {
5546                        frame: rf,
5547                        name: PlSmallStr::from_str(&r_name),
5548                        schema: right_schema.clone(),
5549                        relations: kept_factors(tbl_expr)
5550                            .into_iter()
5551                            .filter_map(get_table_name)
5552                            .collect(),
5553                    },
5554                    &JoinConstraint::On(on_expr),
5555                    JoinType::Inner,
5556                    false,
5557                )?
5558            } else {
5559                lf.clone()
5560                    .cross_join(rf, Some(format_pl_smallstr!(":{}", r_name)))
5561            };
5562            remaining_where = residual;
5563
5564            let joined_schema = self.get_frame_schema(lf)?;
5565            self.record_joined_aliases(
5566                &r_name,
5567                &pending_relations[next],
5568                &left_schema,
5569                &right_schema,
5570                &joined_schema,
5571            )?;
5572            joined_table_names.extend(
5573                kept_factors(tbl_expr)
5574                    .into_iter()
5575                    .filter_map(get_table_name),
5576            );
5577        }
5578        Ok(remaining_where)
5579    }
5580
5581    /// Resolve `Expr::SubPlan` nodes in `exprs` into columns of `lf`, returning the updated
5582    /// frame together with the set of placeholder column names the subqueries were bound to.
5583    ///
5584    /// `shape` selects how the placeholder is referenced; see [`SubqueryShape`].
5585    pub(crate) fn process_subqueries(
5586        &mut self,
5587        lf: LazyFrame,
5588        exprs: Vec<&mut Expr>,
5589        shape: SubqueryShape,
5590    ) -> PolarsResult<(LazyFrame, PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>)> {
5591        let mut subplans = vec![];
5592        let mut subplan_names = PlHashSet::new();
5593
5594        for e in exprs {
5595            *e = e.clone().try_map_expr(|e| {
5596                if let Expr::SubPlan(lp, names) = e {
5597                    assert_eq!(
5598                        names.len(),
5599                        1,
5600                        "multiple columns in subqueries not yet supported"
5601                    );
5602
5603                    let select_expr = names[0].1.clone();
5604                    let mut lf = LazyFrame::from((**lp).clone());
5605                    let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
5606                    polars_ensure!(schema.len() == 1,  SQLSyntax: "SQL subquery returns more than one column");
5607                    let lf = lf.select([select_expr.clone()]);
5608
5609                    // A window lowering can repeat a subquery, as in `SUM((SELECT 1)) OVER ()`.
5610                    if subplan_names.insert(names[0].0.clone()) {
5611                        self.group_scope
5612                            .subquery_plans
5613                            .insert(names[0].0.clone(), lf.clone());
5614                        subplans.push(lf);
5615                    }
5616                    let placeholder = Expr::Column(names[0].0.clone());
5617                    Ok(match shape {
5618                        SubqueryShape::Scalar => placeholder.first(),
5619                        SubqueryShape::Broadcast => placeholder,
5620                    })
5621                } else {
5622                    Ok(e)
5623                }
5624            })?;
5625        }
5626
5627        if subplans.is_empty() {
5628            Ok((lf, subplan_names))
5629        } else {
5630            subplans.insert(0, lf);
5631            Ok((
5632                concat_lf_horizontal(
5633                    subplans,
5634                    HConcatOptions {
5635                        broadcast_unit_length: true,
5636                        ..Default::default()
5637                    },
5638                )?,
5639                subplan_names,
5640            ))
5641        }
5642    }
5643
5644    fn execute_create_table(&mut self, stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
5645        if let Statement::CreateTable(create_table) = stmt {
5646            self.validate_create_table(create_table, false)?;
5647            let CreateTable {
5648                if_not_exists,
5649                or_replace,
5650                temporary,
5651                name,
5652                query,
5653                columns,
5654                like,
5655                ..
5656            } = create_table;
5657
5658            if *temporary {
5659                // A temporary table is always a registered table.
5660                let named = name_parts(name).and_then(|parts| self.catalogs.named_catalog(&parts));
5661                if let Some(catalog) = named {
5662                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "temporary tables cannot be created in catalog '{}'", catalog);
5663                }
5664            } else {
5665                // The caller creates catalog tables (see `catalog_statement`); here they are an error.
5666                self.catalog_create_target(name)?;
5667                self.ensure_not_catalog_table(name, "CREATE TABLE")?;
5668            }
5669            let tbl_name = object_name_to_string(name);
5670            let existing = self.registered_table_key(&tbl_name)?;
5671            if let Some(existing) = &existing {
5672                if *if_not_exists {
5673                    // `IF NOT EXISTS` leaves the existing table as it is.
5674                    return Ok(df! { "Response" => [format!("CREATE TABLE {existing}")] }?.lazy());
5675                }
5676                polars_ensure!(
5677                    !*temporary || *or_replace,
5678                    SQLInterface: "table '{}' already exists; use `CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE`, or `IF NOT EXISTS`",
5679                    existing
5680                );
5681            }
5682            // A table matching ignoring case is replaced under its existing name.
5683            let tbl_name = existing.unwrap_or(tbl_name);
5684            let tbl_name = tbl_name.as_str();
5685            let lf = match (query, columns.is_empty(), like) {
5686                (Some(query), true, None) => {
5687                    // ----------------------------------------------------
5688                    // CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMP] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <name> AS <query>
5689                    // ----------------------------------------------------
5690                    self.execute_query(query)?
5691                },
5692                (None, false, None) => {
5693                    // ----------------------------------------------------
5694                    // CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMP] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <name> (<coldef>, ...)
5695                    // ----------------------------------------------------
5696                    let mut schema = Schema::with_capacity(columns.len());
5697                    for col in columns {
5698                        let col_name = col.name.value.as_str();
5699                        let dtype = map_sql_dtype_to_polars(&col.data_type)?;
5700                        schema.insert_at_index(schema.len(), col_name.into(), dtype)?;
5701                    }
5702                    DataFrame::empty_with_schema(&schema).lazy()
5703                },
5704                (None, true, Some(like_kind)) => {
5705                    // ----------------------------------------------------
5706                    // CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMP] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <name> LIKE <table>
5707                    // ----------------------------------------------------
5708                    let like_name = match like_kind {
5709                        CreateTableLikeKind::Plain(like)
5710                        | CreateTableLikeKind::Parenthesized(like) => &like.name,
5711                    };
5712                    let like_table = object_name_to_string(like_name);
5713                    match get_ignoring_case(&self.table_map.read().unwrap(), &like_table)? {
5714                        Some(table) => table.clone().clear(),
5715                        None => {
5716                            let catalog_table = name_parts(like_name)
5717                                .is_some_and(|parts| self.catalogs.resolve(&parts).is_some());
5718                            polars_ensure!(!catalog_table, SQLInterface: "`CREATE TABLE ... LIKE` is not supported for catalog tables");
5719                            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "table given in LIKE does not exist: {}", like_table)
5720                        },
5721                    }
5722                },
5723                // No valid options provided
5724                (None, true, None) => {
5725                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "CREATE TABLE expected a query, column definitions, or LIKE clause")
5726                },
5727                // Mutually exclusive options
5728                _ => {
5729                    polars_bail!(
5730                        SQLInterface: "CREATE TABLE received mutually exclusive options:\nquery = {:?}\ncolumns = {:?}\nlike = {:?}",
5731                        query,
5732                        columns,
5733                        like,
5734                    )
5735                },
5736            };
5737            self.register(tbl_name, lf);
5738
5739            let df_created = df! { "Response" => [format!("CREATE TABLE {tbl_name}")] };
5740            Ok(df_created.unwrap().lazy())
5741        } else {
5742            unreachable!()
5743        }
5744    }
5745
5746    pub(crate) fn get_table(
5747        &mut self,
5748        relation: &TableFactor,
5749    ) -> PolarsResult<(String, LazyFrame)> {
5750        if let Some(name) = get_table_name(relation) {
5751            self.from_item_frames.remove(&name);
5752        }
5753        match relation {
5754            TableFactor::Table {
5755                name, alias, args, ..
5756            } => {
5757                self.validate_table_factor(relation)?;
5758                if let Some(args) = args {
5759                    return self.execute_table_function(name, alias, &args.args);
5760                }
5761                // A qualified name (`schema.table`) is looked up as a whole, among CTEs,
5762                // registered and catalog tables: the alias of another FROM item is not a table.
5763                let tbl_name = object_name_to_string(name);
5764                if let Some(lf) = self.get_table_unaliased(&tbl_name)? {
5765                    match alias {
5766                        Some(alias) => {
5767                            self.table_aliases
5768                                .insert(alias.name.value.clone(), tbl_name);
5769                            Ok((alias.name.value.clone(), lf))
5770                        },
5771                        None => Ok((tbl_name, lf)),
5772                    }
5773                } else {
5774                    let hint = name_parts(name)
5775                        .and_then(|parts| self.catalogs.unresolved_hint(&parts))
5776                        .unwrap_or_default();
5777                    polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "relation '{}' was not found{}", tbl_name, hint);
5778                }
5779            },
5780            TableFactor::Derived {
5781                lateral,
5782                subquery,
5783                alias,
5784                sample,
5785            } => {
5786                polars_ensure!(!(*lateral), SQLInterface: "`LATERAL` clause is not supported");
5787                polars_ensure!(sample.is_none(), SQLInterface: "table `SAMPLE` clause is not supported");
5788
5789                // Execute the subquery in isolation so that outer join state
5790                // doesn't leak into it and cause spurious ambiguous-column errors
5791                let strict = alias
5792                    .as_ref()
5793                    .is_some_and(|alias| alias.name.value.starts_with(NESTED_PREFIX));
5794                let lf = self.execute_isolated(|ctx| {
5795                    ctx.strict_relations |= strict;
5796                    ctx.execute_query(subquery)
5797                })?;
5798                if let Some(alias) = alias {
5799                    let lf = self.rename_columns_from_table_alias(lf, alias)?;
5800                    let name = alias.name.value.clone();
5801                    self.from_item_frames.insert(name.clone(), lf.clone());
5802                    Ok((name, lf))
5803                } else {
5804                    Ok(("".to_string(), lf))
5805                }
5806            },
5807            TableFactor::UNNEST {
5808                alias,
5809                array_exprs,
5810                with_offset,
5811                with_offset_alias: _,
5812                with_ordinality,
5813            } => {
5814                if let Some(alias) = alias {
5815                    let column_names: Vec<Option<PlSmallStr>> = alias
5816                        .columns
5817                        .iter()
5818                        .map(|c| {
5819                            if c.name.value.is_empty() {
5820                                None
5821                            } else {
5822                                Some(PlSmallStr::from_str(c.name.value.as_str()))
5823                            }
5824                        })
5825                        .collect();
5826
5827                    let column_values: Vec<Series> = array_exprs
5828                        .iter()
5829                        .map(|arr| parse_sql_array(arr, self))
5830                        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
5831
5832                    polars_ensure!(!column_names.is_empty(),
5833                        SQLSyntax:
5834                        "UNNEST table alias must also declare column names, eg: {} (a,b,c)", alias.name.to_string()
5835                    );
5836                    if column_names.len() != column_values.len() {
5837                        let plural = if column_values.len() > 1 { "s" } else { "" };
5838                        polars_bail!(
5839                            SQLSyntax:
5840                            "UNNEST table alias requires {} column name{}, found {}", column_values.len(), plural, column_names.len()
5841                        );
5842                    }
5843                    let column_series: Vec<Column> = column_values
5844                        .into_iter()
5845                        .zip(column_names)
5846                        .map(|(s, name)| {
5847                            if let Some(name) = name {
5848                                s.with_name(name)
5849                            } else {
5850                                s
5851                            }
5852                        })
5853                        .map(Column::from)
5854                        .collect();
5855
5856                    let lf = DataFrame::new_infer_height(column_series)?.lazy();
5857
5858                    if *with_offset || *with_ordinality {
5859                        // TODO: support 'WITH ORDINALITY|OFFSET' modifier.
5860                        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "UNNEST tables do not (yet) support WITH ORDINALITY|OFFSET");
5861                    }
5862                    let table_name = alias.name.value.clone();
5863                    self.from_item_frames.insert(table_name.clone(), lf.clone());
5864                    Ok((table_name, lf))
5865                } else {
5866                    polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "UNNEST table must have an alias");
5867                }
5868            },
5869            TableFactor::NestedJoin {
5870                table_with_joins,
5871                alias,
5872            } => {
5873                // Only an alias makes the parenthesized join a scope of its own; bare parens
5874                // just group, so their relation aliases stay visible to the enclosing query.
5875                match alias {
5876                    Some(alias) => {
5877                        let lf = self
5878                            .execute_isolated(|ctx| ctx.execute_from_statement(table_with_joins))?;
5879                        let lf = self.rename_columns_from_table_alias(lf, alias)?;
5880                        let name = alias.name.value.clone();
5881                        self.from_item_frames.insert(name.clone(), lf.clone());
5882                        Ok((name, lf))
5883                    },
5884                    None => Ok((
5885                        String::new(),
5886                        self.execute_from_statement(table_with_joins)?,
5887                    )),
5888                }
5889            },
5890            // Support bare table, optionally with an alias, for now
5891            _ => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "not yet implemented: {}", relation),
5892        }
5893    }
5894
5895    fn execute_table_function(
5896        &mut self,
5897        name: &ObjectName,
5898        alias: &Option<TableAlias>,
5899        args: &[FunctionArg],
5900    ) -> PolarsResult<(String, LazyFrame)> {
5901        let tbl_fn = object_name_to_string(name);
5902        let tbl_fn = tbl_fn.as_str();
5903        let read_fn = tbl_fn.parse::<PolarsTableFunctions>()?;
5904        let (tbl_name, mut lf) = read_fn.execute(args, self)?;
5905        let tbl_name = match alias {
5906            Some(alias) => {
5907                lf = self.rename_columns_from_table_alias(lf, alias)?;
5908                alias.name.value.clone()
5909            },
5910            None => tbl_name,
5911        };
5912        self.from_item_frames.insert(tbl_name.clone(), lf.clone());
5913        Ok((tbl_name, lf))
5914    }
5915
5916    fn process_order_by(
5917        &mut self,
5918        mut lf: LazyFrame,
5919        order_by: &Option<OrderBy>,
5920        selected: Option<&[Expr]>,
5921    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
5922        if order_by.as_ref().is_none_or(|ob| match &ob.kind {
5923            OrderByKind::Expressions(exprs) => exprs.is_empty(),
5924            OrderByKind::All(_) => false,
5925        }) {
5926            return Ok(lf);
5927        }
5928        let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
5929        let columns_iter = schema.iter_names().map(|e| col(e.clone()));
5930        let (order_by, order_by_all, n_order_cols) = match &order_by.as_ref().unwrap().kind {
5931            OrderByKind::Expressions(exprs) => {
5932                // TODO: will look at making an upstream PR that allows us to more easily
5933                //  create a GenericDialect variant supporting "OrderByKind::All" instead
5934                if exprs.len() == 1
5935                    && matches!(&exprs[0].expr, SQLExpr::Identifier(ident)
5936                        if ident.value.to_uppercase() == "ALL"
5937                        && !schema.iter_names().any(|name| name.to_uppercase() == "ALL"))
5938                {
5939                    // Treat as ORDER BY ALL
5940                    let n_cols = if let Some(selected) = selected {
5941                        selected.len()
5942                    } else {
5943                        schema.len()
5944                    };
5945                    (vec![], Some(&exprs[0].options), n_cols)
5946                } else {
5947                    (exprs.clone(), None, exprs.len())
5948                }
5949            },
5950            OrderByKind::All(opts) => {
5951                let n_cols = if let Some(selected) = selected {
5952                    selected.len()
5953                } else {
5954                    schema.len()
5955                };
5956                (vec![], Some(opts), n_cols)
5957            },
5958        };
5959        let mut descending = Vec::with_capacity(n_order_cols);
5960        let mut nulls_last = Vec::with_capacity(n_order_cols);
5961        let mut by: Vec<Expr> = Vec::with_capacity(n_order_cols);
5962
5963        if let Some(opts) = order_by_all {
5964            if let Some(selected) = selected {
5965                by.extend(selected.iter().cloned());
5966            } else {
5967                by.extend(columns_iter);
5968            };
5969            let options = order_by_sort_options(opts);
5970            nulls_last.resize(by.len(), options.nulls_last);
5971            descending.resize(by.len(), options.descending);
5972        } else {
5973            let columns = &columns_iter.collect::<Vec<_>>();
5974            // A fresh set: the final projection has already dropped the columns any
5975            // earlier pass materialised.
5976            let mut bindings = SubqueryBindings::new();
5977            for ob in order_by {
5978                let options = order_by_sort_options(&ob.options);
5979                nulls_last.push(options.nulls_last);
5980                descending.push(options.descending);
5981
5982                let lowered;
5983                (lf, lowered) = self.lower_correlated_subqueries(
5984                    lf,
5985                    &schema,
5986                    &ob.expr,
5987                    LowerScope::ScalarAndPredicates,
5988                    &mut bindings,
5989                    None,
5990                )?;
5991
5992                // The lowered expression reads the columns that lowering added.
5993                let lowered_schema = match &lowered {
5994                    Cow::Owned(_) => self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?,
5995                    Cow::Borrowed(_) => schema.clone(),
5996                };
5997                // translate order expression, allowing ordinal values
5998                by.push(self.marking_aggregates(|ctx| {
5999                    ctx.expr_or_ordinal(
6000                        &lowered,
6001                        columns,
6002                        selected,
6003                        Some(&lowered_schema),
6004                        "ORDER BY",
6005                    )
6006                })?)
6007            }
6008        }
6009
6010        let mut by: Vec<Expr> = by.into_iter().map(strip_aggregate_marks).collect();
6011        let subquery_names;
6012        (lf, subquery_names) =
6013            self.process_subqueries(lf, by.iter_mut().collect(), SubqueryShape::Broadcast)?;
6014
6015        let sorted = lf.sort_by_exprs(
6016            &by,
6017            SortMultipleOptions::default()
6018                .with_order_descending_multi(descending)
6019                .with_nulls_last_multi(nulls_last),
6020        );
6021        Ok(drop_subquery_placeholders(sorted, subquery_names))
6022    }
6023
6024    /// Point every aggregate restated in `ORDER BY` at the column that holds it.
6025    ///
6026    /// One the `SELECT` list already computes is reached by its output name;
6027    /// any other is returned for the `GROUP BY` to add.
6028    fn resolve_order_by_aggregates(
6029        &mut self,
6030        order_by: &Option<OrderBy>,
6031        projections: &[Expr],
6032        schema: &Schema,
6033        stored_keys: &[(Expr, PlSmallStr)],
6034    ) -> PolarsResult<ResolvedOrderBy> {
6035        let mut clause = order_by.clone();
6036        let mut extra: Vec<(PlSmallStr, Expr)> = Vec::new();
6037
6038        if let Some(OrderBy {
6039            kind: OrderByKind::Expressions(exprs),
6040            ..
6041        }) = &mut clause
6042        {
6043            let output_names = OutputNames::new(projections, schema, schema);
6044            let output_schema = output_names.extend_schema(schema);
6045            for ob in exprs {
6046                // Anything without an aggregate or a computed key already resolves
6047                // against the aggregated frame.
6048                let Ok(parsed) = self
6049                    .marking_aggregates(|ctx| parse_sql_expr(&ob.expr, ctx, Some(&output_schema)))
6050                else {
6051                    continue;
6052                };
6053                if !has_expr(&parsed, |e| {
6054                    is_marked_aggregate(e)
6055                        || matches!(e, Expr::Agg(_) | Expr::Len)
6056                        || stored_keys.iter().any(|(key, _)| key == e)
6057                }) {
6058                    continue;
6059                }
6060                let parsed = output_names.resolve(strip_outer_alias(&parsed));
6061                let name = match projections.iter().find(|p| strip_outer_alias(p) == parsed) {
6062                    Some(projection) => projection.to_field(schema)?.name,
6063                    None => {
6064                        let name = format_pl_smallstr!("__POLARS_ORDERAGG_{}", extra.len());
6065                        extra.push((name.clone(), parsed.alias(name.clone())));
6066                        name
6067                    },
6068                };
6069                ob.expr = SQLExpr::Identifier(Ident::new(name.as_str()));
6070            }
6071        }
6072        Ok((clause, extra))
6073    }
6074
6075    /// Translate one `GROUP BY` item, resolving SELECT aliases and, for the clause
6076    /// itself, ordinal values. A `GROUPING()` argument is an expression to match
6077    /// against the keys, so an integer there is a literal.
6078    fn resolve_group_by_key(
6079        &mut self,
6080        e: &SQLExpr,
6081        projections: &[Expr],
6082        schema: &Schema,
6083        allow_ordinal: bool,
6084    ) -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
6085        let resolve = |ctx: &mut Self, e: &SQLExpr| {
6086            if allow_ordinal {
6087                ctx.expr_or_ordinal(e, projections, None, Some(schema), "GROUP BY")
6088            } else {
6089                parse_sql_expr(e, ctx, Some(schema))
6090            }
6091        };
6092        match e {
6093            SQLExpr::Identifier(ident) => {
6094                match resolve_select_alias(&ident.value, projections, schema) {
6095                    Some(aliased) => Ok(aliased),
6096                    None => resolve(self, e),
6097                }
6098            },
6099            // A constant key, as `GROUP BY 'all'`; numbers are ordinals.
6100            SQLExpr::Value(ValueWithSpan { value, .. })
6101                if !matches!(value, SQLValue::Number(..)) =>
6102            {
6103                parse_sql_expr(e, self, Some(schema))
6104            },
6105            // Drop the alias that restores the unqualified name, so two
6106            // relations sharing a column name give distinct keys.
6107            SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(_) => resolve(self, e).map(|e| strip_outer_alias(&e)),
6108            _ => resolve(self, e),
6109        }
6110    }
6111
6112    /// Bind the grouping sets and every `GROUPING()` call of the block to the
6113    /// resolved keys. A plain `GROUP BY` that uses `GROUPING()` is a single set
6114    /// holding every key.
6115    fn bind_grouping_sets(
6116        &mut self,
6117        group_by_keys: &[Expr],
6118        grouping_sets: Option<Vec<Vec<usize>>>,
6119        projections: &[Expr],
6120        schema: &Schema,
6121        order_by: &Option<OrderBy>,
6122    ) -> PolarsResult<Option<GroupingSets>> {
6123        // Calls in clauses parsed after aggregation must be registered before the
6124        // branches are built; their validation happens when those clauses are parsed.
6125        let order_by_exprs = match order_by {
6126            Some(OrderBy {
6127                kind: OrderByKind::Expressions(exprs),
6128                ..
6129            }) => exprs.iter().map(|ob| &ob.expr).collect(),
6130            _ => vec![],
6131        };
6132        for expr in order_by_exprs {
6133            for args in collect_grouping_calls(expr) {
6134                self.register_grouping_call(args);
6135            }
6136        }
6137        let sets = match grouping_sets {
6138            Some(sets) => sets,
6139            None if self.group_scope.grouping_calls.is_empty() => return Ok(None),
6140            None => vec![(0..group_by_keys.len()).collect()],
6141        };
6142        // Later parses of the same calls must still find these registrations.
6143        let calls = std::mem::take(&mut self.group_scope.grouping_calls);
6144        let resolved_args = calls
6145            .iter()
6146            .map(|call| {
6147                call.args
6148                    .iter()
6149                    .map(|arg| self.resolve_group_by_key(arg, projections, schema, false))
6150                    .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()
6151            })
6152            .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>();
6153        self.group_scope.grouping_calls = calls;
6154        let grouping = GroupingSets::new(
6155            group_by_keys.to_vec(),
6156            sets,
6157            &self.group_scope.grouping_calls,
6158            resolved_args?,
6159        )?;
6160        Ok(Some(grouping))
6161    }
6162
6163    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
6164    fn process_group_by(
6165        &mut self,
6166        mut lf: LazyFrame,
6167        group_by_keys: &[Expr],
6168        projections: Vec<Expr>,
6169        explicit_aliases: &[bool],
6170        having: Option<Expr>,
6171        qualify: Option<(PlSmallStr, Expr)>,
6172        order_by: &Option<OrderBy>,
6173        grouping: Option<&GroupingSets>,
6174        subquery_names: &PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>,
6175    ) -> PolarsResult<(LazyFrame, Vec<PlSmallStr>, Option<OrderBy>)> {
6176        // Ordinary grouping stores each computed key in a hidden column. The other
6177        // expressions read that column, as the key's output name can be taken by
6178        // an input column or by another key.
6179        let mut stored_keys: Vec<(Expr, PlSmallStr)> = Vec::new();
6180        let column_keys: Vec<Expr>;
6181        let group_by_keys = if grouping.is_none() {
6182            let mut prepared = Vec::new();
6183            column_keys = group_by_keys
6184                .iter()
6185                .map(|key| {
6186                    let stripped = strip_outer_alias(key);
6187                    if matches!(stripped, Expr::Column(_)) || is_constant(&stripped) {
6188                        return key.clone();
6189                    }
6190                    let name = unique_column_name();
6191                    prepared.push(stripped.clone().alias(name.clone()));
6192                    stored_keys.push((stripped, name.clone()));
6193                    col(name)
6194                })
6195                .collect();
6196            if !prepared.is_empty() {
6197                lf = lf.with_columns(prepared);
6198            }
6199            &column_keys[..]
6200        } else {
6201            group_by_keys
6202        };
6203        let mut schema_before = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
6204        let key_schema =
6205            expressions_to_schema(group_by_keys, &schema_before, |duplicate_name: &str| {
6206                format!("group_by keys contained duplicate output name '{duplicate_name}'")
6207            })?;
6208        if let Some(grouping) = grouping {
6209            stored_keys = grouping.stored_keys(&key_schema);
6210        }
6211        let mut group_by_keys_schema = key_schema.clone();
6212        // Columns the parsed expressions may name before the aggregation resolves them:
6213        // the whole-frame window partition, and `GROUPING()` values, which are
6214        // per-set constants the projections treat like group keys.
6215        let whole_frame_partition = self.group_scope.whole_frame_partition.clone();
6216        let placeholders: Vec<PlSmallStr> = grouping
6217            .map(|g| g.placeholders().cloned().collect())
6218            .unwrap_or_default();
6219        if whole_frame_partition.is_some() || !placeholders.is_empty() {
6220            let mut extended = Arc::unwrap_or_clone(schema_before);
6221            if let Some(partition) = &whole_frame_partition {
6222                extended.with_column(partition.clone(), DataType::Int32);
6223            }
6224            for placeholder in &placeholders {
6225                extended.with_column(placeholder.clone(), DataType::Int64);
6226                group_by_keys_schema.with_column(placeholder.clone(), DataType::Int64);
6227            }
6228            schema_before = Arc::new(extended);
6229        }
6230
6231        // Disambiguate SELECT-list output-name collisions.
6232        let projections = disambiguate_output_names(
6233            projections
6234                .into_iter()
6235                .zip(explicit_aliases.iter().copied())
6236                .collect(),
6237            &schema_before,
6238        )?;
6239        // Hidden output columns: the ORDER BY items with aggregates or computed keys, and
6240        // the QUALIFY predicate that the block filters on after the aggregation.
6241        let (order_by, mut extra_projections) =
6242            self.resolve_order_by_aggregates(order_by, &projections, &schema_before, &stored_keys)?;
6243        let projections = if grouping.is_none() && !stored_keys.is_empty() {
6244            projections
6245                .into_iter()
6246                .map(|p| {
6247                    let stripped = strip_outer_alias(&p);
6248                    let bound = bind_stored_keys(stripped.clone(), &stored_keys);
6249                    Ok(if bound == stripped {
6250                        p
6251                    } else {
6252                        bound.alias(p.to_field(&schema_before)?.name)
6253                    })
6254                })
6255                .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?
6256        } else {
6257            projections
6258        };
6259
6260        let projections: Vec<Expr> = projections
6261            .into_iter()
6262            .map(reduce_correlated_cols_in_group_context)
6263            .collect();
6264
6265        // Note: HAVING is evaluated in the group context (`group_by().having(...)` for
6266        // ordinary grouping, a post-union filter for grouping sets), so any reference
6267        // to a SELECT alias is resolved to the aggregate it names.
6268        let mut having = having.map(|having_expr| {
6269            let having_expr = having_expr.map_expr(|e| match &e {
6270                Expr::Column(name) => resolve_select_alias(name, &projections, &schema_before)
6271                    .map_or(e, |resolved| strip_outer_alias(&resolved)),
6272                _ => e,
6273            });
6274            let having_expr = match grouping {
6275                // Grouping sets bind the keys once HAVING runs on the combined rows.
6276                Some(_) => having_expr,
6277                None => bind_stored_keys(having_expr, &stored_keys),
6278            };
6279            reduce_correlated_cols_in_group_context(having_expr)
6280        });
6281
6282        // Resolve scalar subqueries in HAVING and the ORDER BY aggregates against the
6283        // pre-aggregation frame.
6284        let new_subquery_names;
6285        let mut exprs: Vec<&mut Expr> = extra_projections.iter_mut().map(|(_, e)| e).collect();
6286        exprs.extend(having.as_mut());
6287        (lf, new_subquery_names) = self.process_subqueries(lf, exprs, SubqueryShape::Scalar)?;
6288        if !new_subquery_names.is_empty() {
6289            let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
6290            let schema_before = Arc::make_mut(&mut schema_before);
6291            for name in &new_subquery_names {
6292                schema_before.with_column(name.clone(), schema.get(name).unwrap().clone());
6293            }
6294        }
6295        for e in extra_projections
6296            .iter_mut()
6297            .map(|(_, e)| e)
6298            .chain(having.as_mut())
6299        {
6300            *e = broadcast_subqueries_in_inputs(
6301                e.clone(),
6302                &new_subquery_names,
6303                &self.group_scope.subqueries_read_per_row,
6304            );
6305        }
6306        let mut subquery_names = subquery_names.clone();
6307        subquery_names.extend(new_subquery_names);
6308
6309        extra_projections
6310            .extend(qualify.map(|(name, e)| (name, reduce_correlated_cols_in_group_context(e))));
6311
6312        // Note: remove the `group_by` keys as Polars adds those implicitly.
6313        let mut aliased_aggregations: PlHashMap<PlSmallStr, PlSmallStr> = PlHashMap::new();
6314        let mut post_agg_projection: Vec<Expr> = Vec::new();
6315        let mut projection_overrides = PlHashMap::with_capacity(projections.len());
6316        let mut projection_aliases = PlHashSet::new();
6317        let mut group_key_aliases = PlHashSet::new();
6318
6319        // Pre-compute group key data (alias-stripped expression + aggregated output
6320        // name) to avoid repeated work matching projections against the group keys
6321        let group_key_data: Vec<_> = group_by_keys
6322            .iter()
6323            .map(|gk| {
6324                (
6325                    strip_outer_alias(gk),
6326                    gk.to_field(&schema_before).ok().map(|f| f.name),
6327                )
6328            })
6329            .collect();
6330
6331        // ORDER BY extras were parsed above and may have registered the partition.
6332        let whole_frame_partition = self.group_scope.whole_frame_partition.clone();
6333        let mut splitter = GroupContextSplitter {
6334            keys: &group_by_keys_schema,
6335            key_exprs: group_key_data
6336                .iter()
6337                .filter_map(|(key, name)| Some((key.clone(), name.clone()?)))
6338                .chain(match grouping {
6339                    Some(_) => vec![],
6340                    None => stored_keys.clone(),
6341                })
6342                .collect(),
6343            whole_frame_partition: whole_frame_partition.as_ref(),
6344            subquery_names: &subquery_names,
6345            subqueries_after_aggregation: grouping.is_none() && group_by_keys.is_empty(),
6346            subqueries_read_after: PlIndexSet::new(),
6347            aggregates: AggregateOutputs::with_capacity(projections.len()),
6348        };
6349        if let Some(having) = &having {
6350            splitter.check_columns_per_group(having)?;
6351        }
6352        // Post-aggregation expressions read computed keys from their stored columns.
6353        let bind_keys = |e: Expr| bind_stored_keys(e, &stored_keys);
6354
6355        let projection_group_key: Vec<Option<PlSmallStr>> = projections
6356            .iter()
6357            .map(|p| {
6358                let p_stripped = strip_outer_alias(p);
6359                group_key_data.iter().find_map(|(gk_stripped, gk_name)| {
6360                    (*gk_stripped == p_stripped)
6361                        .then(|| gk_name.clone())
6362                        .flatten()
6363                })
6364            })
6365            .collect();
6366
6367        for (e, group_key) in projections.iter().zip(&projection_group_key) {
6368            let matches_group_key = group_key.is_some();
6369            let is_non_group_key_expr = !matches_group_key && splitter.requires_group_processing(e);
6370
6371            // Note: if simple aliased expression we defer aliasing until after the group_by.
6372            // Use `e_inner` to track the potentially unwrapped expression for field lookup.
6373            let mut e_inner = e;
6374            if let Expr::Alias(expr, alias) = e {
6375                if e.clone().meta().is_simple_projection(Some(&schema_before)) {
6376                    group_key_aliases.insert(alias.as_ref());
6377                    e_inner = expr
6378                } else if let Expr::Function {
6379                    function: FunctionExpr::StructExpr(StructFunction::FieldByName(name)),
6380                    ..
6381                } = expr.deref()
6382                {
6383                    projection_overrides
6384                        .insert(alias.as_ref(), col(name.clone()).alias(alias.clone()));
6385                } else if !is_non_group_key_expr && !group_by_keys_schema.contains(alias) {
6386                    projection_aliases.insert(alias.as_ref());
6387                }
6388            }
6389            let field = e_inner.to_field(&schema_before)?;
6390            if is_non_group_key_expr {
6391                splitter.check_columns_per_group(e)?;
6392                // Window functions run on the aggregated frame; only the aggregates
6393                // inside them run in the group context. The same holds for anything
6394                // combining aggregates with grouped keys or `GROUPING()` values.
6395                let bound = bind_keys(strip_outer_alias(e));
6396                if splitter.needs_post_aggregation(&bound) {
6397                    let post_agg_expr = splitter.hoist(bound)?;
6398                    post_agg_projection.push(post_agg_expr.alias(field.name.clone()));
6399                    continue;
6400                }
6401                let mut e = e.clone();
6402                // If aggregation colname conflicts with a group key,
6403                // alias it to avoid duplicate/mis-tracked columns
6404                if group_by_keys_schema.get(&field.name).is_some() {
6405                    let alias_name = format_pl_smallstr!("__POLARS_AGG_{}", field.name);
6406                    e = e.alias(alias_name.clone());
6407                    aliased_aggregations.insert(field.name.clone(), alias_name);
6408                }
6409                splitter.aggregates.push(e);
6410            } else if !matches_group_key {
6411                // Non-aggregated columns must be part of the GROUP BY clause
6412                if let Expr::Column(_)
6413                | Expr::Function {
6414                    function: FunctionExpr::StructExpr(StructFunction::FieldByName(_)),
6415                    ..
6416                } = e_inner
6417                {
6418                    if !group_by_keys_schema.contains(&field.name) {
6419                        polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "'{}' should participate in the GROUP BY clause or an aggregate function", &field.name);
6420                    }
6421                } else {
6422                    splitter.check_columns_per_group(e_inner)?;
6423                }
6424            }
6425        }
6426
6427        for (name, e) in &extra_projections {
6428            let bound = bind_keys(strip_outer_alias(e));
6429            if splitter.needs_post_aggregation(&bound) {
6430                let rest = splitter.hoist(bound)?;
6431                post_agg_projection.push(rest.alias(name.clone()));
6432            } else if !splitter.requires_group_processing(&bound) {
6433                post_agg_projection.push(bound.alias(name.clone()));
6434            } else {
6435                splitter.aggregates.push(e.clone());
6436            }
6437        }
6438
6439        if let Some(grouping) = grouping {
6440            polars_ensure!(
6441                !splitter.aggregates.iter().any(|e| grouping.contains_placeholder(e)),
6442                SQLSyntax: "GROUPING() cannot be used inside an aggregate function"
6443            );
6444        }
6445
6446        // With GROUP BY, HAVING runs per group or before the projections, so a `RANDOM()`
6447        // outside its aggregates would not be the value the SELECT list shows.
6448        polars_ensure!(
6449            (grouping.is_none() && group_by_keys.is_empty())
6450                || !having.as_ref().is_some_and(has_random_outside_aggregates),
6451            SQLInterface: "RANDOM() outside an aggregate in HAVING is not supported with GROUP BY"
6452        );
6453        let aggregated = match grouping {
6454            None if group_by_keys.is_empty() => {
6455                // Without GROUP BY there is one aggregated row, which HAVING filters.
6456                let having = having.map(|having| splitter.hoist(having)).transpose()?;
6457                let mut aggregates = splitter.aggregates.into_exprs();
6458                // The row also exists when nothing is aggregated, as in `SELECT 1 ... HAVING`.
6459                if aggregates.is_empty() {
6460                    aggregates.push(len());
6461                }
6462                let mut aggregated = lf.select(aggregates);
6463                if !splitter.subqueries_read_after.is_empty() {
6464                    let mut frames = vec![aggregated];
6465                    frames.extend(
6466                        splitter
6467                            .subqueries_read_after
6468                            .iter()
6469                            .map(|name| self.group_scope.subquery_plans[name].clone()),
6470                    );
6471                    aggregated = concat_lf_horizontal(
6472                        frames,
6473                        HConcatOptions {
6474                            broadcast_unit_length: true,
6475                            ..Default::default()
6476                        },
6477                    )?;
6478                }
6479                match having {
6480                    Some(having) => aggregated.filter(having.cast(DataType::Boolean)),
6481                    None => aggregated,
6482                }
6483            },
6484            None => {
6485                // With a column key, every group has a row. A group-by on scalar keys only runs
6486                // as a select over all rows, which may be none.
6487                let has_column_key = group_by_keys
6488                    .iter()
6489                    .any(|key| matches!(strip_outer_alias(key), Expr::Column(_)));
6490                let in_groups = |e: Expr| {
6491                    if has_column_key {
6492                        assume_groups_have_rows(e)
6493                    } else {
6494                        e
6495                    }
6496                };
6497                let mut group_by = lf.group_by(group_by_keys);
6498                if !has_column_key {
6499                    // That select returns a row even when there are no input rows.
6500                    group_by = group_by.having(len().gt(lit(0)));
6501                }
6502                match having {
6503                    Some(having) => group_by.having(in_groups(strip_aggregate_marks(
6504                        splitter.read_keys_per_group(having),
6505                    ))),
6506                    None => group_by,
6507                }
6508                .agg(
6509                    splitter
6510                        .aggregates
6511                        .into_exprs()
6512                        .into_iter()
6513                        .map(in_groups)
6514                        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
6515                )
6516            },
6517            Some(grouping) => {
6518                // HAVING runs on the combined rows, where it can also see `GROUPING()`.
6519                let having = having
6520                    .map(|having| {
6521                        let having = bind_stored_keys(having, &stored_keys);
6522                        splitter.hoist(having)
6523                    })
6524                    .transpose()?;
6525                let aggregation_projection = splitter.aggregates.into_exprs();
6526                let agg_names = aggregation_projection
6527                    .iter()
6528                    .map(|e| Ok(e.to_field(&schema_before)?.name))
6529                    .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
6530                let aggregated =
6531                    grouping.aggregate(lf, &key_schema, &aggregation_projection, &agg_names)?;
6532                match having {
6533                    Some(having) => aggregated.filter(having.cast(DataType::Boolean)),
6534                    None => aggregated,
6535                }
6536            },
6537        };
6538
6539        let aggregated = if post_agg_projection.is_empty() {
6540            aggregated
6541        } else {
6542            aggregated.with_columns(&post_agg_projection)
6543        };
6544
6545        let projection_schema =
6546            expressions_to_schema(&projections, &schema_before, |duplicate_name: &str| {
6547                format!("group_by aggregations contained duplicate output name '{duplicate_name}'")
6548            })?;
6549
6550        // A final projection to get the proper order and any deferred transforms/aliases
6551        // (will also drop any temporary columns created for the HAVING post-filter)
6552        let final_projection = projection_schema
6553            .iter_names()
6554            .zip(projections.iter().zip(&projection_group_key))
6555            .map(|(name, (projection_expr, group_key))| {
6556                if let Some(expr) = projection_overrides.get(name.as_str()) {
6557                    expr.clone()
6558                } else if let Some(aliased_name) = aliased_aggregations.get(name) {
6559                    col(aliased_name.clone()).alias(name.clone())
6560                } else if let Some(key_name) = group_key {
6561                    // projection is a group key; reference aggregated key col rather than
6562                    // re-evaluating against aggregated frame (incorrect for computed keys)
6563                    if key_name == name {
6564                        col(name.clone())
6565                    } else {
6566                        col(key_name.clone()).alias(name.clone())
6567                    }
6568                } else if group_by_keys_schema.get(name).is_some()
6569                    || projection_aliases.contains(name.as_str())
6570                    || group_key_aliases.contains(name.as_str())
6571                {
6572                    if has_expr(projection_expr, |e| {
6573                        matches!(e, Expr::Agg(_) | Expr::Len | Expr::Over { .. })
6574                    }) {
6575                        col(name.clone())
6576                    } else {
6577                        bind_keys(projection_expr.clone())
6578                    }
6579                } else if is_constant(projection_expr) {
6580                    // Constants are not part of the aggregation; re-evaluate them.
