6581                    projection_expr.clone()
6582                } else {
6583                    col(name.clone())
6584                }
6585            })
6586            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
6587
6588        // Include original GROUP BY columns for ORDER BY access (if aliased).
6589        let mut output_projection = final_projection;
6590        let mut output_names: Vec<PlSmallStr> = projection_schema.iter_names_cloned().collect();
6591        let mut push_hidden = |expr: Expr, name: PlSmallStr| {
6592            output_projection.push(expr);
6593            output_names.push(name);
6594        };
6595        for (name, _) in &extra_projections {
6596            push_hidden(col(name.clone()), name.clone());
6597        }
6598        for key_name in group_by_keys_schema.iter_names() {
6599            if !projection_schema.contains(key_name) {
6600                // Original col name not in output - add for ORDER BY access
6601                push_hidden(col(key_name.clone()), key_name.clone());
6602            } else if group_by_keys.iter().any(|k| is_simple_col_ref(k, key_name)) {
6603                // Original col name in output - check if cross-aliased
6604                let is_cross_aliased = projection_schema
6605                    .iter_names()
6606                    .zip(projections.iter())
6607                    .any(|(name, p)| name == key_name && !is_simple_col_ref(p, key_name));
6608                if is_cross_aliased {
6609                    // Add original name under a prefixed alias for subsequent ORDER BY resolution
6610                    let internal_name = format_pl_smallstr!("__POLARS_ORIG_{}", key_name);
6611                    push_hidden(
6612                        col(key_name.clone()).alias(internal_name.clone()),
6613                        internal_name,
6614                    );
6615                }
6616            }
6617        }
6618        // A literal-only projection (`SELECT 1 ... GROUP BY ()` or `SELECT 1 ... HAVING`)
6619        // must keep the height of the aggregated rows, so the columns are added before the
6620        // frame is narrowed.
6621        let projected = if grouping.is_some() || group_by_keys.is_empty() {
6622            aggregated
6623                .with_columns(&output_projection)
6624                .select(output_names.into_iter().map(col).collect::<Vec<_>>())
6625        } else {
6626            aggregated.select(&output_projection)
6627        };
6628        Ok((
6629            projected,
6630            projection_schema.iter_names_cloned().collect(),
6631            order_by,
6632        ))
6633    }
6634
6635    fn process_limit_offset(
6636        &mut self,
6637        lf: LazyFrame,
6638        limit_clause: &Option<LimitClause>,
6639        fetch: &Option<Fetch>,
6640    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
6641        // Extract limit and offset from LimitClause
6642        let (limit, offset) = match limit_clause {
6643            Some(LimitClause::LimitOffset {
6644                limit,
6645                offset,
6646                limit_by,
6647            }) => {
6648                if !limit_by.is_empty() {
6649                    // TODO: might be able to support as an aggregate `top_k_by` operation?
6650                    //  (https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select/limit-by)
6651                    polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "`LIMIT <n> BY <exprs>` clause is not supported");
6652                }
6653                (limit.as_ref(), offset.as_ref().map(|o| &o.value))
6654            },
6655            Some(LimitClause::OffsetCommaLimit { offset, limit }) => (Some(limit), Some(offset)),
6656            None => (None, None),
6657        };
6658
6659        // Handle FETCH clause (alternative to LIMIT, mutually exclusive); without a
6660        // quantity it fetches one row.
6661        let one_row = SQLExpr::value(SQLValue::Number("1".to_string(), false));
6662        let limit = match (fetch, limit) {
6663            (Some(fetch), None) => Some(fetch.quantity.as_ref().unwrap_or(&one_row)),
6664            (Some(_), Some(_)) => {
6665                polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "cannot use both `LIMIT` and `FETCH` in the same query")
6666            },
6667            (None, limit) => limit,
6668        };
6669
6670        // Apply limit and/or offset
6671        let number = |expr: &SQLExpr| match expr {
6672            SQLExpr::Value(ValueWithSpan {
6673                value: SQLValue::Number(n, _),
6674                ..
6675            }) => Some(n.clone()),
6676            _ => None,
6677        };
6678        let offset_literal = offset.map(|e| number(e).and_then(|n| n.parse::<i64>().ok()));
6679        let limit_literal = limit.map(|e| number(e).and_then(|n| n.parse::<IdxSize>().ok()));
6680        match (offset_literal, limit_literal) {
6681            (Some(Some(offset)), Some(Some(limit))) => Ok(lf.slice(offset, limit)),
6682            (Some(Some(offset)), None) => Ok(lf.slice(offset, IdxSize::MAX)),
6683            (None, Some(Some(limit))) => Ok(lf.limit(limit)),
6684            (None, None) => Ok(lf),
6685            _ => self.slice_by_exprs(lf, offset, limit),
6686        }
6687    }
6688
6689    /// Apply LIMIT/OFFSET values other than integer literals, such as scalar subqueries.
6690    /// A value is a row count: a float rounds half to even and a decimal half away from
6691    /// zero, a negative one raises, a NULL limit is no limit and a NULL offset is 0.
6692    fn slice_by_exprs(
6693        &mut self,
6694        mut lf: LazyFrame,
6695        offset: Option<&SQLExpr>,
6696        limit: Option<&SQLExpr>,
6697    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
6698        let columns: Vec<Expr> = self
6699            .get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?
6700            .iter_names()
6701            .cloned()
6702            .map(Expr::Column)
6703            .collect();
6704        let mut parse = |expr: &SQLExpr| -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
6705            check_query_independent_value(expr, self)?;
6706            parse_sql_expr(expr, self, Some(&Schema::default()))
6707        };
6708        let mut offset = offset.map(&mut parse).transpose()?;
6709        let mut limit = limit.map(&mut parse).transpose()?;
6710        let (mut frame, placeholders) = self.process_subqueries(
6711            lf,
6712            offset.iter_mut().chain(limit.iter_mut()).collect(),
6713            SubqueryShape::Scalar,
6714        )?;
6715        let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut frame)?;
6716        let row_count = |value: Expr| -> PolarsResult<Expr> {
6717            polars_ensure!(
6718                expr_to_leaf_column_names_iter(&value).all(|name| placeholders.contains(&name)),
6719                SQLSyntax: "LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH cannot reference columns"
6720            );
6721            let value = match value.to_field(&schema)?.dtype {
6722                dtype if dtype.is_integer() || dtype.is_null() => value,
6723                DataType::Float32 | DataType::Float64 => value.round(0, RoundMode::HalfToEven),
6724                DataType::Decimal(_, _) => value.round(0, RoundMode::HalfAwayFromZero),
6725                DataType::String => value.strict_cast(DataType::Int64),
6726                dtype => polars_bail!(
6727                    SQLSyntax: "LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH must be a number, found {}", dtype
6728                ),
6729            };
6730            Ok(value
6731                .strict_cast(DataType::UInt64)
6732                .strict_cast(DataType::Int64))
6733        };
6734        let offset = match offset {
6735            Some(offset) => row_count(offset)?.fill_null(lit(0i64)),
6736            None => lit(0i64),
6737        };
6738        let length = match limit {
6739            Some(limit) => row_count(limit)?,
6740            None => lit(NULL).cast(DataType::Int64),
6741        };
6742        Ok(frame.select(
6743            columns
6744                .into_iter()
6745                .map(|column| column.slice(offset.clone(), length.clone()))
6746                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
6747        ))
6748    }
6749
6750    fn process_qualified_wildcard(
6751        &mut self,
6752        ObjectName(idents): &ObjectName,
6753        options: &WildcardAdditionalOptions,
6754        schema: &Schema,
6755    ) -> PolarsResult<Vec<Expr>> {
6756        let mut idents_with_wildcard: Vec<Ident> = idents
6757            .iter()
6758            .filter_map(|p| p.as_ident().cloned())
6759            .collect();
6760        idents_with_wildcard.push(Ident::new("*"));
6761
6762        let exprs = resolve_compound_identifier(self, &idents_with_wildcard, Some(schema))?;
6763        self.process_wildcard_additional_options(exprs, options, schema)
6764    }
6765
6766    /// Apply the options of a wildcard to the columns it selects, in this order: `EXCLUDE`,
6767    /// `EXCEPT` and `ILIKE` drop columns, then `REPLACE` changes them, then `RENAME` renames
6768    /// them.
6769    fn process_wildcard_additional_options(
6770        &mut self,
6771        exprs: Vec<Expr>,
6772        options: &WildcardAdditionalOptions,
6773        schema: &Schema,
6774    ) -> PolarsResult<Vec<Expr>> {
6775        if options.opt_except.is_some() && options.opt_exclude.is_some() {
6776            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "EXCLUDE and EXCEPT wildcard options cannot be used together (prefer EXCLUDE)")
6777        } else if options.opt_exclude.is_some() && options.opt_ilike.is_some() {
6778            polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "EXCLUDE and ILIKE wildcard options cannot be used together")
6779        }
6780
6781        // SELECT * EXCLUDE
6782        let mut exclude = PlHashSet::new();
6783        if let Some(items) = &options.opt_exclude {
6784            match items {
6785                ExcludeSelectItem::Single(name) => {
6786                    exclude.insert(object_name_to_string(name));
6787                },
6788                ExcludeSelectItem::Multiple(names) => {
6789                    exclude.extend(names.iter().map(object_name_to_string));
6790                },
6791            };
6792        }
6793
6794        // SELECT * EXCEPT
6795        if let Some(items) = &options.opt_except {
6796            exclude.insert(items.first_element.value.clone());
6797            exclude.extend(items.additional_elements.iter().map(|i| i.value.clone()));
6798        }
6799
6800        // SELECT * ILIKE
6801        let ilike = options.opt_ilike.as_ref().map(|item| {
6802            let rx = regex::escape(item.pattern.as_str())
6803                .replace('%', ".*")
6804                .replace('_', ".");
6805            polars_utils::regex_cache::compile_regex(format!("^(?is){rx}$").as_str()).unwrap()
6806        });
6807
6808        // Each column keeps its name in the wildcard, also after a rename, so
6809        // `RENAME (a AS b, b AS c)` renames the input `b` and not the renamed `a`.
6810        let mut named_exprs = Vec::with_capacity(exprs.len());
6811        for expr in exprs {
6812            let name = expr.to_field(schema)?.name;
6813            if !exclude.contains(name.as_str())
6814                && ilike.as_ref().is_none_or(|rx| rx.is_match(&name))
6815            {
6816                named_exprs.push((name, expr));
6817            }
6818        }
6819
6820        // SELECT * REPLACE
6821        if let Some(replacements) = &options.opt_replace {
6822            for rp in &replacements.items {
6823                let name = rp.column_name.value.as_str();
6824                let Some((_, expr)) = named_exprs.iter_mut().find(|(n, _)| n == name) else {
6825                    polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "REPLACE column '{}' is not selected by the wildcard", name)
6826                };
6827                *expr = parse_sql_expr(&rp.expr, self, Some(schema))?.alias(name);
6828            }
6829        }
6830
6831        // SELECT * RENAME
6832        if let Some(items) = &options.opt_rename {
6833            let renames = match items {
6834                RenameSelectItem::Single(rename) => std::slice::from_ref(rename),
6835                RenameSelectItem::Multiple(renames) => renames.as_slice(),
6836            };
6837            for rn in renames {
6838                let before = rn.ident.value.as_str();
6839                if let Some((_, expr)) = named_exprs.iter_mut().find(|(n, _)| n == before) {
6840                    *expr = strip_outer_alias(expr).alias(rn.alias.value.as_str());
6841                }
6842            }
6843        }
6844        Ok(named_exprs.into_iter().map(|(_, expr)| expr).collect())
6845    }
6846
6847    fn rename_columns_from_table_alias(
6848        &mut self,
6849        mut lf: LazyFrame,
6850        alias: &TableAlias,
6851    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame> {
6852        if alias.columns.is_empty() {
6853            Ok(lf)
6854        } else {
6855            let schema = self.get_frame_schema(&mut lf)?;
6856            if alias.columns.len() != schema.len() {
6857                polars_bail!(
6858                    SQLSyntax: "number of columns ({}) in alias '{}' does not match the number of columns in the table/query ({})",
6859                    alias.columns.len(), alias.name.value, schema.len()
6860                )
6861            } else {
6862                let existing_columns: Vec<_> = schema.iter_names().collect();
6863                let new_columns: Vec<_> =
6864                    alias.columns.iter().map(|c| c.name.value.clone()).collect();
6865                Ok(lf.rename(existing_columns, new_columns, true))
6866            }
6867        }
6868    }
6869}

6903/// Join identifier parts with dots, as relation names are spelled.
6904pub(crate) fn join_idents(idents: &[Ident]) -> String {

6906        .iter()
6907        .map(|i| i.value.as_str())
6908        .collect::<Vec<_>>()

6912/// Whether `qualifier` names `relation`: the whole name or a trailing run of its dot-separated
6913/// parts (`lineitem` and `tpch.lineitem` both name `tpch.lineitem`), ignoring case.
6914fn qualifier_names(relation: &str, qualifier: &str) -> bool {
6915    let Some(start) = relation.len().checked_sub(qualifier.len()) else {
6916        return false;
6917    };
6918    (start == 0 || relation.as_bytes()[start - 1] == b'.')
6919        && relation
6920            .get(start..)
6921            .is_some_and(|tail| tail.eq_ignore_ascii_case(qualifier))
6922}
6923
6924/// A relation's name in scope, in the parts `FROM` wrote: an alias or a quoted `"a.b"` is one
6925/// part, `tpch.lineitem` two. A catalog table, whose name is rewritten to its full name, is also
6926/// known by the name written for it at that place.
6927#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
6928pub(crate) struct RelationName {
6929    parts: Vec<String>,
6930    written: Option<Vec<String>>,
6931}
6932
6933impl RelationName {
6934    fn new(parts: Vec<String>) -> Self {
6935        Self {
6936            parts,
6937            written: None,
6938        }
6939    }
6940
6941    pub(crate) fn parts(&self) -> &[String] {
6942        &self.parts
6943    }
6944
6945    /// The dotted name, which looks the relation up and identifies it.
6946    pub(crate) fn key(&self) -> String {
6947        self.parts.join(".")
6948    }
6949
6950    /// Add the name the statement wrote at `factor` for this catalog table.
6951    pub(crate) fn spelled(mut self, factor: &TableFactor, spellings: &CatalogSpellings) -> Self {
6952        if let TableFactor::Table {
6953            name, alias: None, ..
6954        } = factor
6955            && let Some(written) = name_position(name).and_then(|at| spellings.get(&at))
6956            && *written != self.parts
6957        {
6958            self.written = Some(written.clone());
6959        }
6960        self
6961    }
6962
6963    /// Whether `qualifier` equals the trailing parts of one of the names, ignoring case unless
6964    /// `exact`.
6965    pub(crate) fn named_by(&self, qualifier: &[Ident], exact: bool) -> bool {
6966        let ends_with = |name: &[String]| {
6967            let Some(start) = name.len().checked_sub(qualifier.len()) else {
6968                return false;
6969            };
6970            name[start..].iter().zip(qualifier).all(|(part, ident)| {
6971                if exact {
6972                    *part == ident.value
6973                } else {
6974                    part.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&ident.value)
6975                }
6976            })
6977        };
6978        ends_with(&self.parts) || self.written.as_deref().is_some_and(ends_with)
6979    }
6980}
6981
6982/// The relations that the longest leading run of `idents` (leaving at least one part) names,
6983/// with the run's length. Exact-case matches win over those equal only ignoring case.
6984pub(crate) fn match_qualifier<'a>(
6985    idents: &[Ident],
6986    relations: impl Iterator<Item = &'a RelationName> + Clone,
6987) -> Option<(Vec<&'a RelationName>, usize)> {
6988    (1..idents.len()).rev().find_map(|len| {
6989        let qualifier = &idents[..len];
6990        let matches: Vec<&RelationName> = relations
6991            .clone()
6992            .filter(|relation| relation.named_by(qualifier, false))
6993            .collect();
6994        let exact: Vec<&RelationName> = matches
6995            .iter()
6996            .copied()
6997            .filter(|relation| relation.named_by(qualifier, true))
6998            .collect();
6999        match (exact.is_empty(), matches.is_empty()) {
7000            (false, _) => Some((exact, len)),
7001            (true, false) => Some((matches, len)),
7002            (true, true) => None,
7003        }
7004    })
7005}
7006
7007/// Error for a qualifier naming several relations in scope.
7008fn ambiguous_relation_err(qualifier: &str, relations: &[&RelationName]) -> PolarsError {
7009    let distinct: PlIndexSet<String> = relations.iter().map(|r| r.key()).collect();
7010    if distinct.len() < relations.len() {
7011        polars_err!(
7012            SQLInterface: "ambiguous reference to table \"{}\" (it appears more than once in FROM; give each an alias)",
7013            qualifier
7014        )
7015    } else {
7016        let names: Vec<String> = distinct.into_iter().collect();
7017        let (last, init) = names.split_last().unwrap();
7018        polars_err!(
7019            SQLInterface: "ambiguous reference to table \"{}\" (use: {} or {})",
7020            qualifier, init.join(", "), last
7021        )
7022    }
7023}
7024
7025/// Casts an `ASOF JOIN` key pair to one dtype. Temporal keys of different dtypes become Int128
7026/// counts of the finest time unit: a common temporal dtype would lose either precision (with the
7027/// coarser unit) or range (with the finer unit).
7028#[cfg(feature = "asof_join")]
7029fn asof_key_pair(
7030    l: Expr,
7031    l_dtype: &DataType,
7032    r: Expr,
7033    r_dtype: &DataType,
7034) -> PolarsResult<(Expr, Expr)> {
7035    if l_dtype == r_dtype {
7036        return Ok((l, r));
7037    }
7038    let supertype = try_get_supertype(l_dtype, r_dtype)?;
7039    if !matches!(supertype, DataType::Datetime(..) | DataType::Duration(_)) {
7040        return Ok((l.cast(supertype.clone()), r.cast(supertype)));
7041    }
7042    let ticks_per_second = |tu: TimeUnit| -> i64 {
7043        match tu {
7044            TimeUnit::Nanoseconds => 1_000_000_000,
7045            TimeUnit::Microseconds => 1_000_000,
7046            TimeUnit::Milliseconds => 1_000,
7047        }
7048    };
7049    let unit = [l_dtype, r_dtype]
7050        .into_iter()
7051        .filter_map(|dtype| match dtype {
7052            DataType::Datetime(tu, _) | DataType::Duration(tu) => Some(*tu),
7053            _ => None,
7054        })
7055        .max_by_key(|tu| ticks_per_second(*tu))
7056        .unwrap_or(TimeUnit::Milliseconds);
7057    let to_ticks = |e: Expr, dtype: &DataType| -> Expr {
7058        let (e, ticks_per_value) = match (dtype, &supertype) {
7059            (DataType::Datetime(tu, _) | DataType::Duration(tu), _) => {
7060                (e, ticks_per_second(unit) / ticks_per_second(*tu))
7061            },
7062            // Milliseconds hold every date without overflow.
7063            (DataType::Date, DataType::Datetime(_, tz)) => (
7064                e.cast(DataType::Datetime(TimeUnit::Milliseconds, tz.clone())),
7065                ticks_per_second(unit) / ticks_per_second(TimeUnit::Milliseconds),
7066            ),
7067            (_, DataType::Datetime(_, tz)) => (e.cast(DataType::Datetime(unit, tz.clone())), 1),
7068            _ => (e.cast(DataType::Duration(unit)), 1),
7069        };
7070        e.to_physical().cast(DataType::Int128) * lit(ticks_per_value)
7071    };
7072    Ok((to_ticks(l, l_dtype), to_ticks(r, r_dtype)))
7073}

7075/// Extract column names from a USING clause in a JoinOperator (if present).
7076fn get_using_cols(op: &JoinOperator) -> Option<impl Iterator<Item = String> + '_> {
7077    use JoinOperator::*;
7078    match op {
7079        Join(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7080        | Inner(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7081        | Left(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7082        | LeftOuter(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7083        | Right(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7084        | RightOuter(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7085        | FullOuter(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7086        | Semi(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7087        | Anti(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7088        | LeftSemi(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7089        | LeftAnti(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7090        | RightSemi(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7091        | RightAnti(JoinConstraint::Using(cols))
7092        | AsOf {
7093            constraint: JoinConstraint::Using(cols),
7094            ..
7095        } => Some(cols.iter().filter_map(|c| {
7096            c.0.first()
7097                .and_then(|p| p.as_ident())
7098                .map(|i| i.value.clone())
7099        })),
7100        _ => None,
7101    }
7102}

7104/// Look up a relation name, falling back to the only case-insensitive match (error if several).
7105fn get_ignoring_case<'a, V>(
7106    map: &'a PlHashMap<String, V>,
7107    name: &str,
7108) -> PolarsResult<Option<&'a V>> {
7109    Ok(key_ignoring_case(map, name)?.map(|key| &map[key]))
7110}
7111
7112/// The key of `map` that `name` refers to: an exact match, else the only key equal to it
7113/// ignoring case. Several keys equal to it ignoring case are an error.
7114fn key_ignoring_case<'a, V>(
7115    map: &'a PlHashMap<String, V>,
7116    name: &str,
7117) -> PolarsResult<Option<&'a String>> {
7118    if let Some((key, _)) = map.get_key_value(name) {
7119        return Ok(Some(key));
7120    }
7121    let mut matches = map.keys().filter(|key| key.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name));
7122    let first = matches.next();
7123    if matches.next().is_some() {
7124        let mut names: Vec<String> = map
7125            .keys()
7126            .filter(|key| key.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
7127            .map(|key| format!("'{key}'"))
7128            .collect();
7129        names.sort();
7130        polars_bail!(
7131            SQLInterface: "relation '{}' matches more than one table ignoring case ({}); write the name with its exact case",
7132            name, names.join(", ")
7133        );
7134    }
7135    Ok(first)
7136}

7138/// Prefix for the internal outer columns produced by correlated-subquery decorrelation.
7139pub(crate) const CORRELATED_COL_PREFIX: &str = "__POLARS_CORR_";
7140
7141pub(crate) fn is_correlated_result_col(name: &str) -> bool {

7145/// The relations of a `FROM` (see `factor_relations`).
7146pub(crate) fn declared_relations(
7147    from: &[TableWithJoins],
7148    spellings: &CatalogSpellings,
7149) -> Vec<RelationName> {
7150    from.iter()
7151        .flat_map(|tbl| factor_relations(kept_factors(tbl).into_iter(), spellings))
7152        .collect()
7153}
7154
7155/// Whether a join returns the columns of its left and of its right input.
7156fn join_keeps_inputs(op: &JoinOperator) -> (bool, bool) {
7157    match op {
7158        JoinOperator::Semi(_)
7159        | JoinOperator::LeftSemi(_)
7160        | JoinOperator::Anti(_)
7161        | JoinOperator::LeftAnti(_) => (true, false),
7162        JoinOperator::RightSemi(_) | JoinOperator::RightAnti(_) => (false, true),
7163        _ => (true, true),
7164    }
7165}
7166
7167/// The table factors of `tbl` whose columns it returns, as a semi or anti join drops one
7168/// of its inputs.
7169fn kept_factors(tbl: &TableWithJoins) -> Vec<&TableFactor> {
7170    let mut factors = vec![&tbl.relation];
7171    for join in &tbl.joins {
7172        let (keep_left, keep_right) = join_keeps_inputs(&join.join_operator);
7173        if !keep_left {
7174            factors.clear();
7175        }
7176        if keep_right {
7177            factors.push(&join.relation);
7178        }
7179    }
7180    factors
7181}
7182
7183/// The relations that table factors bring into scope. A nested join is flattened rather than
7184/// bound to its alias, so its own relations are declared too.
7185fn factor_relations<'a>(
7186    factors: impl Iterator<Item = &'a TableFactor>,
7187    spellings: &CatalogSpellings,
7188) -> Vec<RelationName> {
7189    let mut names = Vec::new();
7190    for factor in factors {
7191        let name = relation_name(factor).map(|name| name.spelled(factor, spellings));
7192        names.extend(name.clone());
7193        if let TableFactor::NestedJoin {
7194            table_with_joins, ..
7195        } = factor
7196        {
7197            // A child named like the join's alias is hidden by it, not a second occurrence.
7198            let children = declared_relations(std::slice::from_ref(table_with_joins), spellings);
7199            names.extend(
7200                children
7201                    .into_iter()
7202                    .filter(|child| Some(child) != name.as_ref()),
7203            );
7204        }
7205    }
7206    names
7207}

7209/// The name a relation is known by: its alias, else its full (possibly qualified) name.
7210pub(crate) fn get_table_name(factor: &TableFactor) -> Option<String> {
7211    relation_name(factor).map(|name| name.key())
7212}
7213
7214/// The name a relation is known by, in parts (see `RelationName`).
7215pub(crate) fn relation_name(factor: &TableFactor) -> Option<RelationName> {
7216    let alias = |alias: &Option<TableAlias>| {
7217        alias
7218            .as_ref()
7219            .map(|a| RelationName::new(vec![a.name.value.clone()]))
7220    };
7221    match factor {
7222        TableFactor::Table { name, alias: a, .. } => alias(a).or_else(|| {
7223            let parts = name.0.iter().filter_map(|p| p.as_ident());
7224            Some(RelationName::new(parts.map(|i| i.value.clone()).collect()))
7225        }),
7226        TableFactor::Derived { alias: a, .. }
7227        | TableFactor::NestedJoin { alias: a, .. }
7228        | TableFactor::TableFunction { alias: a, .. }
7229        | TableFactor::UNNEST { alias: a, .. } => alias(a),
7230        _ => None,
7231    }
7232}

7234/// Check if an expression is a simple column reference (with optional alias) to the given name.
7235fn is_simple_col_ref(expr: &Expr, col_name: &PlSmallStr) -> bool {
7236    match expr {
7237        Expr::Column(n) => n == col_name,
7238        Expr::Alias(inner, _) => matches!(inner.as_ref(), Expr::Column(n) if n == col_name),
7239        _ => false,
7240    }
7241}

7243/// Check that a LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH value is one value for the whole query: outside its
7244/// subqueries it reads no column and has no aggregate, window, user-defined or `UNNEST` call.
7245fn check_query_independent_value(expr: &SQLExpr, ctx: &SQLContext) -> PolarsResult<()> {
7246    struct Check<'a> {
7247        ctx: &'a SQLContext,
7248        subquery_depth: usize,
7249    }
7250
7251    impl sqlparser::ast::Visitor for Check<'_> {
7252        type Break = ();
7253
7254        fn pre_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
7255            self.subquery_depth += 1;
7256            ControlFlow::Continue(())
7257        }
7258
7259        fn post_visit_query(&mut self, _query: &Query) -> ControlFlow<()> {
7260            self.subquery_depth -= 1;
7261            ControlFlow::Continue(())
7262        }
7263
7264        fn pre_visit_expr(&mut self, expr: &SQLExpr) -> ControlFlow<()> {
7265            if self.subquery_depth > 0 {
7266                return ControlFlow::Continue(());
7267            }
7268            let is_valid = match expr {
7269                SQLExpr::Identifier(_)
7270                | SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(_)
7271                | SQLExpr::Wildcard(_)
7272                | SQLExpr::QualifiedWildcard(..) => false,
7273                SQLExpr::Function(function) => {
7274                    function.over.is_none()
7275                        && !PolarsSQLFunctions::try_from_sql(function, self.ctx).is_ok_and(|f| {
7276                            f.is_builtin_aggregate()
7277                                || matches!(
7278                                    f,
7279                                    PolarsSQLFunctions::Udf(_) | PolarsSQLFunctions::Explode
7280                                )
7281                        })
7282                },
7283                _ => true,
7284            };
7285            if is_valid {
7286                ControlFlow::Continue(())
7287            } else {
7288                ControlFlow::Break(())
7289            }
7290        }
7291    }
7292
7293    let mut check = Check {
7294        ctx,
7295        subquery_depth: 0,
7296    };
7297    polars_ensure!(
7298        dyn_visit::visit(expr, &mut check).is_continue(),
7299        SQLSyntax: "LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH must be one value for the query, found {}", expr
7300    );
7301    Ok(())
7302}

7304/// Reject a parsed expression that still carries an unresolved subquery, so that a
7305/// clause which doesn't resolve them reports that in SQL terms.
7306fn reject_unresolved_subquery(expr: &Expr, clause: &str) -> PolarsResult<()> {
7307    polars_ensure!(
7308        !has_expr(expr, |e| matches!(e, Expr::SubPlan(_, _))),
7309        SQLInterface: "subqueries are not currently supported in the {} clause", clause
7310    );
7311    Ok(())
7312}

7314/// Strip the outer alias from an expression (if present) for expression equality comparison.
7315/// Remove every alias, so a join key or predicate names the underlying column.
7316fn strip_join_aliases(expr: Expr) -> Expr {
7317    expr.map_expr(|e| match e {
7318        Expr::Alias(inner, _) => Arc::unwrap_or_clone(inner),
7319        e => e,
7320    })
7321}
7322
7323pub(crate) fn strip_outer_alias(expr: &Expr) -> Expr {
7324    if let Expr::Alias(inner, _) = expr {
7325        inner.as_ref().clone()
7326    } else {
7327        expr.clone()
7328    }
7329}

7331/// Reduce decorrelated correlated-subquery columns, which hold one value per input row,
7332/// to the single value they take within a group. An aggregate reads them per row.
7333fn reduce_correlated_cols_in_group_context(expr: Expr) -> Expr {
7334    match expr {
7335        Expr::Column(name) if is_correlated_result_col(&name) => Expr::Column(name).first(),
7336        e if is_marked_aggregate(&e) => e,
7337        e => e
7338            .map_children(
7339                &mut |c, _| Ok(reduce_correlated_cols_in_group_context(c)),
7340                &mut (),
7341            )
7342            .unwrap(),
7343    }
7344}

7346/// Which inputs of a join a condition reads.
7347enum JoinInputs {
7348    Neither,
7349    Left,
7350    Right,
7351    Both,
7352    Unknown,
7353}
7354
7355/// How a resolved subquery placeholder column should be referenced.
7356#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
7357pub(crate) enum SubqueryShape {
7358    /// `col(<placeholder>).first()` -- a scalar, for filter and aggregation contexts.
7359    Scalar,
7360    /// `col(<placeholder>)` -- the same value at the frame's height, for contexts that
7361    /// reject a length-1 series, such as sorting.
7362    Broadcast,
7363}
7364
7365/// Read the resolved scalar subqueries in the inputs of the windows of `expr`, and those in
7366/// `read_per_row` in its aggregates, as their column, which holds the value on every row:
7367/// these functions read one value per row.
7368fn broadcast_subqueries_in_inputs(
7369    expr: Expr,
7370    subquery_names: &PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>,
7371    read_per_row: &PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>,
7372) -> Expr {
7373    fn broadcast(
7374        expr: Expr,
7375        in_window: bool,
7376        in_aggregate: bool,
7377        subquery_names: &PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>,
7378        read_per_row: &PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>,
7379    ) -> Expr {
7380        match expr {
7381            Expr::Agg(AggExpr::First(inner))
7382                if matches!(
7383                    inner.as_ref(),
7384                    Expr::Column(name) if subquery_names.contains(name)
7385                        && (in_window || (in_aggregate && read_per_row.contains(name)))
7386                ) =>
7387            {
7388                Arc::unwrap_or_clone(inner)
7389            },
7390            e => {
7391                let in_window = in_window || matches!(e, Expr::Over { .. });
7392                let in_aggregate = in_aggregate || is_marked_aggregate(&e);
7393                e.map_children(
7394                    &mut |c, _| {
7395                        Ok(broadcast(
7396                            c,
7397                            in_window,
7398                            in_aggregate,
7399                            subquery_names,
7400                            read_per_row,
7401                        ))
7402                    },
7403                    &mut (),
7404                )
7405                .unwrap()
7406            },
7407        }
7408    }
7409    if subquery_names.is_empty() {
7410        return expr;
7411    }
7412    broadcast(expr, false, false, subquery_names, read_per_row)
7413}
7414
7415/// Replace every resolved scalar subquery in `expr` with a scalar literal, so the
7416/// expression can be height-classified on its own terms. The result is only inspected
7417/// for its shape, never evaluated.
7418fn without_resolved_subqueries(expr: &Expr, subquery_names: &PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>) -> Expr {
7419    expr.clone().map_expr(|e| {
7420        let is_placeholder = matches!(
7421            &e,
7422            Expr::Agg(AggExpr::First(inner))
7423                if matches!(inner.as_ref(), Expr::Column(n) if subquery_names.contains(n))
7424        );
7425        if is_placeholder { lit(1i32) } else { e }
7426    })
7427}
7428
7429/// Drop the placeholder columns `process_subqueries` added to the frame.
7430fn drop_subquery_placeholders(lf: LazyFrame, names: PlHashSet<PlSmallStr>) -> LazyFrame {
7431    if names.is_empty() {
7432        return lf;
7433    }
7434    lf.drop(Selector::ByName {
7435        names: names.into_iter().collect(),
7436        strict: true,
7437    })
7438}
7439
7440/// Resolve a SELECT alias to its underlying expression (for use in GROUP BY).
7441///
7442/// Returns the expression WITH alias if the name matches a projection alias and is NOT a column
7443/// that exists in the schema; otherwise returns `None` to use the default/standard resolution.
7444fn resolve_select_alias(name: &str, projections: &[Expr], schema: &Schema) -> Option<Expr> {
7445    // Original columns take precedence over SELECT aliases
7446    if schema.contains(name) {
7447        return None;
7448    }
7449    // Find a projection with this alias and return its expression (preserving the alias)
7450    projections.iter().find_map(|p| match p {
7451        Expr::Alias(inner, alias) if alias.as_str() == name => {
7452            Some(inner.as_ref().clone().alias(alias.clone()))
7453        },
7454        _ => None,
7455    })
7456}
7457
7458/// Check if all columns referred to in a Polars expression exist in the given Schema.
7459fn expr_cols_all_in_schema(expr: &Expr, schema: &Schema) -> bool {
7460    let mut found_cols = false;
7461    let mut all_in_schema = true;
7462    for e in expr.into_iter() {
7463        if let Expr::Column(name) = e {
7464            found_cols = true;
7465            if !schema.contains(name.as_str()) {
7466                all_in_schema = false;
7467                break;
7468            }
7469        }
7470    }
7471    found_cols && all_in_schema
7472}
7473
7474/// Determine which parsed join expressions actually belong in `left_on` and which in `right_on`.
7475///
7476/// This needs to be handled carefully because in SQL joins you can write "join on" constraints
7477/// either way round, and in joins with more than two tables you can also join against an earlier
7478/// table (e.g.: you could be joining `df1` to `df2` to `df3`, but the final join condition where
7479/// we join `df2` to `df3` could refer to `df1.a = df3.b`); this takes a little more work to
7480/// resolve as our native `join` function operates on only two tables at a time.
7481///
7482/// An operand can also be constant (`ON df1.x = df2.x AND df2.flag = 'y'`), in which case it has
7483/// no table of its own and takes whichever side the other operand does not.
7484fn determine_left_right_join_on(
7485    ctx: &mut SQLContext,
7486    expr_left: &SQLExpr,
7487    expr_right: &SQLExpr,
7488    tbl_left: &TableInfo,
7489    tbl_right: &TableInfo,
7490    join_schema: &Schema,
7491) -> PolarsResult<(Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>)> {
7492    // parse, removing any aliases that may have been added by `resolve_column`
7493    // (called inside `parse_sql_expr`) as we need the actual/underlying col
7494    let refers_to = |expr: &SQLExpr, tbl: &TableInfo| {
7495        tbl.relations
7496            .iter()
7497            .any(|name| expr_refers_to_table(expr, name, &ctx.active_relations))
7498    };
7499    let left_refs = (
7500        refers_to(expr_left, tbl_left),
7501        refers_to(expr_left, tbl_right),
7502    );
7503    let right_refs = (
7504        refers_to(expr_right, tbl_left),
7505        refers_to(expr_right, tbl_right),
7506    );
7507    // an operand's dtypes come from the table it names; the merged schema keeps the left
7508    // dtype for a column name that exists in both tables
7509    let operand_schema = |refs: (bool, bool)| -> &Schema {
7510        match refs {
7511            (true, false) => &tbl_left.schema,
7512            (false, true) => &tbl_right.schema,
7513            _ => join_schema,
7514        }
7515    };
7516    let (left_schema, right_schema) = (operand_schema(left_refs), operand_schema(right_refs));
7517    let left_on = strip_join_aliases(parse_sql_expr(expr_left, ctx, Some(left_schema))?);
7518    let right_on = strip_join_aliases(parse_sql_expr(expr_right, ctx, Some(right_schema))?);
7519    let (left_on, right_on) = convert_int_literal_for_string(
7520        left_on,
7521        right_on,
7522        |e| is_string_expr(e, left_schema),
7523        |e| is_string_expr(e, right_schema),
7524    );
7525
7526    // a constant operand is a literal, or any other expression referencing no column (such as
7527    // `UPPER('it')`); it can be evaluated against either input, so it has no table affinity
7528    let (left_is_const, right_is_const) = (
7529        !expr_references_any_column(expr_left),
7530        !expr_references_any_column(expr_right),
7531    );
7532
7533    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
7534    // simple/typical case: can fully resolve SQL-level table references
7535    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
7536    // if the SQL-level references unambiguously indicate table ownership, we're done
7537    match (left_refs, right_refs) {
7538        // standard: left expr → left table, right expr → right table
7539        ((true, false), (false, true)) => return Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7540        // reversed: left expr → right table, right expr → left table
7541        ((false, true), (true, false)) => return Ok((vec![right_on], vec![left_on])),
7542        // qualified column vs constant: the qualifier alone settles it (note that this also
7543        // covers a column name that is present in *both* schemas, which schema-based
7544        // resolution below cannot disambiguate)
7545        ((true, false), _) if right_is_const => return Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7546        ((false, true), _) if right_is_const => return Ok((vec![right_on], vec![left_on])),
7547        (_, (false, true)) if left_is_const => return Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7548        (_, (true, false)) if left_is_const => return Ok((vec![right_on], vec![left_on])),
7549        // unsupported: one side references *both* tables
7550        ((true, true), _) | (_, (true, true)) if tbl_left.name != tbl_right.name => {
7551            polars_bail!(
7552               SQLInterface: "unsupported join condition: {} side references both '{}' and '{}'",
7553               if left_refs.0 && left_refs.1 {
7554                    "left"
7555                } else {
7556                    "right"
7557                }, tbl_left.name, tbl_right.name
7558            )
7559        },
7560        // fall through to the more involved col/ref resolution
7561        _ => {},
7562    }
7563
7564    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
7565    // more involved: additionally employ schema-based column resolution
7566    // (applies to unqualified columns and/or chained joins)
7567    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
7568    // a constant resolves against either schema, so we report it as belonging to both and let
7569    // the arms below take the side that the other (schema-unique) operand leaves free
7570    let cols_in_schemas = |expr: &Expr, is_const: bool| {
7571        if is_const {
7572            (true, true)
7573        } else {
7574            (
7575                expr_cols_all_in_schema(expr, &tbl_left.schema),
7576                expr_cols_all_in_schema(expr, &tbl_right.schema),
7577            )
7578        }
7579    };
7580    let left_on_cols_in = cols_in_schemas(&left_on, left_is_const);
7581    let right_on_cols_in = cols_in_schemas(&right_on, right_is_const);
7582
7583    match (left_on_cols_in, right_on_cols_in) {
7584        // each expression's columns exist in exactly one schema
7585        ((true, false), (false, true)) => Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7586        ((false, true), (true, false)) => Ok((vec![right_on], vec![left_on])),
7587        // one expression is in both schemas (or is constant) and the other in only one;
7588        // the unique one decides, and the ambiguous one takes the remaining side
7589        ((true, true), (true, false)) => Ok((vec![right_on], vec![left_on])),
7590        ((true, true), (false, true)) => Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7591        ((true, false), (true, true)) => Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7592        ((false, true), (true, true)) => Ok((vec![right_on], vec![left_on])),
7593        // pass through as-is
7594        _ => Ok((vec![left_on], vec![right_on])),
7595    }
7596}
7597
7598/// Returns `(left_on, right_on, join_where_predicates)`.
7599///
7600/// - Equi-conditions (`=`) are returned as paired `left_on`/`right_on` entries.
7601/// - Any other condition is returned as a `join_where` predicate that references columns
7602///   using their merged-schema names (right columns that conflict with the left schema are
7603///   suffixed).
7604fn process_join_on(
7605    ctx: &mut SQLContext,
7606    sql_expr: &SQLExpr,
7607    tbl_left: &TableInfo,
7608    tbl_right: &TableInfo,
7609) -> PolarsResult<(Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>)> {
7610    match sql_expr {
7611        SQLExpr::BinaryOp { left, op, right } => match op {
7612            SQLBinaryOperator::And => {
7613                let (mut left_i, mut right_i, mut preds_i) =
7614                    process_join_on(ctx, left, tbl_left, tbl_right)?;
7615                let (mut left_j, mut right_j, mut preds_j) =
7616                    process_join_on(ctx, right, tbl_left, tbl_right)?;
7617                left_i.append(&mut left_j);
7618                right_i.append(&mut right_j);
7619                preds_i.append(&mut preds_j);
7620                Ok((left_i, right_i, preds_i))
7621            },
7622            SQLBinaryOperator::Eq => {
7623                // Both operands read the same input: not a key pair but a condition on
7624                // that input.
7625                let left_input = join_operand_input(ctx, left, tbl_left, tbl_right);
7626                if left_input.is_some()
7627                    && left_input == join_operand_input(ctx, right, tbl_left, tbl_right)
7628                {
7629                    return process_join_predicate(ctx, sql_expr, tbl_left, tbl_right);
7630                }
7631                // An operand that reads both inputs is no key, but a condition on the
7632                // joined rows.
7633                let inputs =
7634                    [left, right].map(|e| ctx.conjunct_join_inputs(e, tbl_left, tbl_right));
7635                if inputs.iter().any(|i| matches!(i, JoinInputs::Both))
7636                    && !inputs.iter().any(|i| matches!(i, JoinInputs::Unknown))
7637                    && ctx.is_joined_rows_condition(sql_expr, tbl_left, tbl_right)?
7638                {
7639                    return process_join_predicate(ctx, sql_expr, tbl_left, tbl_right);
7640                }
7641                let join_schema = build_join_schema(tbl_left, tbl_right)?;
7642                let (l, r) = determine_left_right_join_on(
7643                    ctx,
7644                    left,
7645                    right,
7646                    tbl_left,
7647                    tbl_right,
7648                    &join_schema,
7649                )?;
7650                Ok((l, r, vec![]))
7651            },
7652            _ => process_join_predicate(ctx, sql_expr, tbl_left, tbl_right),
7653        },
7654        SQLExpr::Nested(expr) => process_join_on(ctx, expr, tbl_left, tbl_right),
7655        _ => process_join_predicate(ctx, sql_expr, tbl_left, tbl_right),
7656    }
7657}
7658
7659/// Which input of a join `expr` reads: `Some(true)` for the left input, `Some(false)` for
7660/// the right one, and `None` if it reads both, neither, or a column found in both.
7661fn join_operand_input(
7662    ctx: &SQLContext,
7663    expr: &SQLExpr,
7664    tbl_left: &TableInfo,
7665    tbl_right: &TableInfo,
7666) -> Option<bool> {
7667    let refers_to = |tbl: &TableInfo| {
7668        tbl.relations
7669            .iter()
7670            .any(|name| expr_refers_to_table(expr, name, &ctx.active_relations))
7671    };
7672    let in_schemas = match (refers_to(tbl_left), refers_to(tbl_right)) {
7673        (false, false) => (
7674            sql_expr_cols_all_in_schema(expr, &tbl_left.schema),
7675            sql_expr_cols_all_in_schema(expr, &tbl_right.schema),
7676        ),
7677        refs => refs,
7678    };
7679    match in_schemas {
7680        (true, false) => Some(true),
7681        (false, true) => Some(false),
7682        _ => None,
7683    }
7684}
7685
7686/// Parse a join condition other than a plain equality into a `join_where` predicate over
7687/// the joined frame, where right-table columns that also exist in the left table carry a suffix.
7688fn process_join_predicate(
7689    ctx: &mut SQLContext,
7690    sql_expr: &SQLExpr,
7691    tbl_left: &TableInfo,
7692    tbl_right: &TableInfo,
7693) -> PolarsResult<(Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>)> {
7694    let suffix = format!(":{}", tbl_right.name);
7695    let conflicts = |name: &str| tbl_left.schema.contains(name) && tbl_right.schema.contains(name);
7696
7697    let mut joined_schema = build_join_schema(tbl_left, tbl_right)?;
7698    for (name, dtype) in tbl_right.schema.iter().filter(|(name, _)| conflicts(name)) {
7699        joined_schema.insert(
7700            PlSmallStr::from_string(format!("{name}{suffix}")),
7701            dtype.clone(),
7702        );
7703    }
7704
7705    // `right_table.col` -> `col:right_table` when the name is also a left column
7706    let mut sql_expr = sql_expr.clone();
7707    let _ = visit_expressions_mut(&mut sql_expr, |e| {
7708        if let SQLExpr::CompoundIdentifier(idents) = e
7709            && let Ok(Some((name, len))) = ctx.resolve_qualifier(idents)
7710            && name == tbl_right.name.as_str()
7711            && conflicts(&idents[len].value)
7712        {
7713            let suffixed = Ident::new(format!("{}{suffix}", idents[len].value));
7714            idents.splice(0..=len, [suffixed]);
7715            if idents.len() == 1 {
7716                *e = SQLExpr::Identifier(idents.pop().unwrap());
7717            }
7718        }
7719        ControlFlow::<()>::Continue(())
7720    });
7721    let predicate = strip_join_aliases(parse_sql_expr(&sql_expr, ctx, Some(&joined_schema))?);
7722    Ok((vec![], vec![], vec![predicate]))
7723}
7724
7725/// Check that a QUALIFY predicate reads a window function, directly or through a SELECT
7726/// alias.
7727fn check_qualify(qualify: &SQLExpr, projection: &[SelectItem]) -> PolarsResult<()> {
7728    let (has_window_fns, column_refs) = QualifyExpression::analyze(qualify);
7729    let references_window_alias = projection.iter().any(|item| {
7730        matches!(item, SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr, alias }
7731            if expr_has_window_functions(expr) && column_refs.contains(&alias.value))
7732    });
7733    polars_ensure!(
7734        has_window_fns || references_window_alias,
7735        SQLSyntax: "QUALIFY clause must reference window functions either explicitly or via SELECT aliases"
7736    );
7737    Ok(())
7738}
7739
7740/// Every `RANDOM()` call is its own draw. A GROUP BY key or ORDER BY item that repeats a
7741/// SELECT item could be read as that item, so these raise rather than draw again.
7742fn check_random_items(select: &Select, query: &Query) -> PolarsResult<()> {
7743    polars_ensure!(
7744        !contains_random(&select.group_by, false),
7745        SQLInterface: "RANDOM() in GROUP BY is not supported; group by a SELECT alias instead"
7746    );
7747    let Some(OrderBy {
7748        kind: OrderByKind::Expressions(order_by),
7749        ..
7750    }) = &query.order_by
7751    else {
7752        return Ok(());
7753    };
7754    let key = |e: &SQLExpr| {
7755        let mut e = e;
7756        while let SQLExpr::Nested(inner) = e {
7757            e = inner;
7758        }
7759        e.to_string().to_lowercase()
7760    };
7761    for item in order_by.iter().filter(|e| contains_random(&e.expr, false)) {
7762        let item_key = key(&item.expr);
7763        let repeats_select_item = select.projection.iter().any(|p| match p {
7764            SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(e) | SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr: e, .. } => {
7765                key(e) == item_key
7766            },
7767            _ => false,
7768        });
7769        polars_ensure!(
7770            !repeats_select_item,
7771            SQLInterface: "RANDOM() in an ORDER BY item that repeats a SELECT item is not supported; order by its alias instead"
7772        );
7773    }
7774    Ok(())
7775}
7776
7777/// Whether `expr` yields one value independent of any input frame.
7778fn is_constant(expr: &Expr) -> bool {
7779    expr.clone()
7780        .meta()
7781        .is_input_independent_scalar()
7782        .unwrap_or(false)
7783}
7784
7785/// Build a unified schema from both tables; needed for multi/chained joins where suffixed
7786/// intermediary/joined cols aren't in an existing schema.
7787fn build_join_schema(tbl_left: &TableInfo, tbl_right: &TableInfo) -> PolarsResult<Schema> {
7788    let mut join_schema = Schema::with_capacity(tbl_left.schema.len() + tbl_right.schema.len());
7789    for (name, dtype) in tbl_left.schema.iter() {
7790        join_schema.insert_at_index(join_schema.len(), name.clone(), dtype.clone())?;
7791    }
7792    for (name, dtype) in tbl_right.schema.iter() {
7793        if !join_schema.contains(name) {
7794            join_schema.insert_at_index(join_schema.len(), name.clone(), dtype.clone())?;
7795        }
7796    }
7797    Ok(join_schema)
7798}
7799
7800/// Rename columns in `expr` that appear in *both* table schemas to their merged-schema
7801/// (right-side suffixed) names, so they resolve against the joined frame.
7802fn suffix_conflicting_columns(
7803    expr: Expr,
7804    tbl_left: &TableInfo,
7805    tbl_right: &TableInfo,
7806    suffix: &str,
7807) -> Expr {
7808    expr.map_expr(|e| match e {
7809        Expr::Column(ref name)
7810            if tbl_left.schema.contains(name.as_str())
7811                && tbl_right.schema.contains(name.as_str()) =>
7812        {
7813            Expr::Column(PlSmallStr::from_string(format!("{name}{suffix}")))
7814        },
7815        other => other,
7816    })
7817}
7818
7819fn process_join_constraint(
7820    constraint: &JoinConstraint,
7821    tbl_left: &TableInfo,
7822    tbl_right: &TableInfo,
7823    ctx: &mut SQLContext,
7824) -> PolarsResult<(Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>, Vec<Expr>)> {
7825    match constraint {
7826        JoinConstraint::On(expr) => {
7827            let (left_on, right_on, predicates) = process_join_on(ctx, expr, tbl_left, tbl_right)?;
7828            // `a = b AND b = a` gives the same key pair twice.
7829            let mut keys: Vec<(Expr, Expr)> = Vec::with_capacity(left_on.len());
7830            for key in left_on.into_iter().zip(right_on) {
7831                if !keys.contains(&key) {
7832                    keys.push(key);
7833                }
7834            }
7835            let (left_on, right_on) = keys.into_iter().unzip();
7836            Ok((left_on, right_on, predicates))
7837        },
7838        JoinConstraint::Using(idents) if !idents.is_empty() => {
7839            let using: Vec<Expr> = idents
7840                .iter()
7841                .map(|ObjectName(parts)| {
7842                    if parts.len() != 1 {
7843                        polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "JOIN \"USING\" clause expects simple column names, not qualified names");
7844                    }
7845                    match parts[0].as_ident() {
7846                        Some(ident) => Ok(col(ident.value.as_str())),
7847                        None => polars_bail!(SQLSyntax: "JOIN \"USING\" clause expects identifiers, not functions"),
7848                    }
7849                })
7850                .collect::<PolarsResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
7851            Ok((using.clone(), using, vec![]))
7852        },
7853        JoinConstraint::Natural => {
7854            let left_names = tbl_left.schema.iter_names().collect::<PlHashSet<_>>();
7855            let right_names = tbl_right.schema.iter_names().collect::<PlHashSet<_>>();
7856            let on: Vec<Expr> = left_names
7857                .intersection(&right_names)
7858                .map(|&name| col(name.clone()))
7859                .collect();
7860            if on.is_empty() {
7861                polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "no common columns found for NATURAL JOIN")
7862            }
7863            Ok((on.clone(), on, vec![]))
7864        },
7865        _ => polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "unsupported SQL join constraint:\n{:?}", constraint),
7866    }
7867}
7868
7869/// Flatten a SQL AND-expression tree into individual leaf conditions.
7870pub(crate) fn flatten_and_conditions(expr: &SQLExpr) -> Vec<&SQLExpr> {
7871    match expr {
7872        SQLExpr::BinaryOp {
7873            left,
7874            op: SQLBinaryOperator::And,
7875            right,
7876        } => {
7877            let mut conditions = flatten_and_conditions(left);
7878            conditions.extend(flatten_and_conditions(right));
7879            conditions
7880        },
7881        SQLExpr::Nested(inner) => flatten_and_conditions(inner),
7882        _ => vec![expr],
7883    }
7884}
7885
7886/// Reconstruct a SQL AND-expression tree from a list of conditions.
7887/// Fold `conditions` into a single expression joined by `op`; `None` if empty.
7888pub(crate) fn combine_conditions(
7889    conditions: Vec<SQLExpr>,
7890    op: SQLBinaryOperator,
7891) -> Option<SQLExpr> {
7892    conditions
7893        .into_iter()
7894        .reduce(|left, right| SQLExpr::BinaryOp {
7895            left: Box::new(left),
7896            op: op.clone(),
7897            right: Box::new(right),
7898        })
7899}
7900
7901/// Check if a SQL expression is a join condition (equi or non-equi comparison) that bridges
7902/// the given left table set and the right table. Operands are matched via qualified table
7903/// references first, falling back to schema membership for unqualified columns; an operand
7904/// found in both schemas (or neither) is ambiguous and matches neither side.
7905fn is_join_comparison(
7906    expr: &SQLExpr,
7907    left_tables: &[String],
7908    right_table: &str,
7909    deferred_tables: &[String],
7910    relations: &[RelationName],
7911    left_schema: &Schema,
7912    right_schema: &Schema,
7913) -> bool {
7914    let refers_to = |expr: &SQLExpr, table: &str| expr_refers_to_table(expr, table, relations);
7915    // A condition naming a relation joined in a later round stays in the
7916    // residual WHERE until that relation is present.
7917    if deferred_tables.iter().any(|table| refers_to(expr, table)) {
7918        return false;
7919    }
7920    // A subquery is not a join key; its correlated columns name outer relations.
7921    if expr_contains_subquery(expr) {
7922        return false;
7923    }
7924    if let SQLExpr::BinaryOp {
7925        left,
7926        op:
7927            SQLBinaryOperator::Eq
7928            | SQLBinaryOperator::Lt
7929            | SQLBinaryOperator::LtEq
7930            | SQLBinaryOperator::Gt
7931            | SQLBinaryOperator::GtEq
7932            | SQLBinaryOperator::NotEq,
7933        right,
7934    } = expr
7935    {
7936        let operand_side = |operand: &SQLExpr| -> (bool, bool) {
7937            let refs_right = refers_to(operand, right_table);
7938            let refs_left = left_tables.iter().any(|t| refers_to(operand, t));
7939            if refs_right || refs_left {
7940                (refs_right, refs_left)
7941            } else {
7942                let in_right = sql_expr_cols_all_in_schema(operand, right_schema);
7943                let in_left = sql_expr_cols_all_in_schema(operand, left_schema);
7944                (in_right && !in_left, in_left && !in_right)
7945            }
7946        };
7947
7948        let (left_is_right, left_is_left) = operand_side(left);
7949        let (right_is_right, right_is_left) = operand_side(right);
7950
7951        // One operand must name only a left table and the other only the right one;
7952        // an operand spanning both stays a filter, as it belongs to neither side.
7953        (left_is_right && !left_is_left && right_is_left && !right_is_right)
7954            || (right_is_right && !right_is_left && left_is_left && !left_is_right)
7955    } else {
7956        false
7957    }
7958}
7959
7960/// Partition a WHERE clause into join predicates (bridging left tables and the
7961/// right table) and residual filter conditions.
7962fn extract_join_predicates(
7963    where_expr: &Option<SQLExpr>,
7964    left_tables: &[String],
7965    right_table: &str,
7966    deferred_tables: &[String],
7967    relations: &[RelationName],
7968    left_schema: &Schema,
7969    right_schema: &Schema,
7970) -> (Option<SQLExpr>, Option<SQLExpr>) {
7971    let Some(expr) = where_expr else {
7972        return (None, None);
7973    };
7974    let conditions = flatten_and_conditions(expr);
7975    let mut join_conds = Vec::new();
7976    let mut filter_conds = Vec::new();
7977    for cond in conditions {
7978        if is_join_comparison(
7979            cond,
7980            left_tables,
7981            right_table,
7982            deferred_tables,
7983            relations,
7984            left_schema,
7985            right_schema,
7986        ) {
7987            join_conds.push(cond.clone());
7988        } else {
7989            filter_conds.push(cond.clone());
7990        }
7991    }
7992    (
7993        combine_conditions(join_conds, SQLBinaryOperator::And),
7994        combine_conditions(filter_conds, SQLBinaryOperator::And),
7995    )
7996}

7998/// Extract table identifiers referenced in a SQL query; uses a visitor to
7999/// collect all table names that appear in FROM clauses, JOINs, TABLE refs
8000/// in set operations, and subqueries.
8001pub fn extract_table_identifiers(
8002    query: &str,
8003    include_schema: bool,
8004    unique: bool,
8005) -> PolarsResult<Vec<String>> {
8006    let ast = parse_sql(query)?;
8007    let mut tables = Vec::new();
8008    for stmt in &ast {
8009        tables.extend(statement_table_identifiers(stmt, include_schema, false));
8010    }
8011    Ok(if unique {
8012        tables
8013            .into_iter()
8014            .collect::<PlIndexSet<_>>()
8015            .into_iter()
8016            .collect()
8017    } else {
8018        tables
8019    })
8020}

8022/// The order to register the CTEs of a `WITH RECURSIVE` in, where a CTE may read any other,
8023/// and whether each CTE reads itself. Each CTE comes after the other CTEs it reads; CTEs that
8024/// read each other are not supported.
8025fn recursive_cte_order(with: &With) -> PolarsResult<(Vec<usize>, Vec<bool>)> {
8026    let names: Vec<String> = with
8027        .cte_tables
8028        .iter()
8029        .map(|cte| cte.alias.name.value.clone())
8030        .collect();
8031    let mut seen = PlHashSet::with_capacity(names.len());
8032    if let Some(name) = names
8033        .iter()
8034        .find(|name| !seen.insert(name.to_ascii_lowercase()))
8035    {
8036        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "CTE name '{}' is used more than once", name)
8037    }
8038    let mut deps: Vec<PlHashSet<usize>> = with
8039        .cte_tables
8040        .iter()
8041        .map(|cte| referenced_ctes(&cte.query, &names))
8042        .collect();
8043    let reads_itself: Vec<bool> = deps
8044        .iter_mut()
8045        .enumerate()
8046        .map(|(idx, deps)| deps.remove(&idx))
8047        .collect();
8048    let mut order = Vec::with_capacity(names.len());
8049    let mut done = vec![false; names.len()];
8050    while order.len() < names.len() {
8051        // Keep the written order among the CTEs that are ready.
8052        let Some(next) =
8053            (0..names.len()).find(|idx| !done[*idx] && deps[*idx].iter().all(|dep| done[*dep]))
8054        else {
8055            let cycle: Vec<&str> = (0..names.len())
8056                .filter(|idx| !done[*idx])
8057                .map(|idx| names[idx].as_str())
8058                .collect();
8059            polars_bail!(
8060                SQLInterface: "mutually recursive CTEs are not supported ({})", cycle.join(", ")
8061            )
8062        };
8063        done[next] = true;
8064        order.push(next);
8065    }
8066    Ok((order, reads_itself))
8067}

8069/// Table identifiers referenced by a single parsed statement.
8070fn statement_table_identifiers(
8071    stmt: &Statement,
8072    include_schema: bool,
8073    unique: bool,
8074) -> Vec<String> {
8075    let mut collector = TableIdentifierCollector {
8076        include_schema,
8077        ..Default::default()
8078    };
8079    let _ = dyn_visit::visit(stmt, &mut collector);
8080    if unique {
8081        collector
8082            .tables
8083            .into_iter()
8084            .collect::<PlIndexSet<_>>()
8085            .into_iter()
8086            .collect()
8087    } else {
8088        collector.tables
8089    }
8090}

8092/// Strictly cast column `name` of type `dtype` to `to`, aligning struct fields by name first.
8093fn cast_matching_struct_fields(name: &PlSmallStr, dtype: &DataType, to: &DataType) -> Expr {
8094    let shape = match_struct_fields(dtype, to);
8095    let expr = col(name.clone());
8096    let expr = if shape != *dtype {
8097        expr.cast(shape)
8098    } else {
8099        expr
8100    };
8101    expr.strict_cast(to.clone())
8102}

8104/// Whether `stmt` is a query that only reads; `INSERT`/`UPDATE` bodies write to the context.
8105fn is_read_only_query(stmt: &Statement) -> bool {
8106    match stmt {
8107        Statement::Query(query) => {
8108            !matches!(query.body.as_ref(), SetExpr::Insert(_) | SetExpr::Update(_))
8109        },
8110        _ => false,
8111    }
8112}

8114/// The names, `IF EXISTS` and `PURGE` of a `DROP` statement, rejecting unsupported modifiers.
8115fn drop_table_parts(stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<(&[ObjectName], bool, bool)> {
8116    // Destructure exhaustively so new sqlparser fields surface as compile errors.
8117    let Statement::Drop {
8118        object_type: _,
8119        names,
8120        if_exists,
8121        purge,
8122
8123        // Unsupported modifiers
8124        cascade,
8125        restrict,
8126        temporary,
8127        table,
8128    } = stmt
8129    else {
8130        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "unexpected statement type; expected DROP")
8131    };
8132    polars_ensure!(!cascade, SQLInterface: "`DROP ... CASCADE` is not supported");
8133    polars_ensure!(!restrict, SQLInterface: "`DROP ... RESTRICT` is not supported");
8134    polars_ensure!(!temporary, SQLInterface: "`DROP TEMPORARY` is not supported");
8135    polars_ensure!(table.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DROP ... ON <table>` is not supported");
8136    Ok((names, *if_exists, *purge))
8137}

8139fn create_schema_parts(stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<(&ObjectName, bool, &[SqlOption])> {
8140    // Destructure exhaustively so new sqlparser fields surface as compile errors.
8141    let Statement::CreateSchema {
8142        schema_name,
8143        if_not_exists,
8144        with,
8145
8146        // Unsupported modifiers
8147        or_replace,
8148        options,
8149        default_collate_spec,
8150        clone,
8151    } = stmt
8152    else {
8153        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "unexpected statement type; expected CREATE SCHEMA")
8154    };
8155    let SchemaName::Simple(name) = schema_name else {
8156        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "`CREATE SCHEMA ... AUTHORIZATION` is not supported")
8157    };
8158    polars_ensure!(!or_replace, SQLInterface: "`CREATE OR REPLACE SCHEMA` is not supported");
8159    polars_ensure!(options.is_none(), SQLInterface: "schema `OPTIONS` clauses are not supported; use `WITH (...)` instead");
8160    polars_ensure!(default_collate_spec.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DEFAULT COLLATE` is not supported");
8161    polars_ensure!(clone.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`CREATE SCHEMA ... CLONE` is not supported");
8162    Ok((name, *if_not_exists, with.as_deref().unwrap_or_default()))
8163}

8165fn drop_schema_parts(stmt: &Statement) -> PolarsResult<(&ObjectName, bool)> {
8166    // Destructure exhaustively so new sqlparser fields surface as compile errors.
8167    let Statement::Drop {
8168        object_type: _,
8169        names,
8170        if_exists,
8171        // The default: a schema must be empty.
8172        restrict: _,
8173
8174        // Unsupported modifiers
8175        cascade,
8176        purge,
8177        temporary,
8178        table,
8179    } = stmt
8180    else {
8181        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "unexpected statement type; expected DROP")
8182    };
8183    polars_ensure!(!cascade, SQLInterface: "`DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE` is not supported; drop its tables first");
8184    polars_ensure!(!purge, SQLInterface: "`DROP SCHEMA ... PURGE` is not supported");
8185    polars_ensure!(!temporary, SQLInterface: "`DROP TEMPORARY` is not supported");
8186    polars_ensure!(table.is_none(), SQLInterface: "`DROP ... ON <table>` is not supported");
8187    let [name] = names.as_slice() else {
8188        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "DROP SCHEMA takes one schema name")
8189    };

8193/// The table and `WHERE` of a `DELETE` statement, rejecting unsupported clauses.
8194fn delete_parts(delete: &Delete) -> PolarsResult<(&TableWithJoins, Option<&SQLExpr>)> {
8195    // Destructure exhaustively so new sqlparser fields surface as compile errors.
8196    let Delete {
8197        delete_token: _,
8198        optimizer_hints: _,
8199        tables,
8200        from,
8201        using,
8202        selection,
8203        returning,
8204        output,
8205        order_by,
8206        limit,
8207    } = delete;
8208    polars_ensure!(tables.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "DELETE expects exactly one table name");
8209    polars_ensure!(using.is_none(), SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support the USING clause");
8210    polars_ensure!(returning.is_none(), SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support the RETURNING clause");
8211    polars_ensure!(output.is_none(), SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support the OUTPUT clause");
8212    polars_ensure!(limit.is_none(), SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support the LIMIT clause");
8213    polars_ensure!(order_by.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support the ORDER BY clause");
8214    let (FromTable::WithFromKeyword(from) | FromTable::WithoutKeyword(from)) = from;
8215    let [from] = from.as_slice() else {
8216        polars_bail!(SQLInterface: "cannot have multiple tables in DELETE FROM (found {})", from.len())
8217    };
8218    polars_ensure!(from.joins.is_empty(), SQLInterface: "DELETE does not support table JOINs");
8219    check_dml_target(&from.relation, "DELETE")?;
8220    Ok((from, selection.as_ref()))
8221}
